Kikuyu: Bũrũri-inĩ wa Uzu nĩ kwarĩ mũndũ watũire kuo wetagwo Ayubu.* Mũndũ ũcio ndaarĩ ũcuuke ningĩ aarĩ mũndũ mũrũngĩrĩru; nĩetigĩrĩte Ngai na agatheemaga maũndũ marĩa mooru.
English: There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job. That man was blameless and upright, and one who feared God,† and turned away from evil.

Kikuyu: Ayubu aarĩ na ariũ mũgwanja na airĩtu atatũ,
English: There were born to him seven sons and three daughters.

Kikuyu: ningĩ nĩ aarĩ na ngʼondu 7,000, na ngamĩĩra 3,000, na ndegwa cia kũigana kuohwo macooki 500, na ndigiri 500, na nĩ aarĩ na ndungata nyingĩ mũno. Nĩwe warĩ mũndũ ũrĩa mũnene mũno kũrĩ andũ arĩa angĩ othe a mwena wa Irathĩro.
English: His possessions also were seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred yoke of oxen, five hundred female donkeys, and a very great household; so that this man was the greatest of all the children of the east.

Kikuyu: Ariũ ake nĩmagĩaga na iruga o mũndũ riita rĩake gwake mũciĩ, na nĩmetaga aarĩ a nyina acio atatũ nĩguo marĩĩanĩre na manyuuanĩre nao.
English: His sons went and held a feast in the house of each one on his birthday; and they sent and called for their three sisters to eat and to drink with them.

Kikuyu: Na matukũ ma maruga maathira, Ayubu nĩamatũmanagĩra moke nĩguo amatherie. Nĩokagĩra rũciinĩ tene akaruta igongona rĩa njino nĩ ũndũ wa o ũmwe wao, tondũ eeciiragia atĩrĩ, “No gũkorwo ciana ciakwa nĩciĩhĩtie ikaruma Ngai na ngoro.” Ũcio nĩguo warĩ mũtũgo wa Ayubu wa mahinda mothe.
English: It was so, when the days of their feasting had run their course, that Job sent and sanctified them, and rose up early in the morning, and offered burnt offerings according to the number of them all. For Job said, “It may be that my sons have sinned, and renounced God in their hearts.” Job did so continually.

Kikuyu: Na rĩrĩ, mũthenya ũmwe araika nĩmathiire kũrũgama mbere ya Jehova, na Shaitani o nake agĩthiĩ hamwe nao.
English: Now on the day when God’s sons came to present themselves before Yahweh,‡ Satan also came among them.

Kikuyu: Nake Jehova akĩũria Shaitani atĩrĩ, “Uuma kũ?” Nake Shaitani agĩcookeria Jehova atĩrĩ, “Nyuma kũriũnga thĩ, o na gũcangacanga kuo kũndũ na kũndũ.”
English: Yahweh said to Satan, “Where have you come from?” Then Satan answered Yahweh, and said, “From going back and forth in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.”

Kikuyu: Ningĩ Jehova akĩũria Shaitani atĩrĩ, “Nĩũcũũranĩtie ũhoro wa ndungata yakwa Ayubu? Ũkoona atĩ kũu thĩ gũtirĩ mũndũ ũngĩ ũhaana take; ndarĩ ũcuuke na nĩmũrũngĩrĩru, mũndũ mwĩtigĩri-Ngai na ũtheemaga maũndũ marĩa mooru?”
English: Yahweh said to Satan, “Have you considered my servant, Job? For there is no one like him in the earth, a blameless and an upright man, one who fears God, and turns away from evil.”

Kikuyu: Shaitani agĩcookia atĩrĩ, “Kaĩ Ayubu agĩĩtigagĩra Ngai o ro ũguo tũhũ?
English: Then Satan answered Yahweh, and said, “Does Job fear God for nothing?

Kikuyu: Githĩ wee ndũmũirigĩire na ũkamũrigiicĩria hamwe na nyũmba yake, o hamwe na maũndũ make mothe? Nĩũrathimĩte wĩra wa moko make, nĩ ũndũ ũcio ũhiũ wake na ndũũru ciake ciyũrĩte bũrũri wothe.
English: Haven’t you made a hedge around him, and around his house, and around all that he has, on every side? You have blessed the work of his hands, and his substance is increased in the land.

Kikuyu: No rĩrĩ, ta tambũrũkia guoko gwaku ũhutie indo ciothe iria arĩ nacio, na ti-itherũ ndarĩ hĩndĩ ategũkũruma o ũthiũ-inĩ waku.”
English: But stretch out your hand now, and touch all that he has, and he will renounce you to your face.”

Kikuyu: Jehova akĩĩra Shaitani atĩrĩ, “No wega, indo ciothe iria arĩ nacio nĩndaciiga moko-inĩ maku, nowe mwene ndũkanamũhutie.” Nake Shaitani akiuma hau mbere ya Jehova.
English: Yahweh said to Satan, “Behold,§ all that he has is in your power. Only on himself don’t stretch out your hand.” So Satan went out from the presence of Yahweh.

Kikuyu: Na rĩrĩ, mũthenya ũmwe hĩndĩ ĩrĩa ariũ na aarĩ a Ayubu maarĩĩaga na makanyua ndibei kwa mũrũ wa nyina wao ũrĩa mũkũrũ-rĩ,
English: It fell on a day when his sons and his daughters were eating and drinking wine in their oldest brother’s house,

Kikuyu: mũkinyia-ũhoro agĩkora Ayubu, akĩmwĩra atĩrĩ, “Ndegwa nĩkũrĩma ikũrĩmaga na mĩraũ, nacio ndigiri ikũrĩĩaga o hau hakuhĩ,
English: that a messenger came to Job, and said, “The oxen were plowing, and the donkeys feeding beside them,

Kikuyu: nao andũ a Sabea† macitharĩkĩra na macitaha. Ndungata nacio maciũraga na rũhiũ rwa njora, na no niĩ nyiki ndahonoka, ndagĩũka gũkũrehere ũhoro!”
English: and the Sabeans attacked, and took them away. Yes, they have killed the servants with the edge of the sword, and I alone have escaped to tell you.”

Kikuyu: O akĩaragia-rĩ, mũkinyia-ũhoro ũngĩ agĩũka, akiuga atĩrĩ, “Mwaki wa Ngai uumire na igũrũ na wacina ngʼondu o na ndungata waniina biũ; no niĩ nyiki ndahonoka, ndagĩũka gũkũrehere ũhoro!”
English: While he was still speaking, another also came and said, “The fire of God has fallen from the sky, and has burned up the sheep and the servants, and consumed them, and I alone have escaped to tell you.”

Kikuyu: O akĩaragia-rĩ, mũkinyia-ũhoro ũngĩ agĩũka, akiuga atĩrĩ, “Akalidei‡ meyũmba mbũtũ ithatũ, maatharĩkĩra ngamĩĩra ciaku na macitaha, maathiĩ nacio. Ndungata nacio maciũraga na rũhiũ rwa njora; na no niĩ nyiki ndahonoka, ndagĩũka gũkũrehere ũhoro!”
English: While he was still speaking, another also came and said, “The Chaldeans made three bands, and swept down on the camels, and have taken them away, yes, and killed the servants with the edge of the sword; and I alone have escaped to tell you.”

Kikuyu: O akĩaragia-rĩ, mũkinyia-ũhoro o ũngĩ agĩũka, akiuga atĩrĩ, “Ariũ na aarĩ aku mekũrĩĩaga, makĩnyuuaga ndibei kwa mũrũ wa nyina wao ũrĩa mũkũrũ;
English: While he was still speaking, there came also another, and said, “Your sons and your daughters were eating and drinking wine in their oldest brother’s house,

Kikuyu: na rĩrĩ, o hĩndĩ ĩyo rũhuho rũnene rwahurutana ruumĩte werũ-inĩ, na ruo rwahũũra nyũmba ĩyo koine ciayo inya, yamomoka, yamag- wĩra maakua; na no niĩ nyiki ndahonoka, ndagĩũka gũkũrehere ũhoro!”
English: and behold, there came a great wind from the wilderness, and struck the four corners of the house, and it fell on the young men, and they are dead. I alone have escaped to tell you.”

Kikuyu: Nake Ayubu aigua-ũhoro ũcio, akĩrũgama, agĩtembũranga nguo yake ya igũrũ, na akĩenjwo mũtwe. Agĩcooka akĩĩgũithia thĩ, akĩhooya Ngai,
English: Then Job arose, and tore his robe, and shaved his head, and fell down on the ground, and worshiped.

Kikuyu: akiuga atĩrĩ: “Ndoimire nda ya maitũ ndĩ njaga, na ngoima thĩ ĩno ndĩ njaga. Nĩ Jehova waheanire, na nĩ Jehova wacookera: rĩĩtwa rĩa Jehova rĩrogoocwo.”
English: He said, “Naked I came out of my mother’s womb, and naked will I return there. Yahweh gave, and Yahweh has taken away. Blessed be Yahweh’s name.”

Kikuyu: Thĩinĩ wa maũndũ macio mothe-rĩ, Ayubu ndaigana kwĩhia na ũndũ wa gũtuĩra Ngai mahĩtia.
English: In all this, Job didn’t sin, nor charge God with wrongdoing.

Kikuyu: Ningĩ nĩ kwarĩ mũthenya ũngĩ araika maathiire kũrũgama mbere ya Jehova, na Shaitani o nake agĩthiĩ hamwe nao kũrũgama mbere yake.
English: Again, on the day when God’s sons came to present themselves before Yahweh, Satan came also among them to present himself before Yahweh.

Kikuyu: Nake Jehova akĩũria Shaitani atĩrĩ, “Uuma kũ?” Nake Shaitani agĩcookeria Jehova atĩrĩ, “Nyuma kũriũnga thĩ o na gũcangacanga kuo kũndũ na kũndũ.”
English: Yahweh said to Satan, “Where have you come from?” Satan answered Yahweh, and said, “From going back and forth in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.”

Kikuyu: Ningĩ Jehova akĩũria Shaitani atĩrĩ, “Nĩũcũũranĩtie ũhoro wa ndungata yakwa Ayubu? Ũkoona atĩ kũu thĩ gũtirĩ mũndũ ũhaana take; ndarĩ ũcuuke na nĩ mũrũngĩrĩru, mũndũ mwĩtigĩri-Ngai na ũtheemaga maũndũ marĩa mooru. Ningĩ no arũmĩtie wĩhokeku wake, o na gũtuĩka nĩwaningĩrĩirie ndĩmwanange hatarĩ gĩtũmi.”
English: Yahweh said to Satan, “Have you considered my servant Job? For there is no one like him in the earth, a blameless and an upright man, one who fears God, and turns away from evil. He still maintains his integrity, although you incited me against him, to ruin him without cause.”

Kikuyu: Nake Shaitani agĩcookeria Jehova, akiuga atĩrĩ, “Gĩkonde kĩrĩhagwo na gĩkonde! Mũndũ no arute indo ciake ciothe nĩguo ahonokie muoyo wake.
English: Satan answered Yahweh, and said, “Skin for skin. Yes, all that a man has he will give for his life.

Kikuyu: No rĩrĩ, ta tambũrũkia guoko gwaku ũhutie mahĩndĩ na nyama cia mwĩrĩ wake, na ti-itherũ ndarĩ hĩndĩ ategũkũruma o ũthiũ-inĩ waku.”
English: But stretch out your hand now, and touch his bone and his flesh, and he will renounce you to your face.”

Kikuyu: Nake Jehova akĩĩra Shaitani atĩrĩ, “No wega, rĩu arĩ moko-inĩ maku; no ndũkahutie muoyo wake.”
English: Yahweh said to Satan, “Behold, he is in your hand. Only spare his life.”

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ ũcio Shaitani akiuma hau mbere ya Jehova, akĩnyamaria Ayubu na ironda ciarĩ na ruo mũno kuuma makinya ma magũrũ make nginya mũtwe.
English: So Satan went out from the presence of Yahweh, and struck Job with painful sores from the sole of his foot to his head.

Kikuyu: Nake Ayubu akĩoya gacere ka nyũngũ ethũage nako, agĩikara thĩ harĩa haitagwo mũhu.
English: He took for himself a potsherd to scrape himself with, and he sat among the ashes.

Kikuyu: Nake mũtumia wake akĩmũũria atĩrĩ, “Anga no ũrũmĩtie wĩhokeku waku o na rĩu? Ruma Ngai wĩkuĩre!”
English: Then his wife said to him, “Do you still maintain your integrity? Renounce God, and die.”

Kikuyu: Nake Ayubu akĩmũcookeria atĩrĩ, “Wee ũraaria ta mũndũ-wa-nja mũkĩĩgu. Kaĩ turĩkĩamũkagĩra o maũndũ mega kuuma kũrĩ Ngai, na tũtiamũkĩre mathĩĩna?” Thĩinĩ wa maũndũ macio mothe-rĩ, Ayubu ndaigana kwĩhia thĩinĩ wa mĩario yake.
English: But he said to her, “You speak as one of the foolish women would speak. What? Shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil?” In all this Job didn’t sin with his lips.

Kikuyu: Na rĩrĩ, hĩndĩ ĩrĩa arata atatũ a Ayubu, nĩo Elifazu ũrĩa Mũtemaani,* na Bilidadi ũrĩa Mũshuhi, na Zofaru ũrĩa Mũnaamathi, maaiguire mathĩĩna marĩa mothe maakorete Ayubu-rĩ, makĩgĩa gĩathĩ, makiuma o mũndũ gwake na magĩcemania nĩguo mathiĩ makamũcakaithie o makĩmũhooreragia.
English: Now when Job’s three friends heard of all this evil that had come on him, they each came from his own place: Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite; and they made an appointment together to come to sympathize with him and to comfort him.

Kikuyu: Rĩrĩa maamuonire marĩ o haraaya-rĩ, makĩrigwo nĩwe nĩ ũrĩa aahaanaga; makĩambĩrĩria kũrĩra maanĩrĩire, na magĩtembũranga nguo ciao, o na makĩĩhurĩria rũkũngũ mĩtwe.
English: When they lifted up their eyes from a distance, and didn’t recognize him, they raised their voices, and wept; and they each tore his robe, and sprinkled dust on their heads toward the sky.

Kikuyu: Ningĩ magĩcooka magĩikara thĩ hamwe nake matukũ mũgwanja, mũthenya na ũtukũ, na gũtirĩ mũndũ wamwaragĩria kiugo o na kĩmwe, nĩgũkorwo nĩmoonire atĩ kũnyamarĩka gwake kwarĩ kũnene mũno.
English: So they sat down with him on the ground seven days and seven nights, and no one spoke a word to him, for they saw that his grief was very great.

Kikuyu: Thuutha wa matukũ macio, Ayubu agĩtumũra kanua, akĩruma mũthenya ũrĩa aaciarirwo.
English: After this Job opened his mouth, and cursed the day of his birth.

Kikuyu: Akiuga atĩrĩ:
English: Job answered:

Kikuyu: “Mũthenya ũrĩa niĩ ndaciarirwo ũroora, o na ũtukũ ũcio kwerirwo atĩrĩ, ‘Mũtumia nĩaciara mwana wa kahĩĩ!’
English: “Let the day perish in which I was born, the night which said, ‘There is a boy conceived.’

Kikuyu: Mũthenya ũcio-rĩ, ũrotuĩka o nduma; Ngai arĩ igũrũ aroaga kũũrũmbũiya; mũthenya ũcio ũroaga gũthererwo nĩ ũtheri.
English: Let that day be darkness. Don’t let God from above seek for it, neither let the light shine on it.

Kikuyu: Mũthenya ũcio ũrokĩĩnyiitĩrwo nĩ nduma nene na kĩĩruru gĩa gĩkuũ; ũrohumbĩrwo nĩ itu; nduma ĩrotooria ũtheri waguo.
English: Let darkness and the shadow of death claim it for their own. Let a cloud dwell on it. Let all that makes the day black terrify it.

Kikuyu: Ũtukũ ũcio-rĩ, ũronyiitwo nĩ nduma ndumanu; ũroaga gũtaranĩrio na mĩthenya ĩrĩa ĩngĩ ya mwaka, o na kana ũtarwo harĩ mweri o na ũrĩkũ.
English: As for that night, let thick darkness seize on it. Let it not rejoice among the days of the year. Let it not come into the number of the months.

Kikuyu: Ũtukũ ũcio ũrothaata; o na gũtikanoigwo ngemi ũtukũ ũcio.
English: Behold, let that night be barren. Let no joyful voice come therein.

Kikuyu: Arĩa marumaga mĩthenya maroruma mũthenya ũcio, o acio moĩ kwarahũra nyamũ ĩrĩa ĩĩtagwo Leviathani.
English: Let them curse it who curse the day, who are ready to rouse up leviathan.

Kikuyu: Njata ciaguo cia rũciinĩ irotuĩka nduma; ũroeterera ũtheri na wage kũwona, o na ũroaga kuona ruoro rũgĩtema,
English: Let the stars of its twilight be dark. Let it look for light, but have none, neither let it see the eyelids of the morning,

Kikuyu: nĩ ũndũ ndũigana kũhinga mĩrango ya nda ya maitũ, na ndũigana kũgirĩrĩria maitho makwa kuona thĩĩna.
English: because it didn’t shut up the doors of my mother’s womb, nor did it hide trouble from my eyes.

Kikuyu: “Ndaagire gũkua ngĩciarwo nĩkĩ? Ndaagire gũkua ngiuma nda nĩkĩ?
English: “Why didn’t I die from the womb? Why didn’t I give up the spirit when my mother bore me?

Kikuyu: Ndaamũkĩrirwo maru-inĩ nĩkĩ? Ndaamũkĩrirwo nyondo-inĩ atĩ nĩguo nyongithio nĩkĩ?
English: Why did the knees receive me? Or why the breast, that I should nurse?

Kikuyu: Nĩgũkorwo rĩu ingĩkomete ndĩ na thayũ; rĩu ingĩrĩ toro hurũkĩte
English: For now I should have lain down and been quiet. I should have slept, then I would have been at rest,

Kikuyu: hamwe na athamaki na aheani kĩrĩra a gũkũ thĩ arĩa meeyakĩire kũndũ kũrĩa kwanangĩku rĩngĩ,
English: with kings and counselors of the earth, who built up waste places for themselves;

Kikuyu: o hamwe na aathani arĩa maarĩ na thahabu, o arĩa maiyũrĩtie nyũmba ciao betha.
English: or with princes who had gold, who filled their houses with silver;

Kikuyu: Ningĩ-rĩ, nĩ kĩĩ kĩagiririe thikwo tĩĩri-inĩ ta kĩhuno o na kana ta gakenge karĩa gatoonire ũtheri wa riũa?
English: or as a hidden untimely birth I had not been, as infants who never saw light.

Kikuyu: Kũu andũ arĩa aaganu nĩmatigĩte kũnyamarĩka, na kũu arĩa anogu nĩmahurũkĩte.
English: There the wicked cease from troubling. There the weary are at rest.

Kikuyu: Kũu-rĩ, mĩgwate o nayo nĩĩkenagĩra kwaraha kwayo; nĩĩtigĩte kũigua kĩgũthũko kĩa nyabaara ya ngombo.
English: There the prisoners are at ease together. They don’t hear the voice of the taskmaster.

Kikuyu: Andũ arĩa anini na arĩa anene othe marĩ kuo, nayo ngombo nĩĩrekereirio kuuma kũrĩ mũmĩathi.
English: The small and the great are there. The servant is free from his master.

Kikuyu: “Nĩ kĩĩ gĩtũmaga andũ arĩa marĩ na mĩnyamaro maheo ũtheri, naguo muoyo ũkaheo arĩa marĩ na ruo rwa ngoro,
English: “Why is light given to him who is in misery, life to the bitter in soul,

Kikuyu: o acio meriragĩria gĩkuũ na gĩtingĩũka, o arĩa magĩcaragia gũkĩra kĩndũ kĩa goro kĩrĩa kĩhithe,
English: who long for death, but it doesn’t come; and dig for it more than for hidden treasures,

Kikuyu: acio maiyũragwo nĩ gĩkeno magakena maakinya mbĩrĩra?
English: who rejoice exceedingly, and are glad, when they can find the grave?

Kikuyu: Nĩ kĩĩ gĩtũmaga muoyo ũheo mũndũ ũũrĩte njĩra, o ũcio mũhingĩrĩrie nĩ Ngai?
English: Why is light given to a man whose way is hidden, whom God has hedged in?

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ handũ ha ndĩe irio, no kuumwo nyumagwo nĩ ngoro; nakuo gũcaaya gwakwa gũitĩkaga ta maaĩ.
English: For my sighing comes before I eat. My groanings are poured out like water.

Kikuyu: Ũndũ ũrĩa ndeetigagĩra nĩũngorete; ũndũ ũrĩa wamakagia mũno nĩguo ũnginyĩrĩire.
English: For the thing which I fear comes on me, that which I am afraid of comes to me.

Kikuyu: Ndionaga thayũ, o na kana ngahoorera; ndionaga ũhurũko, no mĩnyamaro.”
English: I am not at ease, neither am I quiet, neither do I have rest; but trouble comes.”

Kikuyu: Nake Elifazu ũrĩa Mũtemaani agĩcookia, akĩmũũria atĩrĩ:
English: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered,

Kikuyu: “Mũndũ angĩgeria gũkũgwetera koigo kamwe-rĩ, hihi wamũkirĩrĩria? No rĩrĩ, nũũ ũngĩhota kwĩgirĩrĩria kwaria?
English: “If someone ventures to talk with you, will you be grieved? But who can withhold himself from speaking?

Kikuyu: Ririkana ũrĩa wanataara andũ aingĩ, na ũrĩa wanekĩra moko marĩa maregeru hinya.
English: Behold, you have instructed many, you have strengthened the weak hands.

Kikuyu: Ciugo ciaku cianatiirĩrĩra arĩa manahĩngwo makenda kũgũa; nĩwe wanekĩra maru marĩa magondoku hinya.
English: Your words have supported him who was falling, you have made the feeble knees firm.

Kikuyu: No rĩu-rĩ, nĩũkoretwo nĩ thĩĩna, nawe ũkoorwo nĩ hinya; ũhũũrĩtwo, nawe ũkanyiitwo nĩ kĩmako.
English: But now it has come to you, and you faint. It touches you, and you are troubled.

Kikuyu: Githĩ wĩtigĩri Ngai waku tiguo wagĩrĩirwo gũtuĩka ũũmĩrĩru waku, nayo mĩthiĩre yaku ĩtarĩ ũcuuke-rĩ, githĩ tiyo mwĩhoko waku?
English: Isn’t your piety your confidence? Isn’t the integrity of your ways your hope?

Kikuyu: “Ta wĩcũũranie atĩrĩ: Nĩ mũndũ ũrĩkũ wanathĩĩnĩka atekĩte ũũru? Nĩ kũ andũ arĩa arũngĩrĩru marĩ maniinwo?
English: “Remember, now, who ever perished, being innocent? Or where were the upright cut off?

Kikuyu: Niĩ ũrĩa nyonete-rĩ, nĩ atĩ andũ arĩa marĩmaga ũũru, na arĩa mahaandaga thĩĩna-rĩ, maũndũ macio no mo magethaga.
English: According to what I have seen, those who plow iniquity and sow trouble, reap the same.

Kikuyu: Manangagwo nĩ mĩhũmũ ya Ngai; makaniinwo nĩ kĩhuhũkanio kĩa marakara make.
English: By the breath of God they perish. By the blast of his anger are they consumed.

Kikuyu: Mĩrũũthi no ĩrume na ĩrarame, no magego ma mĩrũũthi ĩyo mĩnene nĩmakoinangwo.
English: The roaring of the lion, and the voice of the fierce lion, the teeth of the young lions, are broken.

Kikuyu: Mũrũũthi nĩũkuaga nĩ kwaga gĩa kũguĩma, nacio ciana cia mũrũũthi wa mũgoma ikahurunjũka.
English: The old lion perishes for lack of prey. The cubs of the lioness are scattered abroad.

Kikuyu: “Nĩ kũrĩ kohoro karanginyĩire na hitho, namo matũ makwa marakaigua gakĩhehanwo.
English: “Now a thing was secretly brought to me. My ear received a whisper of it.

Kikuyu: Ũtukũ ngĩĩcũũrania ũhoro wa cioneki cia kũmakania, ũtukũ rĩrĩa andũ makoragwo marĩ toro mũnene,
English: In thoughts from the visions of the night, when deep sleep falls on men,

Kikuyu: ngĩnyiitwo nĩ guoya na kũinaina, namo mahĩndĩ makwa mothe magĩthingitha.
English: fear came on me, and trembling, which made all my bones shake.

Kikuyu: O hĩndĩ ĩyo roho ũraahĩtũkĩra o ũthiũ-inĩ wakwa, nacio njuĩrĩ cia mwĩrĩ wakwa irambarara.
English: Then a spirit passed before my face. The hair of my flesh stood up.

Kikuyu: Roho ũcio ũrarũgama, no ndinahota kũmenya ũrĩa ũratariĩ. Mbere yakwa hararũgama mũhianĩre wa kĩndũ, ndĩracooka ndĩraigua gũkĩario na mĩheehũ gũkĩũrio atĩrĩ,
English: It stood still, but I couldn’t discern its appearance. A form was before my eyes. Silence, then I heard a voice, saying,

Kikuyu: ‘Mũndũ wa gũkua-rĩ, aahota gũtuĩka mũthingu gũkĩra Ngai? Mũndũ aahota gũtuĩka mũtheru gũkĩra Mũmũũmbi?
English: ‘Shall mortal man be more just than God? Shall a man be more pure than his Maker?

Kikuyu: Angĩkorwo Ngai ndangĩhota kwĩhoka ndungata ciake-rĩ, na angĩkorwo nĩonaga araika ake marĩ na mahĩtia-rĩ,
English: Behold, he puts no trust in his servants. He charges his angels with error.

Kikuyu: githĩ to oone mahĩtia maingĩ mũno ma andũ arĩa matũũraga nyũmba cia ndoro, acio mĩthingi yao ĩrĩ rũkũngũ-inĩ, acio mamemendagwo na ihenya gũkĩra kĩĩhuruta!
English: How much more those who dwell in houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust, who are crushed before the moth!

Kikuyu: Kuuma rũciinĩ nginya hwaĩ-inĩ moinangagwo tũcunjĩ; magathira tene na tene matekũrũmbũiyo.
English: Between morning and evening they are destroyed. They perish forever without any regarding it.

Kikuyu: Githĩ mĩkanda ya hema yao ndĩmunyũrĩtwo, nĩguo makue matarĩ na ũũgĩ?’
English: Isn’t their tent cord plucked up within them? They die, and that without wisdom.’

Kikuyu: “Wenda gwĩtana, ĩtana, no rĩrĩ, nũũ ũngĩgwĩtĩka? Nĩ ũrĩkũ wa arĩa atheru ũngĩũrĩra kũrĩ we?
English: “Call now; is there any who will answer you? To which of the holy ones will you turn?

Kikuyu: Rũngʼathio rũũragaga kĩrimũ, naguo ũiru ũkooraga mũndũ ũrĩa mũkĩĩgu.
English: For resentment kills the foolish man, and jealousy kills the simple.

Kikuyu: Niĩ mwene nĩnyonete kĩrimũ gĩkĩgĩa na mĩri, no-o rĩmwe nyũmba yakĩo ĩkĩrumwo.
English: I have seen the foolish taking root, but suddenly I cursed his habitation.

Kikuyu: Ciana ciake nĩiraihanĩrĩirie na ũgitĩri, ihatĩrĩirio igooti-inĩ itarĩ na mũndũ wa gũciciirĩrĩra.
English: His children are far from safety. They are crushed in the gate. Neither is there any to deliver them,

Kikuyu: Ũrĩa mũhũtu arĩĩaga magetha make, amoyaga o na marĩ mĩigua-inĩ, nao arĩa anyootu makahũmagĩra ũtonga wao.
English: whose harvest the hungry eat up, and take it even out of the thorns. The snare gapes for their substance.

Kikuyu: Nĩgũkorwo hatĩka ndĩkunũkaga kuuma thĩ, kana thĩĩna ũkamera tĩĩri-inĩ.
English: For affliction doesn’t come out of the dust, neither does trouble spring out of the ground;

Kikuyu: No rĩrĩ, mũndũ aciaragwo arĩ wa kuonaga thĩĩna, o ta ũrĩa na ma thandĩ cia mwaki irathũkaga na igũrũ.
English: but man is born to trouble, as the sparks fly upward.

Kikuyu: “No rĩrĩ, korwo nĩ niĩ ingĩthaitha Mũrungu; ingĩneana ciira wakwa kũrĩ we.
English: “But as for me, I would seek God. I would commit my cause to God,

Kikuyu: We ekaga maũndũ ma magegania marĩa mataangĩmenyeka, na akaringa ciama itangĩtarĩka.
English: who does great things that can’t be fathomed, marvelous things without number;

Kikuyu: Nĩwe uuragĩria thĩ mbura; na nĩwe ũrehagĩra bũrũri maaĩ.
English: who gives rain on the earth, and sends waters on the fields;

Kikuyu: Arĩa menyiihagia nĩwe ũmatũũgagĩria, nao arĩa marĩ na kĩeha moyagwo na igũrũ makagitĩrwo.
English: so that he sets up on high those who are low, those who mourn are exalted to safety.

Kikuyu: Nĩwe ũthaatagia mĩbango ya arĩa marĩ waara, nĩgeetha moko mao matikagĩe na ũhootani.
English: He frustrates the plans of the crafty, so that their hands can’t perform their enterprise.

Kikuyu: Nĩanyiitaga arĩa oogĩ waara-inĩ wao, namo mathugunda ma arĩa oingumania akaameheria biũ.
English: He takes the wise in their own craftiness; the counsel of the cunning is carried headlong.

Kikuyu: Nduma ĩmakoraga kũrĩ o mũthenya; mũthenya barigici makahambataga taarĩ ũtukũ.
English: They meet with darkness in the day time, and grope at noonday as in the night.

Kikuyu: Nĩahonokagia arĩa abatari kuuma kũrĩ rũhiũ rwa njora rũrĩa rũrĩ tũnua-inĩ twao; amahonokagia moko-inĩ ma arĩa marĩ hinya.
English: But he saves from the sword of their mouth, even the needy from the hand of the mighty.

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ ũcio athĩĩni makagĩa na kĩĩrĩgĩrĩro, naguo ciira ũtarĩ wa kĩhooto ũgatumia kanua.
English: So the poor has hope, and injustice shuts her mouth.

Kikuyu: “Kũrathimwo nĩ mũndũ ũrĩa ũrũngagwo nĩ Ngai; nĩ ũndũ ũcio ndũkamene irũithia rĩa Mwene-Hinya-Wothe.
English: “Behold, happy is the man whom God corrects. Therefore do not despise the chastening of the Almighty.

Kikuyu: Nĩgũkorwo nĩaguraranagia, no rĩrĩ, acookaga akooha nguraro ĩyo wega; nĩatiihanagia, no moko make no mo mahonanagia.
English: For he wounds and binds up. He injures and his hands make whole.

Kikuyu: Nĩagagũteithũra harĩ mĩtino ĩtandatũ; o na ĩrĩ mũgwanja-rĩ, gũtirĩ ũũru ũgaagũkora.
English: He will deliver you in six troubles; yes, in seven no evil will touch you.

Kikuyu: Hĩndĩ ya ngʼaragu nĩagagũkũũra kuuma kũrĩ gĩkuũ, ningĩ hĩndĩ ya mbaara agũkũũre ndũkooragwo na rũhiũ rwa njora.
English: In famine he will redeem you from death; in war, from the power of the sword.

Kikuyu: Nĩũkagitĩrwo harĩ rũcamiũ rwa rũrĩmĩ, na ndũgetigĩra hĩndĩ ĩrĩa mwanangĩko ũgooka.
English: You will be hidden from the scourge of the tongue, neither will you be afraid of destruction when it comes.

Kikuyu: Nĩũgathekerera mwanangĩko na ngʼaragu, na ndũgetigĩra nyamũ cia gũkũ thĩ.
English: You will laugh at destruction and famine, neither will you be afraid of the animals of the earth.

Kikuyu: Nĩgũkorwo nĩũkagĩa na kĩrĩkanĩro na mahiga ma werũ-inĩ, nacio nyamũ cia gĩthaka itũũre irĩ na thayũ nawe.
English: For you will be allied with the stones of the field. The animals of the field will be at peace with you.

Kikuyu: Nawe ũikarage ũũĩ atĩ hema yaku nĩ ngitĩre; nawe nĩũkooya ithabu rĩa indo ciaku ũkore hatirĩ kĩndũ kĩũrĩte.
English: You will know that your tent is in peace. You will visit your fold, and will miss nothing.

Kikuyu: Nĩũkamenya atĩ ciana ciaku nĩikaingĩha, nacio njiaro ciaku cingĩhe o ta nyeki ya gũkũ thĩ.
English: You will know also that your offspring† will be great, your offspring as the grass of the earth.

Kikuyu: Ũgaathiĩ mbĩrĩra-inĩ ũrĩ o na hinya, ũhaana ta itĩĩa cia ngano ĩgethetwo hĩndĩ ya magetha.
English: You will come to your grave in a full age, like a shock of grain comes in its season.

Kikuyu: “Nĩtũtuĩrĩtie ũhoro ũyũ, na nĩ wa ma. Nĩ ũndũ ũcio kĩũigue na ũũmenye wee mwene.”
English: Behold, we have researched it. It is so. Hear it, and know it for your good.”

Kikuyu: Ningĩ Ayubu agĩcookia atĩrĩ:
English: Then Job answered,

Kikuyu: “Naarĩ korwo ruo rũrũ ndĩ naruo rwathimwo, nayo mĩnyamaro ĩno ndĩ nayo yothe ĩigĩrĩrwo ratiri igũrũ!
English: “Oh that my anguish were weighed, and all my calamity laid in the balances!

Kikuyu: Ti-itherũ yakorwo ĩrĩ mĩritũ gũkĩra mũthanga ũrĩa ũrĩ maria-inĩ marĩa manene; na nĩkĩo ndĩrahiũhire kwaria.
English: For now it would be heavier than the sand of the seas, therefore my words have been rash.

Kikuyu: Mĩguĩ ya Mwene-Hinya-Wothe nĩĩndoonyete, naguo roho wakwa nĩũranyua ũrũrũ wayo; maũndũ ma kũmakania mũno ma Ngai nĩmerekeirio harĩ niĩ.
English: For the arrows of the Almighty are within me. My spirit drinks up their poison. The terrors of God set themselves in array against me.

Kikuyu: Njagĩ ya werũ-inĩ-rĩ, nĩyaanagia rĩrĩa ĩrĩ na nyeki ya kũrĩa, kana ndegwa ĩkaania rĩrĩa ĩtuĩrĩirwo?
English: Does the wild donkey bray when he has grass? Or does the ox low over his fodder?

Kikuyu: Irio itarĩ mũcamo nĩ irĩĩkaga itekĩrĩtwo cumbĩ? Mũruru wa itumbĩ ũrĩa mwerũ-rĩ, nĩ urĩ mũrĩo?
English: Can that which has no flavor be eaten without salt? Or is there any taste in the white of an egg?

Kikuyu: Niĩ ndingĩcihutia; irio ta icio no itũme njire ngoro.
English: My soul refuses to touch them. They are as loathsome food to me.

Kikuyu: “Naarĩ korwo ndaheo ũndũ ũrĩa ndĩrahooya, korwo Ngai aahe ũndũ ũrĩa ndĩrerirĩria,
English: “Oh that I might have my request, that God would grant the thing that I long for,

Kikuyu: naguo nĩ atĩ Ngai eetĩkĩre kũũmemenda, arekererie guoko gwake kũũniine!
English: even that it would please God to crush me; that he would let loose his hand, and cut me off!

Kikuyu: Hĩndĩ ĩyo no ngĩe na ũndũ wa kũũhooreria, ũndũ wa gĩkeno ruo-inĩ rũrũ rũtarathira, atĩ niĩ ndikaanĩte ciugo cia Ũrĩa Mũtheru.
English: Let it still be my consolation, yes, let me exult in pain that doesn’t spare, that I have not denied the words of the Holy One.

Kikuyu: “Ndĩ na hinya ũrĩkũ atĩ nĩguo njikare ndĩ na mwĩhoko? Ndĩ na kĩĩrĩgĩrĩro kĩrĩkũ atĩ nĩguo ngirĩrĩrie?
English: What is my strength, that I should wait? What is my end, that I should be patient?

Kikuyu: Niĩ ndĩ hinya ta ihiga? Mwĩrĩ wakwa nĩ wa gĩcango?
English: Is my strength the strength of stones? Or is my flesh of bronze?

Kikuyu: Niĩ ndĩ na hinya wa gwĩteithia, kuona atĩ rĩu nĩndunyĩtwo ũhootani?
English: Isn’t it that I have no help in me, that wisdom is driven away from me?

Kikuyu: “Mũndũ ũtarĩ na kĩĩrĩgĩrĩro aagĩrĩire gũteithio nĩ arata ake, o na angĩkorwo nĩatiganĩirie ũhoro wa gwĩtigĩra Ũrĩa Mwene-Hinya-Wothe.
English: “To him who is ready to faint, kindness should be shown from his friend; even to him who forsakes the fear of the Almighty.

Kikuyu: No ariũ a baba maagĩte kwĩhokeka o ta tũrũũĩ tũrĩa tũhũaga, ningĩ o ta tũrũũĩ tũrĩa tũiyũraga tũkoina,
English: My brothers have dealt deceitfully as a brook, as the channel of brooks that pass away;

Kikuyu: rĩrĩa tũirĩtio nĩ mbarabu ĩgĩtweka, na tũkaiyũrwo nĩ tharunji ĩrĩa ĩratweka,
English: which are black by reason of the ice, in which the snow hides itself.

Kikuyu: no rĩrĩ, tũtithereraga rĩrĩa kwara, na hĩndĩ ya ũrugarĩ tũkahũa mĩtaro-inĩ yatuo.
English: In the dry season, they vanish. When it is hot, they are consumed out of their place.

Kikuyu: Ikundi cia agendi nĩithaamaga njĩra ciacio, ikambata werũ-inĩ, igathirĩra kuo.
English: The caravans that travel beside them turn away. They go up into the waste, and perish.

Kikuyu: Ikundi cia agendi cia Tema icaragia maaĩ, agendi a wonjoria a Sheba makamacaria marĩ na mwĩhoko.
English: The caravans of Tema looked. The companies of Sheba waited for them.

Kikuyu: Magathĩĩnĩka, tondũ makoretwo marĩ na kĩĩrĩgĩrĩro; no maakinya ho magakora hatirĩ kĩndũ.
English: They were distressed because they were confident. They came there, and were confounded.

Kikuyu: O na inyuĩ-rĩ, mũtuĩkĩte andũ matangĩheana ũteithio; muonaga ũndũ wa kũmakania mũgetigĩra.
English: For now you are nothing. You see a terror, and are afraid.

Kikuyu: Niĩ-rĩ, nĩ ndĩ ndoiga atĩrĩ: ‘Heanai kĩndũ nĩ ũndũ wakwa, ngũũrai na indo cianyu,
English: Did I ever say, ‘Give to me’? or, ‘Offer a present for me from your substance’?

Kikuyu: honokiai guoko-inĩ gwa thũ, ngũũrai kuuma moko-inĩ ma arĩa matarĩ tha’?
English: or, ‘Deliver me from the adversary’s hand’? or, ‘Redeem me from the hand of the oppressors’?

Kikuyu: “Atĩrĩrĩ, ndutaai ũhoro na nĩngũkira; nyonereriai harĩa hĩtĩtie.
English: “Teach me, and I will hold my peace. Cause me to understand my error.

Kikuyu: Kaĩ ciugo cia ma irĩ ruo-ĩ! No rĩrĩ, ngarari cianyu nĩ kĩhooto kĩrĩkũ irarehe?
English: How forcible are words of uprightness! But your reproof, what does it reprove?

Kikuyu: Anga mũrenda kũruta mahĩtia ũrĩa njugĩte, mũgatua ciugo cia mũndũ ũũmĩirwo tha taarĩ rũhuho?
English: Do you intend to reprove words, since the speeches of one who is desperate are as wind?

Kikuyu: Inyuĩ o na no mũcuukĩre mwana wa ngoriai mĩtĩ, na mwendie mũrata wanyu.
English: Yes, you would even cast lots for the fatherless, and make merchandise of your friend.

Kikuyu: “No rĩu-rĩ, ndamũthaitha mwĩtĩkĩre kũndora. Anga no ngĩheenanie o maitho-inĩ manyu?
English: Now therefore be pleased to look at me, for surely I will not lie to your face.

Kikuyu: Mwĩcũraniei nĩguo mũtikogomie kĩhooto; njookererai, nĩgũkorwo wĩhokeku wakwa nĩguo ũraarũithio.
English: Please return. Let there be no injustice. Yes, return again. My cause is righteous.

Kikuyu: Nĩ kũrĩ wĩhia ũrĩ mĩromo-inĩ yakwa? Anga kanua gakwa gatingĩhota gũkũũrana maũndũ ma rũmena?
English: Is there injustice on my tongue? Can’t my taste discern mischievous things?

Kikuyu: “Githĩ mũndũ ndakoragwo na ũtungata mũritũ gũkũ thĩ? Githĩ matukũ make matihaana o ta ma mũndũ mwandĩke wĩra?
English: “Isn’t a man forced to labor on earth? Aren’t his days like the days of a hired hand?

Kikuyu: O ta ngombo ĩkwĩrirĩria ciĩruru cia hwaĩ-inĩ, o na kana ta mũndũ mwandĩke ũgũthethũkĩra mũcaara wake-rĩ,
English: As a servant who earnestly desires the shadow, as a hireling who looks for his wages,

Kikuyu: ũguo nĩguo niĩ ngaĩirwo mĩeri ya tũhũ, na ngatuĩrwo atĩ ũtukũ ndaarage ndĩ na kĩeha.
English: so I am made to possess months of misery, wearisome nights are appointed to me.

Kikuyu: Rĩrĩa ndakoma ndĩyũragia atĩrĩ, ‘Ndĩrĩũkĩra rĩ?’ Ũtukũ ũkaraiha, na ngaraara ngĩĩgarũra nginya gũgakĩa.
English: When I lie down, I say, ‘When will I arise, and the night be gone?’ I toss and turn until the dawning of the day.

Kikuyu: Mwĩrĩ wakwa ũiyũrĩtwo nĩ igunyũ na ngũcĩ, nakĩo gĩkonde gĩakwa gĩatũkangĩte na gĩgatogota.
English: My flesh is clothed with worms and clods of dust. My skin closes up, and breaks out afresh.

Kikuyu: “Matukũ makwa maraathira na ihenya rĩkĩrĩte rĩa kanyamũ karĩa gakonjithanagia uuthi ngoora ĩgĩtumwo, magagĩkinya mũthia itarĩ na kĩĩrĩgĩrĩro.
English: My days are swifter than a weaver’s shuttle, and are spent without hope.

Kikuyu: Wee Ngai-rĩ, ririkana atĩ muoyo wakwa no ta mĩhũmũ; namo maitho makwa matigacooka kuona ũndũ mwega rĩngĩ.
English: Oh remember that my life is a breath. My eye will no more see good.

Kikuyu: Riitho rĩrĩa rĩranyona rĩtigacooka kũnyona rĩngĩ; mũkaanjaria, no ndigakorwo ho.
English: The eye of him who sees me will see me no more. Your eyes will be on me, but I will not be.

Kikuyu: O ta ũrĩa itu rĩthiiaga rĩkabuĩria, ũguo noguo ũrĩa ũthiiaga mbĩrĩra-inĩ atacookaga kuoneka.
English: As the cloud is consumed and vanishes away, so he who goes down to Sheol† will come up no more.

Kikuyu: Ndagacooka kũinũka gwake mũciĩ; harĩa aaikaraga ndagacooka kuonwo ho.
English: He will return no more to his house, neither will his place know him any more.

Kikuyu: “Nĩ ũndũ ũcio-rĩ, ndigũkira; ngwaria nĩ ũndũ wa ũrĩa roho wakwa ũrĩ na ruo, ndĩtetere nĩ ũndũ wa ũrĩa ngoro yakwa ĩrĩ na marũrũ.
English: “Therefore I will not keep silent. I will speak in the anguish of my spirit. I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.

Kikuyu: Niĩ-rĩ, ndĩ iria rĩa maaĩ, kana nyamũ ĩrĩa nene ĩtũũraga iria thĩinĩ kũrĩa kũriku, atĩ nĩkĩo nangagĩrwo?
English: Am I a sea, or a sea monster, that you put a guard over me?

Kikuyu: Rĩrĩa ngwĩciiria ũrĩrĩ wakwa nĩguo ũkũũhooreria, na atĩ gĩtanda gĩakwa no kĩĩniinĩre gũteta-rĩ,
English: When I say, ‘My bed will comfort me. My couch will ease my complaint,’

Kikuyu: o na hĩndĩ ĩyo ũũmakagia na irooto, o na ũkanjiguithia guoya na cioneki,
English: then you scare me with dreams and terrify me through visions,

Kikuyu: nĩ ũndũ ũcio ngathuura kaba gũitwo, na gĩkuũ, handũ ha gũikara na mwĩrĩ ũyũ wakwa.
English: so that my soul chooses strangling, death rather than my bones.

Kikuyu: Nĩthũire muoyo wakwa; ndikwenda gũtũũra nginya tene. Tigana na niĩ tondũ matukũ makwa no ma tũhũ.
English: I loathe my life. I don’t want to live forever. Leave me alone, for my days are but a breath.

Kikuyu: “Mũndũ-rĩ, akĩrĩ kĩ, tondũ ũmwĩkĩrĩire ũguo, na ũkamũrũmbũyia mũno ũguo,
English: What is man, that you should magnify him, that you should set your mind on him,

Kikuyu: atĩ ũmũthuthuuragia ngoro o rũciinĩ, na ũkamũgeragia mahinda mothe?
English: that you should visit him every morning, and test him every moment?

Kikuyu: Kaĩ gũtarĩ hĩndĩ ũgaatiga gũikara ũndorete, kana ũtigane na niĩ o na kahinda kanini?
English: How long will you not look away from me, nor leave me alone until I swallow down my spittle?

Kikuyu: Angĩkorwo nĩnjĩhĩtie-rĩ, nĩ atĩa niĩ ngwĩkĩte, Wee mũrori wa andũ? Nĩ kĩĩ gĩtũmĩte ũnjorote? Kaĩ nduĩkĩte mũrigo harĩwe?
English: If I have sinned, what do I do to you, you watcher of men? Why have you set me as a mark for you, so that I am a burden to myself?

Kikuyu: Nĩ kĩĩ kĩragiria ũnjohere mahĩtia makwa na ũndekere mehia makwa? Nĩgũkorwo ndĩ hakuhĩ gũkoma tĩĩri-inĩ; nawe nĩũkanjaria no ndigakorwo ho.”
English: Why do you not pardon my disobedience, and take away my iniquity? For now will I lie down in the dust. You will seek me diligently, but I will not be.”

Kikuyu: Nake Bilidadi ũrĩa Mũshuhi agĩcookia, akĩũria atĩrĩ:
English: Then Bildad the Shuhite answered,

Kikuyu: “Nĩ nginya rĩ ũgũikara ũkĩaragia maũndũ ta macio? Ciugo ciaku no ta inegene rĩa rũhuho rũkĩhurutana.
English: “How long will you speak these things? Shall the words of your mouth be a mighty wind?

Kikuyu: Mũrungu-rĩ, nĩogomagia ciira wa kĩhooto? Ũcio Mwene-Hinya-Wothe nĩogomagia ũndũ ũrĩa ũrĩ wa ma?
English: Does God pervert justice? Or does the Almighty pervert righteousness?

Kikuyu: Rĩrĩa ciana ciaku ciamwĩhĩirie-rĩ, nĩacirekereirie iherithio nĩ ũndũ wa mehia ma cio.
English: If your children have sinned against him, he has delivered them into the hand of their disobedience.

Kikuyu: No rĩrĩ, wee ũngĩcũthĩrĩria Mũrungu na wĩthaithanĩrĩre harĩ Ũcio Mwene-Hinya-Wothe,
English: If you want to seek God diligently, make your supplication to the Almighty.

Kikuyu: ũngĩkorwo ũrĩ mũtheru na mũrũngĩrĩru-rĩ, o na rĩu no arahũke nĩ ũndũ waku nĩguo agũcookie handũ harĩa hakwagĩrĩire.
English: If you were pure and upright, surely now he would awaken for you, and make the habitation of your righteousness prosperous.

Kikuyu: O na gũtuĩka kĩambĩrĩria gĩaku no kĩoneke kĩrĩ kĩnini, thuutha-inĩ nĩũkagaacĩra mũno.
English: Though your beginning was small, yet your latter end would greatly increase.

Kikuyu: “Ũria ũhoro harĩ njiarwa cia tene, na ũtuĩrie maũndũ marĩa maithe mao meerutire,
English: “Please inquire of past generations. Find out about the learning of their fathers.

Kikuyu: nĩgũkorwo ithuĩ tũraciarirwo o ro ira na tũtirĩ ũndũ tũũĩ, namo matukũ maitũ ma gũikara gũkũ thĩ no ta kĩĩruru.
English: (For we are but of yesterday, and know nothing, because our days on earth are a shadow.)

Kikuyu: Acio githĩ to makũrute na makũhe ũhoro? Acio githĩ to maarie ũhoro marĩ na ũmenyo?
English: Shall they not teach you, tell you, and utter words out of their heart?

Kikuyu: Irura-rĩ, no rĩkũre handũ hatarĩ itomboya? Ithanjĩ-rĩ, no rĩtheereme handũ hatarĩ maaĩ?
English: “Can the papyrus grow up without mire? Can the rushes grow without water?

Kikuyu: Rĩngĩkũrĩra handũ hatarĩ maaĩ rĩũmaga narua gũkĩra nyeki, o na rĩtakinyĩte rĩa gũtuuo.
English: While it is yet in its greenness, not cut down, it withers before any other reed.

Kikuyu: Ũcio nĩguo mũthia wa arĩa othe mariganagĩrwo nĩ Mũrungu; ũguo no ta guo mwĩhoko wa arĩa matooĩ Ngai ũthiraga.
English: So are the paths of all who forget God. The hope of the godless man will perish,

Kikuyu: Kĩrĩa ehokete no kĩndũ kĩhũthũ; kĩrĩa egiritanagia nakĩo no ta rũrenda rwa mbũmbũĩ.
English: whose confidence will break apart, whose trust is a spider’s web.

Kikuyu: Etiiranagia na rũrenda rwake, naruo rũgatuĩka; akenyiitĩrĩra harĩ ruo, no rũtingĩmũtiirĩrĩra.
English: He will lean on his house, but it will not stand. He will cling to it, but it will not endure.

Kikuyu: Ahaana ta mũtĩ ũitĩrĩirio maaĩ wega ũrĩ riũa-inĩ, ũtambũrũkĩtie thuuna ciaguo mũgũnda-inĩ;
English: He is green before the sun. His shoots go out along his garden.

Kikuyu: mĩri yaguo ĩĩthiororokeirie kĩhumbu kĩa mahiga, na ĩcaragia ha kwĩgwatĩrĩra rwaro-inĩ rwa mahiga.
English: His roots are wrapped around the rock pile. He sees the place of stones.

Kikuyu: No rĩrĩa wakũũrwo harĩa ũraarĩ-rĩ, handũ hau hagakaana mũtĩ ũcio, hakoiga atĩrĩ, ‘Niĩ ndirĩ ndakuona.’
English: If he is destroyed from his place, then it will deny him, saying, ‘I have not seen you.’

Kikuyu: Ti-itherũ muoyo waguo ũmaga ũgathira, naho hau tĩĩri-inĩ ũcio hagakũra mĩtĩ ĩngĩ.
English: Behold, this is the joy of his way. Out of the earth, others will spring.

Kikuyu: “Ti-itherũ Mũrungu ndangĩrega mũndũ ũtarĩ ũcuuke, kana ekĩre moko ma arĩa mekaga ũũru hinya.
English: “Behold, God will not cast away a blameless man, neither will he uphold the evildoers.

Kikuyu: Na rĩrĩ, no arĩiyũria kanua gaku mĩtheko, nayo mĩromo yaku yanĩrĩre nĩ gũkena.
English: He will still fill your mouth with laughter, your lips with shouting.

Kikuyu: Thũ ciaku nĩikahumbwo thoni, nacio hema cia arĩa aaganu itigacooka kuonwo.”
English: Those who hate you will be clothed with shame. The tent of the wicked will be no more.”

Kikuyu: Ningĩ Ayubu agĩcookia, akiuga atĩrĩ:
English: Then Job answered,

Kikuyu: “Ti-itherũ nĩnjũũĩ ũhoro ũcio nĩ wa ma. No rĩrĩ, mũndũ angĩhota atĩa gũkorwo arĩ mũthingu mbere ya Mũrungu?
English: “Truly I know that it is so, but how can man be just with God?

Kikuyu: O na korwo mũndũ enda gũkararania na Ngai-rĩ, ndangĩhota kũmũcookeria kĩũria o na kĩmwe harĩ ciũria ngiri.
English: If he is pleased to contend with him, he can’t answer him one time in a thousand.

Kikuyu: Ũũgĩ wake nĩ mũingĩ mũno, na ũhoti wake nĩ mũnene. Nũũ wanaregana nake akĩgaacĩra?
English: God is wise in heart, and mighty in strength. Who has hardened himself against him and prospered?

Kikuyu: Eeheragia irĩma itekũmenya, na agacingʼaũrania nĩ kũrakara.
English: He removes the mountains, and they don’t know it, when he overturns them in his anger.

Kikuyu: Athingithagia thĩ ĩkoima handũ hayo, na akainainia itugĩ ciayo.
English: He shakes the earth out of its place. Its pillars tremble.

Kikuyu: Aathaga riũa rĩkaaga kũratha; nake agiragĩrĩria ũtheri wa njata.
English: He commands the sun and it doesn’t rise, and seals up the stars.

Kikuyu: Nĩwe watambũrũkirie igũrũ arĩ o wiki, na athiiaga agĩkinyangaga makũmbĩ ma iria.
English: He alone stretches out the heavens, and treads on the waves of the sea.

Kikuyu: Nĩwe Mũũmbi wa njata iria ciĩtagwo Nduba, na Karaũ, na Kĩrĩmĩra, o na ikundi cia njata cia mwena wa gũthini.
English: He makes the Bear, Orion, and the Pleiades, and the rooms of the south.

Kikuyu: Nĩekaga magegania matangĩmenyeka, na akaringa ciama itangĩtarĩka.
English: He does great things past finding out; yes, marvelous things without number.

Kikuyu: Rĩrĩa aahĩtũkĩra harĩa ndĩ, ndingĩmuona; o na rĩrĩa aathiĩra harĩa ndĩ ndimenyaga.
English: Behold, he goes by me, and I don’t see him. He passes on also, but I don’t perceive him.

Kikuyu: Angĩgutha kĩndũ-rĩ, nũũ ũngĩhota kũmũgiria? Nũũ ũngĩmũũria atĩrĩ, ‘Nĩ atĩa ũreka?’
English: Behold, he snatches away. Who can hinder him? Who will ask him, ‘What are you doing?’

Kikuyu: Ngai ndahingagĩrĩria marakara make; o na arĩa maateithagĩrĩria Rahabu nĩmamũinamagĩrĩra.
English: “God will not withdraw his anger. The helpers of Rahab stoop under him.

Kikuyu: “Niĩ-rĩ, ndaakĩhota atĩa kũmũkararia? Ingĩruta kũ ciugo cia kũmũcookeria?
English: How much less will I answer him, and choose my words to argue with him?

Kikuyu: O na korwo ndihĩtĩtie-rĩ, ndingĩhota kũmũcookeria ũndũ; ũrĩa ingĩĩka no gũthaitha ingĩthaitha Mũnjiirithia anjiguĩre tha.
English: Though I were righteous, yet I wouldn’t answer him. I would make supplication to my judge.

Kikuyu: O na ingĩamwĩtire nake anjĩtĩke-rĩ, ndingĩĩtĩkia nĩangĩathikĩrĩirie.
English: If I had called, and he had answered me, yet I wouldn’t believe that he listened to my voice.

Kikuyu: We angĩamemendire na kĩhuhũkanio, na aingĩhie ironda ciakwa hatarĩ gĩtũmi.
English: For he breaks me with a storm, and multiplies my wounds without cause.

Kikuyu: Ndarekaga njookererwo nĩ mĩhũmũ, no nĩahatagĩrĩria na mathĩĩna.
English: He will not allow me to catch my breath, but fills me with bitterness.

Kikuyu: Korwo no ũhoro wa hinya-rĩ, we arĩ hinya mũno! Na korwo no ũhoro wa ciira wa kĩhooto-rĩ, nũũ ũngĩmwĩta?
English: If it is a matter of strength, behold, he is mighty! If of justice, ‘Who,’ says he, ‘will summon me?’

Kikuyu: O na korwo ndiahĩtĩtie-rĩ, kanua gakwa no kandue mũhĩtia; korwo ndiarĩ na ũcuuke-rĩ, nĩkangĩanduire mũhĩtia.
English: Though I am righteous, my own mouth will condemn me. Though I am blameless, it will prove me perverse.

Kikuyu: “O na gũtuĩka ndirĩ na ũcuuke-rĩ, ndikwĩrĩrĩra; muoyo wakwa nĩndĩwagĩire kĩene.
English: I am blameless. I don’t respect myself. I despise my life.

Kikuyu: Ũhoro no ũrĩa ũmwe; nĩkĩo ndĩroiga atĩrĩ, ‘Aniinaga arĩa matarĩ ũcuuke o na akaniina arĩa aaganu.’
English: “It is all the same. Therefore I say he destroys the blameless and the wicked.

Kikuyu: Hĩndĩ ĩrĩa ihũũra rĩarehe gĩkuũ kĩa narua, nĩathekagĩrĩra kũũrwo nĩ hinya kwa arĩa matarĩ na mahĩtia.
English: If the scourge kills suddenly, he will mock at the trial of the innocent.

Kikuyu: Hĩndĩ ĩrĩa bũrũri wagĩa moko-inĩ ma andũ aaganu, nĩahingaga aciirithania maitho. Akorwo ti we-rĩ, nũũ wĩkaga ũguo?
English: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked. He covers the faces of its judges. If not he, then who is it?

Kikuyu: “Matukũ makwa marahanyũka gũkĩra mũkinyia-ũhoro; mombũkaga matarĩ na gĩkeno o na kĩnini.
English: “Now my days are swifter than a runner. They flee away. They see no good.

Kikuyu: Mahĩtũkaga na ihenya mũno ta tũtarũ twa irura,* kana ta nderi igũcuuhũkĩra kĩndũ gĩa kũrĩa.
English: They have passed away as the swift ships, as the eagle that swoops on the prey.

Kikuyu: Ingiuga atĩrĩ, ‘Nĩngũriganĩrwo nĩ mateta makwa, nĩngũtiga gũtukia gĩthiithi, ngene,’
English: If I say, ‘I will forget my complaint, I will put off my sad face, and cheer up,’

Kikuyu: no ngeetigĩra mĩnyamaro yakwa yothe, nĩgũkorwo nĩnjũũĩ ndũkandua atĩ ndiĩhĩtie.
English: I am afraid of all my sorrows. I know that you will not hold me innocent.

Kikuyu: Kuona atĩ nĩndĩkĩtie gũtuuo mũhĩtia-rĩ, nĩ kĩĩ gĩgũtũma ndĩĩnogie tũhũ?
English: I will be condemned. Why then do I labor in vain?

Kikuyu: O na ingĩĩthamba na thabuni, na ndĩĩthambe moko na igata-rĩ,
English: If I wash myself with snow, and cleanse my hands with lye,

Kikuyu: no ũndikirie irima rĩa gĩcoro nĩgeetha o na nguo ciakwa iithũũre.
English: yet you will plunge me in the ditch. My own clothes will abhor me.

Kikuyu: “We ti mũndũ ta niĩ atĩ nĩguo ndĩmũcookerie, nĩguo tũngʼethanĩre igooti-inĩ.
English: For he is not a man, as I am, that I should answer him, that we should come together in judgment.

Kikuyu: Naarĩ korwo nĩ harĩ mũndũ ũngĩtũiguithania, atũigĩrĩre guoko gwake ithuĩ eerĩ,
English: There is no umpire between us, that might lay his hand on us both.

Kikuyu: mũndũ wa kũnjehereria rũthanju rwa Ngai, nĩgeetha ndigacooke kũmakio nĩ itebeebania rĩake.
English: Let him take his rod away from me. Let his terror not make me afraid;

Kikuyu: Hĩndĩ ĩyo nĩingĩacooka kwaragia itekũmwĩtigĩra, no ũrĩa ndariĩ rĩu-rĩ, ndingĩhota.
English: then I would speak, and not fear him, for I am not so in myself.

Kikuyu: “Nĩthũire gũtũũra muoyo ũyũ; nĩ ũndũ ũcio ndikũhingĩrĩria mateta makwa, o na nĩ ngwaria nĩ ũndũ wa ũrĩa ngoro yakwa ĩrĩ na marũrũ.
English: “My soul is weary of my life. I will give free course to my complaint. I will speak in the bitterness of my soul.

Kikuyu: Ngwĩra Ngai atĩrĩ: Tiga kũndua mwĩhia, no nyonia kĩrĩa ũrandũithĩria.
English: I will tell God, ‘Do not condemn me. Show me why you contend with me.

Kikuyu: Kaĩ ũkenagio nĩ kũũhinyĩrĩria, ũgathũũra wĩra wa moko maku, o rĩrĩa ũrakenera mathugunda ma andũ arĩa aaganu?
English: Is it good to you that you should oppress, that you should despise the work of your hands, and smile on the counsel of the wicked?

Kikuyu: Kaĩ maitho maku marĩ o ta maitho ma andũ? Kaĩ muonere waku ũhaana o ta wa mũndũ?
English: Do you have eyes of flesh? Or do you see as man sees?

Kikuyu: Kaĩ matukũ maku maigana ta ma andũ, kana mĩaka yaku ĩkaigana o ta ya mũndũ,
English: Are your days as the days of mortals, or your years as man’s years,

Kikuyu: nĩguo ũcarĩrĩrie mahĩtia makwa, o na ũtuĩragie mehia makwa,
English: that you inquire after my iniquity, and search after my sin?

Kikuyu: o na gũtuĩka wee nĩũũĩ atĩ ndiĩhĩtie, na ũkamenya atĩ gũtirĩ mũndũ ũngĩhota kũũhonokia moko-inĩ maku?
English: Although you know that I am not wicked, there is no one who can deliver out of your hand.

Kikuyu: “Moko maku nĩmo maathondekire na makĩnyũmba. Rĩu nĩũgũkĩgarũrũka ũnyanange?
English: “ ‘Your hands have framed me and fashioned me altogether, yet you destroy me.

Kikuyu: Ririkana atĩ wanyũũmbire ta rĩũmba. Rĩu ũgũcooka ũndue rũkũngũ rĩngĩ?
English: Remember, I beg you, that you have fashioned me as clay. Will you bring me into dust again?

Kikuyu: Githĩ ndwanjitire ta iria, na ũgĩcooka ũkĩĩmatia ta maguta marĩo,
English: Haven’t you poured me out like milk, and curdled me like cheese?

Kikuyu: ũkĩĩhumbĩra na nyama na gĩkonde, na ũkĩohania mahĩndĩ na mĩkiha yakwa hamwe.
English: You have clothed me with skin and flesh, and knit me together with bones and sinews.

Kikuyu: Nĩwaaheire muoyo o na ũkĩnyonia ũtugi waku; naguo ũmenyereri waku nĩguo ũtũirie roho wakwa.
English: You have granted me life and loving kindness. Your visitation has preserved my spirit.

Kikuyu: “No nĩwahithire maũndũ maya ngoro-inĩ yaku, na nĩnjũũĩ no warĩ na ũndũ ũyũ meciiria-inĩ maku:
English: Yet you hid these things in your heart. I know that this is with you:

Kikuyu: Ingĩehirie wee nĩwanyonaga, na ndũngĩagire kũũherithia nĩ ũndũ wa wĩhia wakwa.
English: if I sin, then you mark me. You will not acquit me from my iniquity.

Kikuyu: Kaĩ akorwo nĩnjĩhĩtie ndĩ na haaro-ĩ! O na ingĩiguĩka ndiĩkĩte ũũru, ndingĩhota gũtiira mũtwe wakwa, nĩgũkorwo njiyũrĩtwo nĩ thoni, na ngarikĩra mathĩĩna-inĩ makwa.
English: If I am wicked, woe to me. If I am righteous, I still will not lift up my head, being filled with disgrace, and conscious of my affliction.

Kikuyu: Ingĩtiira mũtwe wakwa-rĩ, wee ũnjeemaga o ta mũrũũthi, na ningĩ ũkonania ũhoti waku mũnene wa kũnjũkĩrĩra.
English: If my head is held high, you hunt me like a lion. Again you show yourself powerful to me.

Kikuyu: Nĩũndeheire aira angĩ manjũkĩrĩre, na nĩwongereire marakara maku igũrũ rĩakwa; mbũtũ ciaku ikanjũkĩrĩra o ta makũmbĩ ma maaĩ marũmanĩrĩire.
English: You renew your witnesses against me, and increase your indignation on me. Changes and warfare are with me.

Kikuyu: “Nĩ kĩĩ gĩatũmire ũndute nda ya maitũ? Naarĩ korwo ndakuire itoneetwo nĩ maitho ma mũndũ o na ũmwe.
English: “ ‘Why, then, have you brought me out of the womb? I wish I had given up the spirit, and no eye had seen me.

Kikuyu: Naarĩ korwo ndiaciarirwo, kana korwo ndaciarirwo njerekeirio mbĩrĩra!
English: I should have been as though I had not been. I should have been carried from the womb to the grave.

Kikuyu: Githĩ matukũ makwa o na marĩ manini matikirie gũthira? Tigana na niĩ nĩguo ngĩe na gĩkeno gwa kahinda kanini,
English: Aren’t my days few? Stop! Leave me alone, that I may find a little comfort,

Kikuyu: kamũira thiĩte kũrĩa mũndũ athiiaga na ndacooke, bũrũri wa nduma, o nduma nene ya gĩkuũ,
English: before I go where I will not return from, to the land of darkness and of the shadow of death;

Kikuyu: o bũrũri ũrĩa ũtukũ wakuo ũrĩ mũtumanu mũno, bũrũri wa nduma ya gĩkuũ, na ũtarĩ kĩhaarĩro, kũrĩa o na ũtheri ũhaana o ta nduma.”
English: the land dark as midnight, of the shadow of death, without any order, where the light is as midnight.’ ”

Kikuyu: Nake Zofaru ũrĩa Mũnaamathi agĩcookia, akĩũria atĩrĩ:
English: Then Zophar, the Naamathite, answered,

Kikuyu: “Ciugo icio ciothe-rĩ, nĩcikwaga gũcookio? Mwaria ũyũ-rĩ, nĩegũgĩtuuo mwagĩrĩru?
English: “Shouldn’t the multitude of words be answered? Should a man full of talk be justified?

Kikuyu: Mwĩraho ũcio waku-rĩ, nĩguo ũgũkiria andũ naguo? No kwage mũndũ ũngĩgũkaania rĩrĩa ũranyũrũrania?
English: Should your boastings make men hold their peace? When you mock, will no man make you ashamed?

Kikuyu: Wee ũreera Ngai atĩrĩ, ‘Wĩtĩkio wakwa ndũrĩ ũcuuke, o na niĩ ndĩ mũtheru maitho-inĩ maku.’
English: For you say, ‘My doctrine is pure. I am clean in your eyes.’

Kikuyu: Naarĩ korwo Ngai no aarie, atumũre mĩromo yake agũũkĩrĩre,
English: But oh that God would speak, and open his lips against you,

Kikuyu: na akũguũrĩrie hitho cia ũũgĩ, nĩ ũndũ ũũgĩ ũrĩa wa ma nĩ wa mĩena ĩĩrĩ. Menya ũndũ ũyũ; atĩ Ngai ndakũherithĩtie kũringana na ũrĩa mehia maku maigana.
English: that he would show you the secrets of wisdom! For true wisdom has two sides. Know therefore that God exacts of you less than your iniquity deserves.

Kikuyu: “Wee no ũhote kũmenya maũndũ marĩa mahithe ma Ngai? Kana no ũhote gũtuĩria kũna maũndũ ma Mwene-Hinya-Wothe?
English: “Can you fathom the mystery of God? Or can you probe the limits of the Almighty?

Kikuyu: Maũndũ make nĩmatũũgĩru gũkĩra igũrũ, wee nĩ atĩa ũngĩka? Nĩ mariku gũkĩra ũriku wa mbĩrĩra, wee nĩ atĩa ũngĩmenya?
English: They are high as heaven. What can you do? They are deeper than Sheol.† What can you know?

Kikuyu: Gĩthimo kĩamo nĩ kĩraihu gũkĩra thĩ na nĩ kĩaramu gũkĩra iria rĩrĩa inene.
English: Its measure is longer than the earth, and broader than the sea.

Kikuyu: “Angĩũka agũikie njeera-rĩ, acooke etane ciira-rĩ, nũũ ũngĩmũgiria?
English: If he passes by, or confines, or convenes a court, then who can oppose him?

Kikuyu: Ti-itherũ nĩoĩ andũ arĩa maheenanagia; na rĩrĩa oona ũndũ mũũru-rĩ, githĩ ndaũmenyaga?
English: For he knows false men. He sees iniquity also, even though he doesn’t consider it.

Kikuyu: No rĩrĩ, mũndũ ũtarĩ ũũgĩ ndangĩtuĩka mũũgĩ o na rĩ, o ta ũrĩa njaũ ya ndigiri ya gĩthaka ĩtarĩ hĩndĩ ĩngĩciarwo ĩrĩ mũndũ.
English: An empty-headed man becomes wise when a man is born as a wild donkey’s colt.

Kikuyu: “No rĩrĩ, ũngĩneana ngoro yaku kũrĩ Ngai, na ũtambũrũkie moko maku kũrĩ we,
English: “If you set your heart aright, stretch out your hands toward him.

Kikuyu: ũngĩeheria mehia marĩa marĩ guoko-inĩ gwaku, na ũgirie ũũru ũikare thĩinĩ wa hema yaku-rĩ,
English: If iniquity is in your hand, put it far away. Don’t let unrighteousness dwell in your tents.

Kikuyu: hĩndĩ ĩyo no ũhote gũtiira ũthiũ waku na igũrũ ũtegũconoka; no ũrũgame wega ũtarĩ na guoya.
English: Surely then you will lift up your face without spot. Yes, you will be steadfast, and will not fear,

Kikuyu: Ti-itherũ nĩũkariganĩrwo nĩ mathĩĩna maku, ũmaririkanage o ta maaĩ marĩkĩtie gũtherera.
English: for you will forget your misery. You will remember it like waters that have passed away.

Kikuyu: Mũtũũrĩre waku nĩũgacangarara gũkĩra mũthenya barigici, nayo nduma ĩgaatuĩka o ta rũciinĩ.
English: Life will be clearer than the noonday. Though there is darkness, it will be as the morning.

Kikuyu: Ũgũtũũra ũrĩ na mwĩhoko tondũ ũrĩ na ũgitĩri, ũkehũgũraga harĩa ũrĩ, na ũkahurũka ũtarĩ na ũgwati.
English: You will be secure, because there is hope. Yes, you will search, and will take your rest in safety.

Kikuyu: Nĩũgakomaga, gũtarĩ na mũndũ ũngĩtũma wĩtigĩre, nao andũ aingĩ nĩmakeyendithagia harĩ we.
English: Also you will lie down, and no one will make you afraid. Yes, many will court your favor.

Kikuyu: No rĩrĩ, maitho ma andũ arĩa aaganu nĩmakaaga kuona, na matikoona gwa kũũrĩra; naguo ũndũ ũrĩa meriragĩria ũgaatuĩka mũcaayo wa gĩkuũ.”
English: But the eyes of the wicked will fail. They will have no way to flee. Their hope will be the giving up of the spirit.”

Kikuyu: Ningĩ Ayubu agĩcookia atĩrĩ:
English: Then Job answered,

Kikuyu: “Hatirĩ nganja inyuĩ nĩ inyuĩ andũ, naguo ũũgĩ ũgaathiranĩra na inyuĩ rĩrĩa mũgaakua!
English: “No doubt, but you are the people, and wisdom will die with you.

Kikuyu: No rĩrĩ, ndĩ na ũmenyo o ta inyuĩ; mũtirĩ oogĩ kũngĩra. Nũũ ũtooĩ maũndũ macio mothe?
English: But I have understanding as well as you; I am not inferior to you. Yes, who doesn’t know such things as these?

Kikuyu: “Nduĩkĩte mũndũ wa gũthekererwo nĩ arata akwa, o na gũtuĩka nĩndakaĩire Ngai nake akĩnjigua: niĩ nduĩkĩte mũndũ wa gũthekererwo, o na gũtuĩka ndĩ mũthingu na ndirĩ ũcuuke!
English: I am like one who is a joke to his neighbor, I, who called on God, and he answered. The just, the blameless man is a joke.

Kikuyu: Andũ arĩa maikaraga megangarĩte manyũrũragia mũtino, makona ta ũndũ ũcio ũkoraga o andũ arĩa magũrũ mao matenderũkaga.
English: In the thought of him who is at ease there is contempt for misfortune. It is ready for them whose foot slips.

Kikuyu: Hema cia atunyani nĩcio ciikaraga igaacĩire, na andũ arĩa marakaragia Mũrungu nĩo maikaraga na thayũ, o acio makuuaga ngai yao na moko.
English: The tents of robbers prosper. Those who provoke God are secure, who carry their god in their hands.

Kikuyu: “No ta kĩũrie nyamũ, na nĩigũkũruta ũhoro, kana ũrie nyoni cia rĩera-inĩ, na nĩigũkwĩra;
English: “But ask the animals now, and they will teach you; the birds of the sky, and they will tell you.

Kikuyu: kana warĩrie thĩ, na nĩĩgũkũruta ũhoro, kana ũkĩarĩrie thamaki cia iria-inĩ, nacio nĩigũkũhe ũhoro.
English: Or speak to the earth, and it will teach you. The fish of the sea will declare to you.

Kikuyu: Nĩ irĩkũ cia icio ciothe itooĩ atĩ nĩ guoko kwa Jehova gwĩkĩte ũndũ ũyũ?
English: Who doesn’t know that in all these, Yahweh’s hand has done this,

Kikuyu: Mĩoyo ya ciũmbe ciothe ĩrĩ guoko-inĩ gwake, o na mĩhũmũ ya andũ othe.
English: in whose hand is the life of every living thing, and the breath of all mankind?

Kikuyu: Githĩ gũtũ gũtithuuranagia ciugo o ta ũrĩa rũrĩmĩ rũcamaga irio?
English: Doesn’t the ear try words, even as the palate tastes its food?

Kikuyu: Githĩ ũũgĩ ndũkoragwo na andũ arĩa akũrũ? Githĩ gũtũũra mũno gũtirehaga ũmenyo?
English: With aged men is wisdom, in length of days understanding.

Kikuyu: “Ũũgĩ na hinya nĩ cia Ngai; mataaro na ũmenyo nĩ ciake.
English: “With God is wisdom and might. He has counsel and understanding.

Kikuyu: Kĩrĩa amomoraga gĩtingĩakwo rĩngĩ; mũndũ ũrĩa aahingĩra njeera gũtirĩ mũndũ ũngĩmuohora.
English: Behold, he breaks down, and it can’t be built again. He imprisons a man, and there can be no release.

Kikuyu: Ahingagĩrĩria maaĩ, gũkaaga mbura; ningĩ aamarekereria makaananga bũrũri.
English: Behold, he withholds the waters, and they dry up. Again, he sends them out, and they overturn the earth.

Kikuyu: Hinya na ũtooria nĩ ciake; mũheenio na mũheenania eerĩ no ake.
English: With him is strength and wisdom. The deceived and the deceiver are his.

Kikuyu: Aheani kĩrĩra amatongoragia matarĩ nguo, na agatua aciirithania irimũ.
English: He leads counselors away stripped. He makes judges fools.

Kikuyu: Nĩohoraga mĩnyororo ĩrĩa athamaki moohaga andũ nayo, akamooha mũcibi njohero.*
English: He loosens the bond of kings. He binds their waist with a belt.

Kikuyu: Athĩnjĩri-Ngai amatongoragia marutĩtwo nguo, na akangʼaũrania andũ arĩa mehaandire tene.
English: He leads priests away stripped, and overthrows the mighty.

Kikuyu: Nĩakiragia mĩromo ya aheani kĩrĩra arĩa meehoketwo, nao athuuri akamatunya ũhoro wa gũkũũrana maũndũ.
English: He removes the speech of those who are trusted, and takes away the understanding of the elders.

Kikuyu: We nĩagagĩra arĩa atĩĩku bata, nao arĩa marĩ na hinya nĩamatunyaga indo ciao cia mbaara.
English: He pours contempt on princes, and loosens the belt of the strong.

Kikuyu: Nĩaguũragia maũndũ marĩa mariku ma nduma, na nduma nene ya gĩkuũ akamiumĩria ũtheri-inĩ.
English: He uncovers deep things out of darkness, and brings out to light the shadow of death.

Kikuyu: Anenehagia ndũrĩrĩ, agacooka agaciananga; aingĩhagia ndũrĩrĩ, agacooka agacihurunja.
English: He increases the nations, and he destroys them. He enlarges the nations, and he leads them captive.

Kikuyu: Nĩagaagagia meciiria ma atongoria a gũkũ thĩ; akamaingata, morũũrage werũ-inĩ mũtheri ũtarĩ njĩra.
English: He takes away understanding from the chiefs of the people of the earth, and causes them to wander in a wilderness where there is no way.

Kikuyu: Mahambaataga nduma-inĩ kũrĩa gũtarĩ ũtheri; ningĩ atũmaga matũgũũge ta mũndũ mũrĩĩu.
English: They grope in the dark without light. He makes them stagger like a drunken man.

Kikuyu: “Atĩrĩrĩ, maitho makwa nĩmonete maũndũ macio mothe, matũ makwa nĩmamaiguĩte na magataũkĩrwo nĩmo.
English: “Behold, my eye has seen all this. My ear has heard and understood it.

Kikuyu: Ũrĩa mũũĩ o na niĩ nĩnjũũĩ; mũtirĩ oogĩ kũngĩra.
English: What you know, I know also. I am not inferior to you.

Kikuyu: No niĩ ndĩrenda kwaria na Mwene-Hinya-Wothe, na ngerirĩria gũciira na Mũrungu.
English: “Surely I would speak to the Almighty. I desire to reason with God.

Kikuyu: No inyuĩ-rĩ, mũranjigĩrĩra ndeto cia maheeni; inyuothe mũrĩ athondekani a tũhũ!
English: But you are forgers of lies. You are all physicians of no value.

Kikuyu: Naarĩ korwo mwakira ki! Ũndũ ũcio ũngĩtuĩka ũũgĩ harĩ inyuĩ.
English: Oh that you would be completely silent! Then you would be wise.

Kikuyu: Na rĩrĩ, thikĩrĩriai kĩhooto gĩakwa; iguai gũthaithana kwa mĩromo yakwa.
English: Hear now my reasoning. Listen to the pleadings of my lips.

Kikuyu: Kaĩ mũngĩaria ũũru mũkĩarĩrĩria Mũrungu? Kaĩ mũngĩaria maheeni igũrũ rĩake?
English: Will you speak unrighteously for God, and talk deceitfully for him?

Kikuyu: Kaĩ mũngĩmuonia kĩmenyano? Kaĩ mũgũciirĩrĩra Mũrungu?
English: Will you show partiality to him? Will you contend for God?

Kikuyu: Angĩmũtuĩria inyuĩ-rĩ, ũndũ ũcio no ũtuĩke mwega? No mũmũheenie ta ũrĩa mũngĩheenia mũndũ?
English: Is it good that he should search you out? Or as one deceives a man, will you deceive him?

Kikuyu: Ti-itherũ no amũrũithie mũngĩtuĩka a kuonania kĩmenyano na hitho.
English: He will surely reprove you if you secretly show partiality.

Kikuyu: Hĩ, riiri wake ndũngĩmũmakia? Mũtingĩnyiitwo nĩ guoya nĩ ũndũ wake?
English: Won’t his majesty make you afraid and his dread fall on you?

Kikuyu: Mĩario yanyu ya ũũgĩ nĩ thimo hũthũ o ta mũhu; ihooto cianyu no ta kwĩgitĩra na rĩũmba.
English: Your memorable sayings are proverbs of ashes. Your defenses are defenses of clay.

Kikuyu: “Kirai ki, mũreke njarie; o ũrĩa ndĩrĩona-rĩ, rekei nyone.
English: “Be silent! Leave me alone, that I may speak. Let come on me what will.

Kikuyu: Nĩ kĩĩ gĩgũtũma ndĩtoonyie ũgwati-inĩ na ngaiga muoyo wakwa moko-inĩ makwa?
English: Why should I take my flesh in my teeth, and put my life in my hand?

Kikuyu: O na angĩnjũraga-rĩ, niĩ nowe ndĩrĩĩhokaga; na ti-itherũ nĩ ngatetera mĩthiĩre yakwa hau mbere yake.
English: Behold, he will kill me. I have no hope. Nevertheless, I will maintain my ways before him.

Kikuyu: Ti-itherũ, ũndũ ũyũ noguo ũgaatuĩka wa kũũhonokia, nĩgũkorwo mũndũ ũtooĩ Ngai ndangĩũmĩrĩria gũũka mbere yake!
English: This also will be my salvation, that a godless man will not come before him.

Kikuyu: Thikĩrĩriai wega ũhoro wakwa; matũ manyu nĩmakĩigue ũrĩa nguuga.
English: Listen carefully to my speech. Let my declaration be in your ears.

Kikuyu: Ti-itherũ nĩhaarĩirie ciira wakwa, na nĩnjũũĩ nĩ nguoneka ndĩ wa kĩhooto.
English: See now, I have set my cause in order. I know that I am righteous.

Kikuyu: Nĩ kũrĩ mũndũ ũngĩhota gũũthitanga? Angĩkorwo nĩ kũrĩ-rĩ, no gũkira ngũkira ngue.
English: Who is he who will contend with me? For then I would hold my peace and give up the spirit.

Kikuyu: “Wee Ngai, ta kĩĩhe o maũndũ maya meerĩ, na ndigũcooka gũkwĩhitha:
English: “Only don’t do two things to me, then I will not hide myself from your face:

Kikuyu: Atĩrĩ, eheria guoko gwaku, gũikare kũraya na niĩ, na ũtige kũũmakia na imakania ciaku.
English: withdraw your hand far from me, and don’t let your terror make me afraid.

Kikuyu: Ningĩ ũnjĩte na nĩngwĩtĩka, kana ũkĩreke njarie, nawe ũnjookerie.
English: Then call, and I will answer, or let me speak, and you answer me.

Kikuyu: Nĩ mahĩtia na mehia maigana niĩ njĩkĩte? Nyonia ihĩtia na rĩĩhia rĩakwa.
English: How many are my iniquities and sins? Make me know my disobedience and my sin.

Kikuyu: Ũraahitha ũthiũ waku nĩkĩ, na ũkandua thũ yaku?
English: Why do you hide your face, and consider me your enemy?

Kikuyu: Nĩũngĩnyamaria ithangũ rĩrahurutwo nĩ rũhuho? Nĩũgũtengʼerania na maragara momũ?
English: Will you harass a driven leaf? Will you pursue the dry stubble?

Kikuyu: Nĩgũkorwo nĩ wandĩkĩte maũndũ marũrũ ma kũnjũkĩrĩra, na ũkaangaĩra igai rĩa mehia ma ũnini wakwa.
English: For you write bitter things against me, and make me inherit the iniquities of my youth.

Kikuyu: Wohaga magũrũ makwa na mĩnyororo; ũrangagĩra njĩra ciakwa ciothe na ũndũ wa gũcora njoro makinya ma magũrũ makwa.
English: You also put my feet in the stocks, and mark all my paths. You set a bound to the soles of my feet,

Kikuyu: “Nĩ ũndũ ũcio mũndũ amocaga ta kĩndũ kĩbuthĩte, agathira ta nguo ĩrĩĩtwo nĩ memenyi.
English: though I am decaying like a rotten thing, like a garment that is moth-eaten.

Kikuyu: “Mũndũ ũciarĩtwo nĩ mũndũ-wa-nja-rĩ, aikaraga o matukũ manini, namo makaiyũrwo nĩ mathĩĩna.
English: “Man, who is born of a woman, is of few days, and full of trouble.

Kikuyu: Akũraga ta ihũa na agacooka akooma; ahĩtũkaga na ihenya ta kĩĩruru, na ndatũũraga.
English: He grows up like a flower, and is cut down. He also flees like a shadow, and doesn’t continue.

Kikuyu: Mũndũ ta ũcio wakĩmũkũũrĩra maitho? Mũndũ ta ũcio wamũrehe mbere yaku aciirithio?
English: Do you open your eyes on such a one, and bring me into judgment with you?

Kikuyu: Nũũ ũngĩhota kũruta kĩndũ gĩtheru kuuma harĩ kĩndũ kĩrĩa gĩtarĩ gĩtheru? Gũtirĩ o na ũmwe!
English: Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean? Not one.

Kikuyu: Matukũ ma mũndũ nĩ matare; nĩũtuĩte mũigana wa mĩeri yake, na nĩũmũigĩire mĩhaka ĩrĩa ataangĩkĩra.
English: Seeing his days are determined, the number of his months is with you, and you have appointed his bounds that he can’t pass.

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ ũcio tiga kũmũrora, tigana nake, nginya arĩĩkie mĩthenya yake ta mũthũkũmi.
English: Look away from him, that he may rest, until he accomplishes, as a hireling, his day.

Kikuyu: “Mũtĩ-rĩ, nĩwĩrĩgagĩrĩrwo atĩ ũngĩtemwo, no ũthethũke rĩngĩ, na atĩ mathethũka maguo matikaaga.
English: “For there is hope for a tree if it is cut down, that it will sprout again, that the tender branch of it will not cease.

Kikuyu: O na mĩri yaguo ĩngĩkũrĩra thĩ na gĩthukĩ kĩaguo kĩũmĩre tĩĩri-inĩ,
English: Though its root grows old in the earth, and its stock dies in the ground,

Kikuyu: ũngĩkaguucia maaĩ-rĩ, nĩũgathethũka na ũrute honge ta mũtĩ wa kũhaandwo.
English: yet through the scent of water it will bud, and sprout boughs like a plant.

Kikuyu: No mũndũ akuuaga agathikwo; aatuĩkana-rĩ, ndacookaga kuonwo rĩngĩ.
English: But man dies, and is laid low. Yes, man gives up the spirit, and where is he?

Kikuyu: O ta ũrĩa maaĩ mahũũaga kũu iria-inĩ, na ta ũrĩa mũtaro wa rũũĩ ũngʼaraga ũkooma-rĩ,
English: As the waters fail from the sea, and the river wastes and dries up,

Kikuyu: ũguo noguo mũndũ akomaga na ndacookaga gũũkĩra rĩngĩ; o nginya rĩrĩa igũrũ rĩgaathira-rĩ, andũ matirĩ hĩndĩ magookĩra kana maarahũrwo mookĩre.
English: so man lies down and doesn’t rise. Until the heavens are no more, they will not awake, nor be roused out of their sleep.

Kikuyu: “Naarĩ korwo wahitha thĩinĩ wa mbĩrĩra, na ũnjige hitho-inĩ nginya rĩrĩa marakara maku magaathira! Naarĩ korwo wanduĩra gĩathĩ, ũgaacooka kũndirikana hĩndĩ ĩyo.
English: “Oh that you would hide me in Sheol,† that you would keep me secret until your wrath is past, that you would appoint me a set time and remember me!

Kikuyu: Mũndũ akua-rĩ, nĩagatũũra muoyo rĩngĩ? Matukũ makwa mothe ma wĩra mũritũ-rĩ, ngweterera ihinda rĩakwa rĩa kwerũhĩrio hinya rĩkinye.
English: If a man dies, will he live again? I would wait all the days of my warfare, until my release should come.

Kikuyu: Wee ũgetana, na niĩ nĩngagwĩtĩka; na nĩũkeerirĩria kĩũmbe gĩkĩ wombire na moko maku.
English: You would call, and I would answer you. You would have a desire for the work of your hands.

Kikuyu: Hĩndĩ ĩyo nĩũgatara makinya makwa, no ndũkarũmbũiya mehia makwa.
English: But now you count my steps. Don’t you watch over my sin?

Kikuyu: Mahĩtia makwa meekĩrĩtwo mondo-inĩ, ĩkoohwo na ĩkahũũrwo mũhũũri; nĩũkahumbĩra mehia makwa.
English: My disobedience is sealed up in a bag. You fasten up my iniquity.

Kikuyu: “No rĩrĩ, o ta ũrĩa kĩrĩma kĩenjekaga na gĩkamomoka, na o ta ũrĩa rwaro rwa ihiga rũeheragio handũ ha ruo,
English: “But the mountain falling comes to nothing. The rock is removed out of its place.

Kikuyu: na o ta ũrĩa maaĩ mamuthũraga mahiga, na o ta ũrĩa mbura nene ĩtwaraga tĩĩri-rĩ, ũguo noguo wanangaga kĩĩrĩgĩrĩro kĩa mũndũ.
English: The waters wear the stones. The torrents of it wash away the dust of the earth. So you destroy the hope of man.

Kikuyu: Wee ũmũtooragia o rĩmwe rĩa kũigana, nake agathira; ũgarũraga gĩthiithi gĩake ũrĩa kĩhaana, na ũkamũingata.
English: You forever prevail against him, and he departs. You change his face, and send him away.

Kikuyu: Ariũ ake mangĩheo gĩtĩĩo, ndangĩmenya ũhoro ũcio; mangĩconorithio, we ndoonaga ũndũ ũcio.
English: His sons come to honor, and he doesn’t know it. They are brought low, but he doesn’t perceive it of them.

Kikuyu: We no ruo rwa mwĩrĩ wake aiguaga, nake atũũraga o ecaayagĩra.”
English: But his flesh on him has pain, and his soul within him mourns.”

Kikuyu: Nake Elifazu ũrĩa Mũtemaani akĩũria atĩrĩ:
English: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered,

Kikuyu: “Mũndũ mũũgĩ no acookie ũhoro na kwĩgereria, kana aiyũrie nda yake na rũhuho ruumĩte na irathĩro?
English: “Should a wise man answer with vain knowledge, and fill himself with the east wind?

Kikuyu: No eciirĩrĩre na ciugo cia tũhũ, kana na mĩario ĩtarĩ bata?
English: Should he reason with unprofitable talk, or with speeches with which he can do no good?

Kikuyu: No wee-rĩ, nĩũracambia ũhoro wa gwĩtigĩra Ngai, na ũkagirĩrĩria ũhoro wa andũ kwĩrutĩra Mũrungu.
English: Yes, you do away with fear, and hinder devotion before God.

Kikuyu: Mehia maku nĩmo mataaraga kanua gaku; nawe ũthuurĩte kwaria na rũrĩmĩ rwa mũndũ mwara.
English: For your iniquity teaches your mouth, and you choose the language of the crafty.

Kikuyu: Kanua gaku wee mwene nĩko karagũtuĩra ciira, ti gakwa: nayo mĩromo yaku wee mwene ĩkaaria ũira wa gũgũũkĩrĩra.
English: Your own mouth condemns you, and not I. Yes, your own lips testify against you.

Kikuyu: “Wee nĩwe mũndũ wa mbere gũciarwo? Wee-rĩ, waciarirwo mbere ya irĩma igĩe ho?
English: “Are you the first man who was born? Or were you brought out before the hills?

Kikuyu: Wee nĩũthikagĩrĩria ndundu ya Ngai? Wee wiki-rĩ, nowe ũrigĩtie na ũũgĩ?
English: Have you heard the secret counsel of God? Do you limit wisdom to yourself?

Kikuyu: Nĩ atĩa ũũĩ ithuĩ tũtooĩ? Nĩ ũmenyo ũrĩkũ ũrĩ naguo ithuĩ tũtarĩ?
English: What do you know that we don’t know? What do you understand which is not in us?

Kikuyu: Tũrĩ na athuuri marĩ na mbuĩ na arĩa akũrũ mũno, andũ akũrũ o na gũkĩra thoguo.
English: With us are both the gray-headed and the very aged men, much older than your father.

Kikuyu: Ndũiganĩtwo nĩ ũhoorerania wa Mũrungu, o na kana ũhoro ũcio warĩirio na ũhooreri?
English: Are the consolations of God too small for you, even the word that is gentle toward you?

Kikuyu: Ngoro yaku ĩgũteete nĩkĩ, na nĩ kĩĩ kĩratũma ũikare ũkiunaga maitho,
English: Why does your heart carry you away? Why do your eyes flash,

Kikuyu: nĩguo werekerie marakara maku kũrĩ Mũrungu, o na ũgaitũrũra ciugo ta icio kuuma kanua gaku?
English: that you turn your spirit against God, and let such words go out of your mouth?

Kikuyu: “Mũndũ akĩrĩ kĩ, atĩ no ahote gũtuĩka mũtheru, o na mũndũ ũciarĩtwo nĩ mũndũ-wa-nja nake akĩrĩ kĩĩ, atĩ no ahote gũtuĩka mũthingu?
English: What is man, that he should be clean? What is he who is born of a woman, that he should be righteous?

Kikuyu: Angĩkorwo Ngai ndangĩhota kwĩhoka andũ arĩa ake aamũre-rĩ, na kũngĩkorwo o na igũrũ ti gũtheru maitho-inĩ make-rĩ,
English: Behold, he puts no trust in his holy ones. Yes, the heavens are not clean in his sight;

Kikuyu: mũndũ akĩrĩ kĩ atĩ amwĩhoke? Mũndũ nĩ mwaganu na nĩ kĩmaramari, anyuuaga waganu ta maaĩ!
English: how much less one who is abominable and corrupt, a man who drinks iniquity like water!

Kikuyu: “Wee ta thikĩrĩria na nĩngũgũtaarĩria; reke ngwĩre ũrĩa nyonete,
English: “I will show you, listen to me; that which I have seen I will declare

Kikuyu: ngwĩre ũrĩa andũ arĩa oogĩ moigĩte, matekũhitha ũndũ o na ũmwe wa ũhoro ũrĩa maaheirwo nĩ maithe mao,
English: (which wise men have told by their fathers, and have not hidden it;

Kikuyu: (o acio oiki maaheetwo bũrũri hĩndĩ ĩrĩa gũtaarĩ mũndũ wa kũngĩ watuĩkanagia gatagatĩ-inĩ kao):
English: to whom alone the land was given, and no stranger passed among them):

Kikuyu: Atĩrĩ, mũndũ mwaganu akoragwo na mĩnyamaro matukũ make mothe. Matukũ mothe ma ũcio ũtarĩ tha-rĩ, maigĩirwo o mĩnyamaro.
English: the wicked man writhes in pain all his days, even the number of years that are laid up for the oppressor.

Kikuyu: Aiguaga o mĩgambo ya kũmakania mũno; hĩndĩ ĩrĩa maũndũ mothe moneka ta marĩ mega-rĩ, atunyani makamũtharĩkĩra.
English: A sound of terrors is in his ears. In prosperity the destroyer will come on him.

Kikuyu: Ndarĩ na kĩĩrĩgĩrĩro gĩa gwĩthara kuuma nduma-inĩ; etereirio kũũragwo na rũhiũ rwa njora.
English: He doesn’t believe that he will return out of darkness. He is waited for by the sword.

Kikuyu: Orũũraga agĩcaragia irio, oragie atĩrĩ, ‘Irĩ na kũ?’ Aikaraga amenyete atĩ mũthenya wa nduma ũrĩ o hakuhĩ.
English: He wanders abroad for bread, saying, ‘Where is it?’ He knows that the day of darkness is ready at his hand.

Kikuyu: Mĩnyamaro na ruo rwa ngoro nĩcio imũmakagia; imũtooragia taarĩ mũthamaki wĩhaarĩirie kũmũtharĩkĩra,
English: Distress and anguish make him afraid. They prevail against him, as a king ready to the battle.

Kikuyu: nĩ ũndũ ainainagĩria Mũrungu ngundi, na akangʼathĩria Mwene-Hinya-Wothe,
English: Because he has stretched out his hand against God, and behaves himself proudly against the Almighty,

Kikuyu: akamũguthũkĩra angʼathĩtie, arĩ na ngo yake mata ya hinya.
English: he runs at him with a stiff neck, with the thick shields of his bucklers,

Kikuyu: “O na gũtuĩka ũthiũ wake nĩ mũnoru, na njohero yake ĩkaneneha nĩ kũnora-rĩ,
English: because he has covered his face with his fatness, and gathered fat on his thighs.

Kikuyu: agaatũũraga matũũra maanangĩku, na aikarage nyũmba itatũũragwo nĩ mũndũ, nyũmba itigairie o kũmomoka ituĩke ihumbu cia mahiga.
English: He has lived in desolate cities, in houses which no one inhabited, which were ready to become heaps.

Kikuyu: Ndagacooka gũkorwo arĩ mũtongu, naguo ũtonga wake ndũgatũũra, o na kana indo ciake itheereme kũu bũrũri-inĩ.
English: He will not be rich, neither will his substance continue, neither will their possessions be extended on the earth.

Kikuyu: Ndakahota kũũrĩra nduma; rũrĩrĩmbĩ nĩrũkahoohia thuuna ciake, nayo mĩhũmũ ya kanua ka Ngai nĩĩkamweheria.
English: He will not depart out of darkness. The flame will dry up his branches. He will go away by the breath of God’s mouth.

Kikuyu: Nĩatige kwĩheenia na ũndũ wa kwĩhoka maũndũ ma tũhũ, nĩgũkorwo gũtirĩ kĩndũ makaamũrehere.
English: Let him not trust in emptiness, deceiving himself, for emptiness will be his reward.

Kikuyu: Ihinda rĩake rĩtanakinya-rĩ, nĩakarĩhio mũigana wake wothe, na honge ciake itikarura.
English: It will be accomplished before his time. His branch will not be green.

Kikuyu: Agaatuĩka ta mũthabibũ ũhũrũrĩtwo thabibũ ciaguo itarĩ njĩru, ahaane ta mũtamaiyũ ũraita kĩro kĩaguo.
English: He will shake off his unripe grape as the vine, and will cast off his flower as the olive tree.

Kikuyu: Nĩgũkorwo andũ a thiritũ ya arĩa matooĩ Ngai matũũraga marĩ thaata, na mwaki nĩũgaacina hema cia arĩa mendete mahaki.
English: For the company of the godless will be barren, and fire will consume the tents of bribery.

Kikuyu: Magĩaga nda cia mathĩĩna, na magaciara waganu; nda ciao ithugundaga o maheeni.”
English: They conceive mischief and produce iniquity. Their heart prepares deceit.”

Kikuyu: Ningĩ Ayubu agĩcookia atĩrĩ:
English: Then Job answered,

Kikuyu: “Nĩnjiguĩte maũndũ maingĩ ta macio; inyuothe mũrĩ ahoorerania a kũnyamarania!
English: “I have heard many such things. You are all miserable comforters!

Kikuyu: Mĩario ĩyo yanyu mĩingĩ ya mũhũhũtĩko-rĩ, ndĩrĩĩthira? Nĩ kĩĩ kĩramũthĩĩnia, gĩgatũma mũtinde mũgĩkararania?
English: Shall vain words have an end? Or what provokes you that you answer?

Kikuyu: O na niĩ no njarie ta inyuĩ, korwo nĩ inyuĩ mũrĩ harĩa ndĩ; niĩ no njarie mĩario mĩega ya kũmũciirithia na ndĩmũinainĩrie mũtwe.*
English: I also could speak as you do. If your soul were in my soul’s place, I could join words together against you, and shake my head at you,

Kikuyu: No rĩrĩ, kanua gakwa no kamũũmĩrĩrie; ũhoorerania uumĩte mĩromo-inĩ yakwa no ũmũhoorerie.
English: but I would strengthen you with my mouth. The solace of my lips would relieve you.

Kikuyu: “No o na ndaaria-rĩ, ruo rwakwa rũtirathira; o na ndegirĩrĩria kwaria-rĩ, rũtiranjeherera.
English: “Though I speak, my grief is not subsided. Though I forbear, what am I eased?

Kikuyu: Ti-itherũ, Wee Ngai nĩũũnogeetie; nĩũharaganĩtie nyũmba yakwa yothe.
English: But now, God, you have surely worn me out. You have made all my company desolate.

Kikuyu: Wee nĩũnjoheete, naguo ũndũ ũcio ũgatuĩka ũira; ũhĩnju ũyũ ndĩ naguo nĩwambararĩte ũkaanyumbũra ũrĩa ndariĩ.
English: You have shriveled me up. This is a witness against me. My leanness rises up against me. It testifies to my face.

Kikuyu: Ngai nĩandooretie na akandembũranga nĩ ũrĩa arakarĩte, akaahagaranĩria magego; ũcio thũ yakwa nĩangũũrĩire maitho.
English: He has torn me in his wrath and persecuted me. He has gnashed on me with his teeth. My adversary sharpens his eyes on me.

Kikuyu: Andũ nĩmathamĩtie tũnua twao maathekerere; mangũthaga rũthĩa makĩĩnyũrũragia, na makanyiitana hamwe manjũkĩrĩre.
English: They have gaped on me with their mouth. They have struck me on the cheek reproachfully. They gather themselves together against me.

Kikuyu: Mũrungu nĩandekereirie kũrĩ andũ arĩa ooru, na akanjikia mĩtego-inĩ ya arĩa aaganu.
English: God delivers me to the ungodly, and casts me into the hands of the wicked.

Kikuyu: Niĩ ndaikarĩte wega, nowe agĩĩthethera; aanyiitire mũmero, akĩĩhehenja. We anduĩte cabaa wake wa kũrathagwo;
English: I was at ease, and he broke me apart. Yes, he has taken me by the neck, and dashed me to pieces. He has also set me up for his target.

Kikuyu: aikia a mĩguĩ ake nĩmandigiicĩirie. Aratheeca higo ciakwa atarĩ na tha, na agaita maaĩ makwa ma nyongo thĩ.
English: His archers surround me. He splits my kidneys apart, and does not spare. He pours out my bile on the ground.

Kikuyu: Aatharĩkagĩra maita maingĩ maingĩ; anguthũkagĩra ta njamba ya ita.
English: He breaks me with breach on breach. He runs at me like a giant.

Kikuyu: “Ndumĩire gĩkonde gĩakwa kĩa mwĩrĩ nguo ya ikũnia, na ngahitha thiithi wakwa rũkũngũ-inĩ.
English: I have sewed sackcloth on my skin, and have thrust my horn in the dust.

Kikuyu: Ũthiũ wakwa nĩũtunĩhĩte nĩkũrĩra, nduma nene ĩgakĩhumbĩra maitho makwa;
English: My face is red with weeping. Deep darkness is on my eyelids,

Kikuyu: no rĩrĩ, moko makwa matirĩ ũndũ wa ũhinya mekĩte namo mahooya makwa nĩ matheru.
English: although there is no violence in my hands, and my prayer is pure.

Kikuyu: “Wee thĩ-rĩ, ndũkahumbĩre thakame yakwa; kĩrĩro gĩakwa kĩroaga gũkaahuurũkio!
English: “Earth, don’t cover my blood. Let my cry have no place to rest.

Kikuyu: O na rĩu-rĩ, mũira wakwa arĩ igũrũ; ũcio mũnjiirĩrĩri arĩ o igũrũ.
English: Even now, behold, my witness is in heaven. He who vouches for me is on high.

Kikuyu: Mũũthaithanĩrĩri nĩ mũrata wakwa rĩrĩa maitho makwa maraita maithori harĩ Ngai;
English: My friends scoff at me. My eyes pour out tears to God,

Kikuyu: nĩathaithanagĩrĩra mũndũ kũrĩ Ngai, o ta ũrĩa mũndũ athaithanagĩrĩra mũratawe.
English: that he would maintain the right of a man with God, of a son of man with his neighbor!

Kikuyu: “No mĩaka mĩnini ĩgũthira, thiĩ rũgendo rũrĩa mũndũ athiiaga na ndacooke.
English: For when a few years have come, I will go the way of no return.

Kikuyu: Roho wakwa nĩmũthuthĩku, matukũ makwa nĩmathirĩte, mbĩrĩra nĩyo ĩnjetereire.
English: “My spirit is consumed. My days are extinct and the grave is ready for me.

Kikuyu: Ti-itherũ thiũrũrũkĩirio nĩ andũ a kũũnyũrũria; maitho makwa no nginya meerorere rũmena rwao.
English: Surely there are mockers with me. My eye dwells on their provocation.

Kikuyu: “Wee Ngai-rĩ, ta kĩĩhe kĩndũ gĩa kũrũgamĩrĩra thiirĩ wakwa kĩrĩa ũretia, tondũ-rĩ, nũũ ũngĩ ũngĩĩtĩkĩra kũruta kĩndũ gĩake kĩĩndũgamĩrĩre?
English: “Now give a pledge. Be collateral for me with yourself. Who is there who will strike hands with me?

Kikuyu: Wee nĩwaagithĩtie meciiria mao ũmenyo; nĩ ũndũ ũcio ndũngĩmetĩkĩria mahootane.
English: For you have hidden their heart from understanding, therefore you will not exalt them.

Kikuyu: Mũndũ angĩkaana arata ake nĩ ũndũ wa kĩheo-rĩ, maitho ma ciana ciake nĩmakoora.
