English: He who denounces his friends for plunder, even the eyes of his children will fail.

Kikuyu: “Ngai nĩanduĩte mũndũ wa kuunwo thimo nĩ andũ othe, nduĩkĩte mũndũ wa gũtuagĩrwo mata ũthiũ nĩ andũ.
English: “But he has made me a byword of the people. They spit in my face.

Kikuyu: Maitho makwa nĩ maroora nĩ gwĩthikĩra; ciĩga ciakwa ciothe ihũthĩte o ta kĩĩruru.
English: My eye also is dim by reason of sorrow. All my members are as a shadow.

Kikuyu: Andũ arĩa arũngĩrĩru nĩmagegetio nĩ ũhoro ũcio; andũ arĩa matarĩ na ũũru mekĩte nĩmarahũkĩte mokĩrĩre andũ arĩa matooĩ Ngai.
English: Upright men will be astonished at this. The innocent will stir himself up against the godless.

Kikuyu: O na kũrĩ ũguo-rĩ, arĩa athingu nĩmarĩrũmagia njĩra ciao, nao arĩa marĩ moko matheru nĩmarĩongagĩrĩrwo hinya.
English: Yet the righteous will hold to his way. He who has clean hands will grow stronger and stronger.

Kikuyu: “No rĩrĩ, ta gĩũkei inyuothe, geriai o rĩngĩ! Niĩ ndirĩ ndĩrona mũndũ mũũgĩ gatagatĩ kanyu.
English: But as for you all, come back. I will not find a wise man among you.

Kikuyu: Matukũ makwa nĩ mathiru, mĩbango yakwa nĩmĩharaganie, o na merirĩria ma ngoro yakwa.
English: My days are past. My plans are broken off, as are the thoughts of my heart.

Kikuyu: Andũ aya magarũraga ũtukũ makaũtua mũthenya; nduma yamakinyĩrĩra moigaga atĩrĩ, ‘Ũtheri ũrĩ o hakuhĩ.’
English: They change the night into day, saying ‘The light is near’ in the presence of darkness.

Kikuyu: Angĩkorwo mũciĩ ũrĩa njĩrĩgĩrĩire no mbĩrĩra, angĩkorwo ingĩara ũrĩrĩ wakwa o nduma-inĩ-rĩ,
English: If I look for Sheol† as my house, if I have spread my couch in the darkness,

Kikuyu: angĩkorwo no njĩĩre ũhoro wa kũbutha atĩrĩ, ‘Wee nĩwe baba,’ na njĩĩre kĩgunyũ atĩrĩ, ‘Wee nĩwe maitũ’ kana ‘Nĩwe mwarĩ wa maitũ-rĩ’,
English: if I have said to corruption, ‘You are my father,’ and to the worm, ‘My mother,’ and ‘My sister,’

Kikuyu: mwĩhoko wakwa ũkĩrĩ kũ? Nũũ ũngĩnyonera mwĩhoko?
English: where then is my hope? As for my hope, who will see it?

Kikuyu: Na rĩrĩ, mwĩhoko nĩũharũrũkĩte nginya ihingo-inĩ cia gĩkuũ? Nĩtũgũgĩikũrũkania hamwe rũkũngũ-inĩ?”
English: Shall it go down with me to the gates of Sheol,‡ or descend together into the dust?”

Kikuyu: Ningĩ Bilidadi ũrĩa Mũshuhi agĩcookia, akĩũria atĩrĩ:
English: Then Bildad the Shuhite answered,

Kikuyu: “Ũrĩĩtiga kwaria mĩario ĩno rĩ? Gĩa na ũũgĩ nĩguo o na ithuĩ tũhote kwaria.
English: “How long will you hunt for words? Consider, and afterwards we will speak.

Kikuyu: Nĩ kĩĩ kĩratũma ũtuone tũhaana ta ngʼombe, na tũgatuuo irimũ maitho-inĩ maku?
English: Why are we counted as animals, which have become unclean in your sight?

Kikuyu: Wee ũrehanyũrũra nĩ ũndũ wa ũrĩa ũrakarĩte-rĩ, thĩ no ĩthaamwo nĩ ũndũ waku? Kana no nginya ndwaro cia mahiga cieherio harĩa itũire?
English: You who tear yourself in your anger, will the earth be forsaken for you? Or will the rock be removed out of its place?

Kikuyu: “Tawa wa mũndũ mwaganu nĩmũhorie; rũrĩrĩmbĩ rwa mwaki wake nĩrũtigĩte gwakana.
English: “Yes, the light of the wicked will be put out. The spark of his fire won’t shine.

Kikuyu: Ũtheri ũrĩa ũrĩ thĩinĩ wa hema yake ũtuĩkĩte nduma; naguo tawa ũrĩa ũrĩ hakuhĩ nake ũkahora.
English: The light will be dark in his tent. His lamp above him will be put out.

Kikuyu: Hinya wa mũkinyũkĩrie wake nĩmũhũthie; namo mathugunda make makamũgũithia thĩ.
English: The steps of his strength will be shortened. His own counsel will cast him down.

Kikuyu: Makinya make mamũikagia wabu-inĩ, nake akoorũraga thĩinĩ wa marima mayo.
English: For he is cast into a net by his own feet, and he wanders into its mesh.

Kikuyu: Mũtego ũmũnyiitĩire ndiira-inĩ ya kũgũrũ; mũtego ũgakĩmũrũmia biũ.
English: A snare will take him by the heel. A trap will catch him.

Kikuyu: Ahithĩirwo kĩana kĩa rũrigi tĩĩri-inĩ, akaambĩrwo mũtego njĩra-inĩ yake.
English: A noose is hidden for him in the ground, a trap for him on the path.

Kikuyu: Imakania imuumagĩrĩra na mĩena yothe, na ikamũtengʼeragia harĩa hothe aagerera.
English: Terrors will make him afraid on every side, and will chase him at his heels.

Kikuyu: Mũtino nĩũmũhũũtĩire; mwanangĩko wetereire agwe.
English: His strength will be famished. Calamity will be ready at his side.

Kikuyu: Mũtino ũrĩĩaga icunjĩ cia gĩkonde gĩake; narĩo irigithathi rĩa gĩkuũ rĩgatambuuranga ciĩga ciake.
English: The members of his body will be devoured. The firstborn of death will devour his members.

Kikuyu: Aguucĩtio, akarutwo ũgitĩri-inĩ wa hema yake, na agatwarwo kũrĩ mũthamaki wa imakania.
English: He will be rooted out of the security of his tent. He will be brought to the king of terrors.

Kikuyu: Mwaki nĩguo ũtũũraga hema-inĩ yake; ũbiriti ũgwakana nĩũhurunjĩtwo gĩikaro gĩake.
English: There will dwell in his tent that which is none of his. Sulfur will be scattered on his habitation.

Kikuyu: Mĩri yake yũmagĩra tĩĩri-inĩ, nacio honge ciake ikahooha na igũrũ.
English: His roots will be dried up beneath. His branch will be cut off above.

Kikuyu: Kĩririkano gĩake nĩ gĩgaathira thĩ; ndarĩ rĩĩtwa bũrũri-inĩ.
English: His memory will perish from the earth. He will have no name in the street.

Kikuyu: Akaarutũrũrwo ũtheri-inĩ atwarwo nduma-inĩ na nĩakaingatwo oime thĩ ĩno.
English: He will be driven from light into darkness, and chased out of the world.

Kikuyu: Ndarĩ ciana kana njiaro thĩinĩ wa andũ ao, o na ndarĩ mũndũ wake ũgaatigara kũrĩa aatũũraga.
English: He will have neither son nor grandson among his people, nor any remaining where he lived.

Kikuyu: Andũ a mwena wa ithũĩro nĩmakagegio nĩ maũndũ marĩa mamũkorete; andũ a mwena wa irathĩro manyiitwo nĩ kĩmako.
English: Those who come after will be astonished at his day, as those who went before were frightened.

Kikuyu: Ti-itherũ ũguo nĩguo gĩikaro kĩa mũndũ mwaganu gũkahaana; kũndũ kwa mũndũ ũrĩa ũtooĩ Mũrungu-rĩ, gwake kũhaana ũguo.”
English: Surely such are the dwellings of the unrighteous. This is the place of him who doesn’t know God.”

Kikuyu: Nake Ayubu akĩũria atĩrĩ:
English: Then Job answered,

Kikuyu: “Mũkũũnyariira nginya-rĩ, mũkĩĩhehenjaga na ciugo?
English: “How long will you torment me, and crush me with words?

Kikuyu: Rĩu mũrĩ kũndetia maita ikũmi; mũũtharĩkĩire mũtarĩ na thoni.
English: You have reproached me ten times. You aren’t ashamed that you attack me.

Kikuyu: Angĩkorwo nĩ ma atĩ nĩhĩtĩtie njĩra, ihĩtia rĩakwa rĩgũikara rĩrĩ thĩĩna wakwa.
English: If it is true that I have erred, my error remains with myself.

Kikuyu: Mũngĩkorwo ti-itherũ nĩmũgwĩtũũgĩria igũrũ rĩakwa, na mũgĩe na mweke wa kũnjũkĩrĩra nĩ ũndũ wa ũguo njonorithĩtio,
English: If indeed you will magnify yourselves against me, and plead against me my reproach,

Kikuyu: no kĩmenyei atĩ Ngai nĩwe ũũhĩtĩirie, akandigiicĩria na wabu wake.
English: know now that God has subverted me, and has surrounded me with his net.

Kikuyu: “O na gũtuĩka nĩngayaga ngoiga atĩrĩ, ‘Ndĩĩmũhĩtĩrie!’ Niĩ ndirĩ ũndũ njookagĩrio; o na gũtuĩka nĩhooyaga ndeithio, gũtirĩ kĩhooto nyonaga.
English: “Behold, I cry out of wrong, but I am not heard. I cry for help, but there is no justice.

Kikuyu: Nĩahingĩire njĩra na niĩ ndingĩhota kũhĩtũka; tũcĩra twakwa nĩatwĩkĩrĩte nduma.
English: He has walled up my way so that I can’t pass, and has set darkness in my paths.

Kikuyu: Nĩanjaũrĩte gĩtĩĩo gĩakwa, na akanduta thũmbĩ mũtwe.
English: He has stripped me of my glory, and taken the crown from my head.

Kikuyu: Andarũrangaga kuuma mbarĩ ciothe nginya ngathira; amunyaga mwĩhoko wakwa o ta mũtĩ.
English: He has broken me down on every side, and I am gone. He has plucked my hope up like a tree.

Kikuyu: Marakara make nĩmanjakanĩire; andaraga hamwe na thũ ciake.
English: He has also kindled his wrath against me. He counts me among his adversaries.

Kikuyu: Mbũtũ ciake cia ita injerekagĩra na hinya; ciakaga ihumbu cia kũnjũkĩrĩra, igathiũrũrũkĩria hema yakwa.
English: His troops come on together, build a siege ramp against me, and encamp around my tent.

Kikuyu: “Nĩanyamũranĩtie na ariũ a baba makaahutatĩra; andũ arĩa tũyaine nao nĩmeĩndigithĩtie biũ.
English: “He has put my brothers far from me. My acquaintances are wholly estranged from me.

Kikuyu: Andũ a mbarĩ ciitũ nĩmathiĩte makandiga; arata akwa nĩmariganĩirwo nĩ niĩ.
English: My relatives have gone away. My familiar friends have forgotten me.

Kikuyu: Ageni akwa na ndungata ciakwa cia andũ-a-nja matuaga ta matanjũũĩ; maanyonaga ta ndĩ mũndũ uumĩte kũndũ kũngĩ.
English: Those who dwell in my house and my maids consider me a stranger. I am an alien in their sight.

Kikuyu: Njĩtaga ndungata yakwa, no ndĩngĩnjĩtĩka, o na ndĩmĩthaithĩte na kanua gakwa niĩ mwene.
English: I call to my servant, and he gives me no answer. I beg him with my mouth.

Kikuyu: Mĩhũmũ ya kanua gakwa nĩmĩnungu harĩ mũtumia wakwa; nduĩkĩte wa kũmenwo harĩ ariũ a maitũ.
English: My breath is offensive to my wife. I am loathsome to the children of my own mother.

Kikuyu: O na tũhĩĩ tũrĩa tũnini nĩtũũnyararĩte, rĩrĩa ndatuumĩrĩra no gũũthekerera tũũthekagĩrĩra.
English: Even young children despise me. If I arise, they speak against me.

Kikuyu: Arata akwa arĩa manguhĩrĩirie othe nĩmathũire; andũ arĩa nyendeete nĩmahutatĩire makaanjũkĩrĩra.
English: All my familiar friends abhor me. They whom I loved have turned against me.

Kikuyu: Niĩ thirĩte ngatigara o gĩkonde na mahĩndĩ; niĩ ndigarĩirwo no kĩni kĩa magego giiki.
English: My bones stick to my skin and to my flesh. I have escaped by the skin of my teeth.

Kikuyu: “Njiguĩrai tha, inyuĩ arata akwa, iguai tha, nĩgũkorwo guoko kwa Ngai nĩkũngũthĩte.
English: “Have pity on me. Have pity on me, you my friends, for the hand of God has touched me.

Kikuyu: Mũthingatanaga na niĩ o ta ũrĩa Mũrungu aathingataga nĩkĩ? Mũtirĩ mũraiganwo nĩ nyama ciakwa?
English: Why do you persecute me as God, and are not satisfied with my flesh?

Kikuyu: “Naarĩ korwo ciugo ciakwa nĩciandĩkĩtwo, igakĩandĩkwo ibuku-inĩ rĩa gĩkũnjo,
English: “Oh that my words were now written! Oh that they were inscribed in a book!

Kikuyu: igakarwo na karamu ga kĩgera igũrũ rĩa ngocorai, kana igakururwo rwaro-inĩ rwa ihiga itũũre nginya tene!
English: That with an iron pen and lead they were engraved in the rock forever!

Kikuyu: Nĩnjũũĩ atĩ Mũngũũri arĩ muoyo, na atĩ marigĩrĩrio-inĩ nĩwe ũkaarũgama thĩ ĩno.
English: But as for me, I know that my Redeemer lives. In the end, he will stand upon the earth.

Kikuyu: Nakĩo gĩkonde gĩkĩ gĩakwa kĩarĩkia gũthira, na mwĩrĩ ũyũ wa nyama ũkorwo ũtarĩ ho, hĩndĩ ĩyo nĩ ngoona Ngai;
English: After my skin is destroyed, then I will see God in my flesh,

Kikuyu: niĩ mwene nĩngamwĩonera na maitho, niĩ mwene, ti mũndũ ũngĩ. Ĩ ngoro yakwa ndĩkĩrĩ na wendo mũnene!
English: whom I, even I, will see on my side. My eyes will see, and not as a stranger. “My heart is consumed within me.

Kikuyu: “Mũngiuga atĩrĩ, ‘Ĩ nĩtũthingatane nake, kuona atĩ nĩwe kĩhumo gĩa thĩĩna ũyũ,’
English: If you say, ‘How we will persecute him!’ because the root of the matter is found in me,

Kikuyu: inyuĩ ene nĩmwagĩrĩirwo nĩ gwĩtigĩra rũhiũ rwa njora; nĩgũkorwo mangʼũrĩ nĩmakarehithia kũherithanio na rũhiũ rwa njora, na hĩndĩ ĩyo nĩmũkamenya atĩ nĩ kũrĩ ũtuanĩri wa ciira.”
English: be afraid of the sword, for wrath brings the punishments of the sword, that you may know there is a judgment.”

Kikuyu: Nake Zofaru ũrĩa Mũnaamathi agĩcookia atĩrĩ:
English: Then Zophar the Naamathite answered,

Kikuyu: “Meciiria makwa nĩ mathĩĩnĩku, na nĩkĩo ngũcookia, nĩ ũndũ nĩndangĩkĩte mũno.
English: “Therefore my thoughts answer me, even by reason of my haste that is in me.

Kikuyu: Ndĩraigua irũithia rĩa kũnjonorithia, naguo ũmenyo wakwa nĩũranjĩkĩra hinya wa gũcookia.
English: I have heard the reproof which puts me to shame. The spirit of my understanding answers me.

Kikuyu: “Ti-itherũ nĩũũĩ ũrĩa gũtũire kuuma tene rĩrĩa mũndũ aigirwo gũkũ thĩ ĩno,
English: Don’t you know this from old time, since man was placed on earth,

Kikuyu: atĩ kũrũũhia kwa arĩa aaganu no gwa kahinda, o nakĩo gĩkeno kĩa andũ arĩa matooĩ Ngai no gĩa kahinda kanini.
English: that the triumphing of the wicked is short, the joy of the godless but for a moment?

Kikuyu: O na gũtuĩka mwĩtĩĩo wake nĩ ũkinyaga o igũrũ, naguo mũtwe wake ũkahutia matu-rĩ,
English: Though his height mount up to the heavens, and his head reach to the clouds,

Kikuyu: agaathira nginya tene o ta mai make mwene; arĩa manamuona mooragie atĩrĩ, ‘Kaĩ aathiire kũ?’
English: yet he will perish forever like his own dung. Those who have seen him will say, ‘Where is he?’

Kikuyu: Airagĩria ta kĩroto, akaaga kuoneka rĩngĩ, akaingatwo ta kĩoneki kĩa ũtukũ.
English: He will fly away as a dream, and will not be found. Yes, he will be chased away like a vision of the night.

Kikuyu: Riitho rĩrĩa rĩamuonaga rĩtikamuona rĩngĩ; harĩa aaikaraga hatikamuona rĩngĩ.
English: The eye which saw him will see him no more, neither will his place see him any more.

Kikuyu: Ciana ciake ikaageragia kwĩiguithania na athĩĩni; moko make mwene no nginya magaacookia ũtonga wake kũrĩa aaũrutire.
English: His children will seek the favor of the poor. His hands will give back his wealth.

Kikuyu: Hinya wa wĩthĩ ũrĩa ũiyũrĩte mahĩndĩ-inĩ make ũgaakoma hamwe nake rũkũngũ-inĩ.
English: His bones are full of his youth, but youth will lie down with him in the dust.

Kikuyu: “O na gũtuĩka ũũru ũrĩ mũrĩo ũrĩ kanua gake, na nĩaũhithaga rungu rwa rũrĩmĩ rwake,
English: “Though wickedness is sweet in his mouth, though he hide it under his tongue,

Kikuyu: o na gũtuĩka ndangĩhota kũũrekia na aũigaga kanua gake-rĩ,
English: though he spare it, and will not let it go, but keep it still within his mouth,

Kikuyu: irio ciake nĩikarũra irĩ nda yake; igaatuĩka ũrũrũ wa nduĩra thĩinĩ wake.
English: yet his food in his bowels is turned. It is cobra venom within him.

Kikuyu: Nĩagatahĩka ũtonga ũrĩa ameretie; Mũrungu nĩagatũma aũtahĩke.
English: He has swallowed down riches, and he will vomit them up again. God will cast them out of his belly.

Kikuyu: Nĩakoonga thumu wa nyoka; magego ma nyoka nĩmo makaamũũraga.
English: He will suck cobra venom. The viper’s tongue will kill him.

Kikuyu: Ndagakenera tũrũũĩ, njũũĩ iria ithereraga ũũkĩ na ngorono.
English: He will not look at the rivers, the flowing streams of honey and butter.

Kikuyu: Kĩndũ kĩrĩa anogeire no nginya agagĩcookia atakĩrĩte; ndagakenera uumithio wa wonjoria wake.
English: He will restore that for which he labored, and will not swallow it down. He will not rejoice according to the substance that he has gotten.

Kikuyu: Nĩgũkorwo nĩahinyĩrĩirie athĩĩni, akamatiga matarĩ na kĩndũ; nĩatunyanĩte nyũmba iria ataakire.
English: For he has oppressed and forsaken the poor. He has violently taken away a house, and he will not build it up.

Kikuyu: “Ti-itherũ merirĩria make matingĩthira; ndangĩĩhonokia na indo iria eigĩire.
English: “Because he knew no quietness within him, he will not save anything of that in which he delights.

Kikuyu: Gũtirĩ kĩndũ atigĩirio gĩa kũrĩa; ũtonga wake ndũgatũũra.
English: There was nothing left that he didn’t devour, therefore his prosperity will not endure.

Kikuyu: Hĩndĩ ĩrĩa aiganĩire nĩ ũndũ wa kũingĩhia indo, mĩnyamaro nĩĩkamũnyiita; ũkĩa nĩũkamũkora na nditi nene.
English: In the fullness of his sufficiency, distress will overtake him. The hand of everyone who is in misery will come on him.

Kikuyu: Hĩndĩ ĩrĩa aiyũrĩtie nda yake-rĩ, nĩguo Ngai akaarekereria marakara make mahiũ mamũkore na amuurĩrie mahũũra make.
English: When he is about to fill his belly, God will cast the fierceness of his wrath on him. It will rain on him while he is eating.

Kikuyu: O na angĩũrĩra indo cia mbaara cia kĩgera, akaarathwo na mũguĩ wa gĩcango.
English: He will flee from the iron weapon. The bronze arrow will strike him through.

Kikuyu: Aũcomoraga kuuma ngʼongʼo wake, mũtheece ũcio mũkengu akaũcomora kuuma ini-inĩ rĩake. Imakania nĩikamũkorerera;
English: He draws it out, and it comes out of his body. Yes, the glittering point comes out of his liver. Terrors are on him.

Kikuyu: nduma nene nĩyetereire igĩĩna ciake. Mwaki ũtarĩ mũhurutĩre nĩũkamũcina, na ũniine kĩrĩa gĩtigaire thĩinĩ wa hema yake.
English: All darkness is laid up for his treasures. An unfanned fire will devour him. It will consume that which is left in his tent.

Kikuyu: Igũrũ nĩrĩkaguũria wĩhia wake; thĩ nayo nĩĩkarahũka ĩmũũkĩrĩre.
English: The heavens will reveal his iniquity. The earth will rise up against him.

Kikuyu: Kĩguũ nĩgĩgathereria nyũmba yake, indo cia nyũmba yake ithererio nĩ kĩguũ mũthenya ũcio wa mangʼũrĩ ma Ngai.
English: The increase of his house will depart. They will rush away in the day of his wrath.

Kikuyu: Ũcio nĩguo ũndũ ũrĩa Ngai agayagĩra arĩa aaganu, igai rĩrĩa maathĩrĩirwo nĩ Mũrungu.”
English: This is the portion of a wicked man from God, the heritage appointed to him by God.”

Kikuyu: Ningĩ Ayubu agĩcookia atĩrĩ:
English: Then Job answered,

Kikuyu: “Thikĩrĩriai wega ciugo ciakwa; rekei ũndũ ũyũ ũtuĩke nĩguo mũkũũhooreria naguo.
English: “Listen diligently to my speech. Let this be your consolation.

Kikuyu: Ngirĩrĩriai na niĩ njarie, na ndaarĩkia kwaria-rĩ, mũgĩcooke mũũnyũrũrie.
English: Allow me, and I also will speak. After I have spoken, mock on.

Kikuyu: “Niĩ-rĩ, kaĩ mateta makwa meerekeirio mũndũ? Ngũkĩaga kũremwo nĩ gũkirĩrĩria nĩkĩ?
English: As for me, is my complaint to man? Why shouldn’t I be impatient?

Kikuyu: Ta ndorai mũgege; mwĩnyiite tũnua twanyu na moko nĩ kũmaka.
English: Look at me, and be astonished. Lay your hand on your mouth.

Kikuyu: Ndĩciiragia ũhoro ũyũ ngamaka mũno; ngethithimũkwo nĩ mwĩrĩ, ngambĩrĩria kũinaina.
English: When I remember, I am troubled. Horror takes hold of my flesh.

Kikuyu: Atĩrĩ, andũ arĩa aaganu marekagwo matũũre muoyo nĩkĩ, magakũra o na magakĩrĩrĩria kũgĩa na ũhoti?
English: “Why do the wicked live, become old, yes, and grow mighty in power?

Kikuyu: Nĩmeonagĩra ciana ciao ikĩgaacĩra kũu marĩ, makoona rũciaro rwao rũkĩĩhaanda mbere ya maitho mao.
English: Their child is established with them in their sight, their offspring before their eyes.

Kikuyu: Mĩciĩ yao ĩikaraga ĩgitĩirwo na ĩtarĩ na guoya; naruo rũthanju rwa Ngai rũtimahũũraga.
English: Their houses are safe from fear, neither is the rod of God upon them.

Kikuyu: Ndegwa ciao itiagaga kũgwatia; ngʼombe ciao iciaraga, na itihunaga.
English: Their bulls breed without fail. Their cows calve, and don’t miscarry.

Kikuyu: Moimagaragia twana twao tũingĩ o ta rũũru; ciana icio ciao ikaina igĩtũrũhaga.
English: They send out their little ones like a flock. Their children dance.

Kikuyu: Nao o ene mainaga makĩhũũraga tũhembe na inanda cia mũgeeto; mekenagia na mũgambo wa mũtũrirũ.
English: They sing to the tambourine and harp, and rejoice at the sound of the pipe.

Kikuyu: Matũũraga mĩaka yao magaacĩire, na magathiĩ mbĩrĩra-inĩ marĩ na thayũ.
English: They spend their days in prosperity. In an instant they go down to Sheol.†

Kikuyu: Na no-o meeraga Mũrungu atĩrĩ, ‘Thiĩ! Tigana na ithuĩ! Tũtikwenda kũmenya njĩra ciaku.
English: They tell God, ‘Depart from us, for we don’t want to know about your ways.

Kikuyu: Mwene-Hinya-Wothe nĩwe ũ, atĩ nĩguo tũmũtungatagĩre? Tũkũgunĩka nakĩ tũngĩmũhooya?’
English: What is the Almighty, that we should serve him? What profit should we have, if we pray to him?’

Kikuyu: No rĩrĩ, kũgaacĩra kwao gũtirĩ moko-inĩ mao ene, nĩ ũndũ ũcio niĩ njikaraga haraaya na kĩrĩra kĩa andũ arĩa aaganu.
English: Behold, their prosperity is not in their hand. The counsel of the wicked is far from me.

Kikuyu: “Na rĩrĩ, nĩ maita maigana tawa wa arĩa aaganu ũhoragio? Nĩ maita maigana makoragwo nĩ mũtino, na nĩ maita maigana Ngai amagayagĩra ruo nĩ kũmarakarĩra?
English: “How often is it that the lamp of the wicked is put out, that their calamity comes on them, that God distributes sorrows in his anger?

Kikuyu: Nĩ maita maigana matuĩkaga ta nyeki nyũmũ ĩkũhurutwo nĩ rũhuho, o na kana ta maragara marĩa mombũragwo nĩ kĩhuhũkanio?
English: How often is it that they are as stubble before the wind, as chaff that the storm carries away?

Kikuyu: Kuugagwo atĩrĩ, ‘Ngai aigagĩra ciana iherithia rĩa ithe wao.’ No rĩrĩ, nĩ kaba Ngai aherithie mũndũ ũcio we mwene, nĩguo amenye nĩehĩtie!
English: You say, ‘God lays up his iniquity for his children.’ Let him recompense it to himself, that he may know it.

Kikuyu: Maitho make nĩmeyonere mwanangĩko wake mwene; nĩarekwo akunde mangʼũrĩ ma Mwene-Hinya-Wothe.
English: Let his own eyes see his destruction. Let him drink of the wrath of the Almighty.

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ-rĩ, anga no eetangaga ha ũhoro wa andũ ake arĩa agaatiga na thuutha, matukũ make maathira?
English: For what does he care for his house after him, when the number of his months is cut off?

Kikuyu: “Nĩ kũrĩ mũndũ o na ũmwe ũngĩhota kũruta Mũrungu atĩ nĩguo agĩe na ũmenyo, kuona atĩ Mũrungu nĩwe ũtuanagĩra ciira, o na agatuĩra arĩa atũũgĩirie mũno?
English: “Shall any teach God knowledge, since he judges those who are high?

Kikuyu: Nĩ kũrĩ mũndũ ũkuuaga arĩ na hinya wake wothe, arĩ mũgitĩre wega biũ, na arĩ na thayũ,
English: One dies in his full strength, being wholly at ease and quiet.

Kikuyu: mwĩrĩ wake ũheetwo irio wega, na mahĩndĩ ma mĩthiimo yake marĩ o maigũ.
English: His pails are full of milk. The marrow of his bones is moistened.

Kikuyu: Mũndũ ũngĩ agakua arĩ na marũrũ ma ngoro, atarĩ aakenera kĩndũ kĩega o na kĩ.
English: Another dies in bitterness of soul, and never tastes of good.

Kikuyu: Makomaga o ro ũndũ ũmwe tĩĩri-inĩ, na eerĩ-rĩ, igunyũ ikamahumbĩra.
English: They lie down alike in the dust. The worm covers them.

Kikuyu: “Niĩ nĩnjũũĩ wega ũrĩa mũreciiria, ngamenya mathugunda manyu maakũhĩtĩria namo.
English: “Behold, I know your thoughts, the plans with which you would wrong me.

Kikuyu: Mũrooria atĩrĩ, ‘Rĩu nyũmba ya mũndũ ũrĩa mũnene ĩkĩrĩ ha, na hema ĩrĩa andũ aaganu maratũũraga-rĩ, ĩkĩrĩ ha?’
English: For you say, ‘Where is the house of the prince? Where is the tent in which the wicked lived?’

Kikuyu: Kaĩ mũtarĩ muoria andũ arĩa mathiiaga ngʼendo? Kaĩ mũtarũmbũyagia ũrĩa mamwĩraga:
English: Haven’t you asked wayfaring men? Don’t you know their evidences,

Kikuyu: atĩ mũndũ ũrĩa mwaganu nĩ aiguagĩrwo tha mũthenya wa mũtino, atĩ nĩahonokagio mũthenya wa mangʼũrĩ?
English: that the evil man is reserved to the day of calamity, that they are led out to the day of wrath?

Kikuyu: Nũũ ũreganaga na mĩtugo ya mũndũ mwaganu maitho-inĩ make? Nũũ ũmũrĩhagia kũringana na maũndũ marĩa aaneka?
English: Who will declare his way to his face? Who will repay him what he has done?

Kikuyu: Atwaragwo mbĩrĩra-inĩ, nayo mbĩrĩra yake ĩkarangagĩrwo.
English: Yet he will be borne to the grave. Men will keep watch over the tomb.

Kikuyu: Tĩĩri wa gĩtuamba nĩũrĩ mũrĩo harĩ we; andũ othe nĩwe marũmagĩrĩra, na kĩrĩndĩ gĩtangĩtarĩka gĩgathiiaga mbere yake.
English: The clods of the valley will be sweet to him. All men will draw after him, as there were innumerable before him.

Kikuyu: “Mwakĩhota atĩa kũũhooreria na ndeto cia tũhũ? Hatirĩ kĩndũ gĩtigaru harĩ macookio manyu tiga o maheeni!”
English: So how can you comfort me with nonsense, because in your answers there remains only falsehood?”

Kikuyu: Nake Elifazu ũrĩa Mũtemaani agĩcookia atĩrĩ:
English: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered,

Kikuyu: “Mũndũ aahota kũguna Mũrungu? O na mũndũ mũũgĩ-rĩ, akĩhota kũmũguna?
English: “Can a man be profitable to God? Surely he who is wise is profitable to himself.

Kikuyu: Nĩ gĩkeno kĩrĩkũ ũthingu waku ũngĩrehere Mwene-Hinya-Wothe? Nĩ uumithio ũrĩkũ angĩgĩa naguo angĩkorwo mĩthiĩre yaku ndĩrĩ ũcuuke?
English: Is it any pleasure to the Almighty that you are righteous? Or does it benefit him that you make your ways perfect?

Kikuyu: “Arakũrũithia na agagũthitanga nĩ ũndũ wa wĩtigĩri Ngai waku?
English: Is it for your piety that he reproves you, that he enters with you into judgment?

Kikuyu: Githĩ waganu waku ti mũnene? Mehia maku-rĩ, makĩrĩ mũthia?
English: Isn’t your wickedness great? Neither is there any end to your iniquities.

Kikuyu: Wetirie ũgitĩri kuuma kũrĩ ariũ a thoguo hatarĩ gĩtũmi; nĩwaũrire andũ nguo, ũkĩmatiga njaga.
English: For you have taken pledges from your brother for nothing, and stripped the naked of their clothing.

Kikuyu: Arĩa anogu ndwamaheire maaĩ, na nĩwaimire arĩa ahũtu irio,
English: You haven’t given water to the weary to drink, and you have withheld bread from the hungry.

Kikuyu: o na gũtuĩka warĩ mũndũ ũrĩ hinya, ũrĩ na mĩgũnda: mũndũ ũheetwo gĩtĩĩo, na watũũraga kuo.
English: But as for the mighty man, he had the earth. The honorable man, he lived in it.

Kikuyu: Nĩwaingatire atumia a ndigwa matarĩ na kĩndũ, na ũkĩniina hinya wa arĩa matarĩ na maithe.
English: You have sent widows away empty, and the arms of the fatherless have been broken.

Kikuyu: Nĩkĩo ũthiũrũrũkĩirio nĩ mĩtego, nĩkĩo thĩĩna wa narua ũkũmakagia,
English: Therefore snares are around you. Sudden fear troubles you,

Kikuyu: nĩkĩo ũtumanĩirwo nĩ nduma, ũkaremwo nĩkuona, na nokĩo mũiyũro wa maaĩ ũkũhubanĩirie.
English: or darkness, so that you can not see, and floods of waters cover you.

Kikuyu: “Githĩ Ngai ndarĩ o kũu igũrũ o igũrũ? O na ta kĩone ũrĩa njata iria irĩ igũrũ mũno itũũgĩrĩte!
English: “Isn’t God in the heights of heaven? See the height of the stars, how high they are!

Kikuyu: No rĩrĩ, wee ũroiga atĩrĩ, ‘Mũrungu nĩ atĩa angĩmenya? No atuanĩre ciira nduma-inĩ ta ĩno?
English: You say, ‘What does God know? Can he judge through the thick darkness?

Kikuyu: Matu matumanu nĩmamũhumbĩrĩte, nĩ ũndũ ũcio ndangĩtuona rĩrĩa egũceera kũu igũrũ gacũmbĩrĩ.’
English: Thick clouds are a covering to him, so that he doesn’t see. He walks on the vault of the sky.’

Kikuyu: Ũgũtũũra ũgeraga o njĩra ya tene ĩrĩa andũ aaganu managerera?
English: Will you keep the old way, which wicked men have trodden,

Kikuyu: Nĩmahuririo ihinda rĩao rĩtanakinya, mĩthingi yao ĩgĩthererio nĩ mũiyũro wa maaĩ.
English: who were snatched away before their time, whose foundation was poured out as a stream,

Kikuyu: Nao meerire Mũrungu atĩrĩ, ‘Tigana na ithuĩ! Mwene-Hinya-Wothe-rĩ, angĩtwĩka atĩa?’
English: who said to God, ‘Depart from us!’ and, ‘What can the Almighty do for us?’

Kikuyu: No rĩrĩ, nĩwe waiyũririe nyũmba ciao na indo njega, nĩ ũndũ ũcio niĩ njikaraga haraaya na kĩrĩra kĩa andũ arĩa aaganu.
English: Yet he filled their houses with good things, but the counsel of the wicked is far from me.

Kikuyu: “Andũ arĩa athingu nĩmeyonagĩra mwanangĩko wa acio aaganu, magakena; arĩa matarĩ na ũũru mekĩte mamanyũrũragia makiugaga atĩrĩ:
English: The righteous see it, and are glad. The innocent ridicule them,

Kikuyu: ‘Ti-itherũ thũ ciitũ nĩnyanange, mwaki nĩũcinĩte ũtonga wao.’
English: saying, ‘Surely those who rose up against us are cut off. The fire has consumed their remnant.’

Kikuyu: “Athĩkĩra Ngai ũikare ũrĩ na thayũ nake, ũndũ ũyũ nĩguo ũgaakũrehere ũgaacĩru.
English: “Acquaint yourself with him now, and be at peace. By it, good will come to you.

Kikuyu: Ĩtĩkĩra ũrutani wa kanua gake, na ũige ciugo ciake ngoro-inĩ yaku.
English: Please receive instruction from his mouth, and lay up his words in your heart.

Kikuyu: Ũngĩcookerera ũcio Mwene-Hinya-Wothe, nĩegũkwamũkĩra; ũngĩeheria waganu kũraya na hema yaku,
English: If you return to the Almighty, you will be built up, if you put away unrighteousness far from your tents.

Kikuyu: na ũte ngũmba ciaku cia thahabu rũkũngũ-inĩ, na thahabu yaku ya Ofiri ũmĩte na kũu ndwaro-inĩ cia mahiga kũu mũkuru-inĩ,
English: Lay your treasure in the dust, the gold of Ophir among the stones of the brooks.

Kikuyu: hĩndĩ ĩyo ũcio Mwene-Hinya-Wothe agaatuĩka thahabu yaku, na atuĩke betha ĩrĩa njega mũno harĩ we.
English: The Almighty will be your treasure, and precious silver to you.

Kikuyu: Ti-itherũ, hĩndĩ ĩyo nĩũkona gĩkeno thĩinĩ wa ũcio Mwene-Hinya-Wothe, na nĩũgatiirĩra Ngai ũthiũ waku.
English: For then you will delight yourself in the Almighty, and will lift up your face to God.

Kikuyu: Nĩũkamũhooya, nake nĩagakũigua, nawe nĩũkahingia mĩĩhĩtwa yaku.
English: You will make your prayer to him, and he will hear you. You will pay your vows.

Kikuyu: Ũrĩa watua wĩkwo nĩguo ũrĩkagwo, naguo ũtheri nĩ ũkaara njĩra-inĩ ciaku.
English: You will also decree a thing, and it will be established to you. Light will shine on your ways.

Kikuyu: Hĩndĩ ĩrĩa andũ angĩ manyiihio, nawe ũkoiga, ‘Nĩmatũũgĩrio!’ Hĩndĩ ĩyo nĩakahonokia arĩa makuĩte ngoro.
English: When they cast down, you will say, ‘be lifted up.’ He will save the humble person.

Kikuyu: Nĩakahonokia o na ũrĩa ũrĩ na ũcuuke, ahonokio nĩ ũndũ wa ũtheru wa moko maku.”
English: He will even deliver him who is not innocent. Yes, he will be delivered through the cleanness of your hands.”

Kikuyu: Ningĩ Ayubu agĩcookia atĩrĩ:
English: Then Job answered,

Kikuyu: “O na ũmũthĩ gũteta gwakwa no kũrũrũ; guoko gwake nĩkũnditũhĩire o na ngĩcaayaga ũguo.
English: “Even today my complaint is rebellious. His hand is heavy in spite of my groaning.

Kikuyu: Naarĩ korwo nĩnjũũĩ kũrĩa ingĩmuona; Naarĩ korwo no hote gũthiĩ kũrĩa aikaraga!
English: Oh that I knew where I might find him! That I might come even to his seat!

Kikuyu: Ingĩĩyarĩrĩria harĩ we, njiyũrie kanua gakwa ihooto.
English: I would set my cause in order before him, and fill my mouth with arguments.

Kikuyu: No nyende kũmenya ũrĩa angĩĩnjookeria, ndĩcũũranie ũrĩa angĩnjĩĩra.
English: I would know the words which he would answer me, and understand what he would tell me.

Kikuyu: No anjũkĩrĩre na ũhoti wake mũnene? Aca, ndangĩhatĩrĩria na thitango.
English: Would he contend with me in the greatness of his power? No, but he would listen to me.

Kikuyu: Hau-rĩ, mũndũ mũrũngĩrĩru no atware ciira wake mbere yake, na niĩ njohorithio kuuma kũrĩ mũnjiirithia nginya tene.
English: There the upright might reason with him, so I should be delivered forever from my judge.

Kikuyu: “No rĩrĩ, ingĩthiĩ mwena wa irathĩro, we ndarĩ kuo; ingĩthiĩ mwena wa ithũĩro, ndiramuona.
English: “If I go east, he is not there. If I go west, I can’t find him.

Kikuyu: Hĩndĩ ĩrĩa arĩ wĩra-inĩ mwena wa gathigathini, ndimuonaga; rĩrĩa athiĩ mwena wa gũthini, ndimuonaga o na hanini.
English: He works to the north, but I can’t see him. He turns south, but I can’t catch a glimpse of him.

Kikuyu: Nowe-rĩ, nĩooĩ njĩra ĩrĩa ngeragĩra; aarĩkia kũngeria, ngoima haana o ta thahabu.
English: But he knows the way that I take. When he has tried me, I will come out like gold.

Kikuyu: Magũrũ makwa moimĩte makinya make thuutha; nũmagĩrĩra njĩra yake itekwahũka na mwena.
English: My foot has held fast to his steps. I have kept his way, and not turned away.

Kikuyu: Niĩ nditiganĩirie maathani ma mĩromo yake; njĩkĩrĩire ciugo cia kanua gake gũkĩra irio ciakwa cia o mũthenya.
English: I haven’t gone back from the commandment of his lips. I have treasured up the words of his mouth more than my necessary food.

Kikuyu: “No rĩrĩ, arũgamaga arĩ o wiki; nũũ ũngĩhota kũregana nake? Ekaga o ũrĩa ekwenda.
English: But he stands alone, and who can oppose him? What his soul desires, even that he does.

Kikuyu: Ahingagia ũndũ ũrĩa anduĩrĩire, na arĩ o na mĩbango mĩingĩ ta ĩyo anjigĩire.
English: For he performs that which is appointed for me. Many such things are with him.

Kikuyu: Kĩu nĩkĩo gĩtũmĩte nyiitwo nĩ kĩmako ndĩ mbere yake; ndeciiria maũndũ macio mothe-rĩ, ngamwĩtigĩra.
English: Therefore I am terrified at his presence. When I consider, I am afraid of him.

Kikuyu: Mũrungu nĩatũmĩte ngoro yakwa yũrwo nĩ hinya; ũcio Mwene-Hinya-Wothe nĩatũmĩte nyiitwo nĩ guoya.
English: For God has made my heart faint. The Almighty has terrified me.

Kikuyu: No rĩrĩ, ndikirĩtio nĩ nduma, ĩĩ nduma ĩyo ndumanu ĩhumbĩrĩte ũthiũ wakwa.
English: Because I was not cut off before the darkness, neither did he cover the thick darkness from my face.

Kikuyu: “Nĩ kĩĩ kĩgiragia Mwene-Hinya-Wothe araarĩrie mahinda ma ciira? Nĩ kĩĩ gĩtũmaga arĩa mamũũĩ meterere mĩthenya ta ĩyo o tũhũ?
English: “Why aren’t times laid up by the Almighty? Why don’t those who know him see his days?

Kikuyu: Kũrĩ andũ meeheragia mahiga ma mũhaka, na makarĩithia ndũũru cia mahiũ iria maiyĩte.
English: There are people who remove the landmarks. They violently take away flocks, and feed them.

Kikuyu: Moyaga ndigiri ya mwana wa ngoriai, na magakuua ndegwa ya mũtumia wa ndigwa ĩtuĩke ya kũrũgamĩrĩra thiirĩ wao.
English: They drive away the donkey of the fatherless, and they take the widow’s ox for a pledge.

Kikuyu: Nĩ meeheragia andũ arĩa abatari njĩra-inĩ, na makahatĩrĩria athĩĩni othe a bũrũri magatũma mathiĩ makehithe.
English: They turn the needy out of the way. The poor of the earth all hide themselves.

Kikuyu: O ta njagĩ cia werũ, noguo andũ arĩa athĩĩni marokagĩra wĩra wa kũhaara kĩndũ gĩa kũrĩa; kũu bũrũri ũrĩa ũtagĩaga kĩndũ nĩkuo marutaga irio cia kũhe ciana ciao.
English: Behold, as wild donkeys in the desert, they go out to their work, seeking diligently for food. The wilderness yields them bread for their children.

Kikuyu: Monganagia ngaragatha mĩgũnda-inĩ, na makahaara matigari mĩgũnda ya mĩthabibũ ya arĩa aaganu.
English: They cut their food in the field. They glean the vineyard of the wicked.

Kikuyu: Maraaraga njaga nĩ kwaga nguo; matirĩ kĩndũ gĩa kwĩhumbĩra rĩrĩa kwagĩa heho.
English: They lie all night naked without clothing, and have no covering in the cold.

Kikuyu: Maconjoragio nĩ mbura ya irĩma-inĩ, nao makenyiitĩrĩra mahiga nĩ ũndũ wa kwaga ha kwĩyũa.
English: They are wet with the showers of the mountains, and embrace the rock for lack of a shelter.

Kikuyu: Mahuragia mwana wa ngoriai kuuma nyondo-inĩ; nako gakenge ka mũthĩĩni gatahagwo nĩ ũndũ wa thiirĩ.
English: There are those who pluck the fatherless from the breast, and take a pledge of the poor,

Kikuyu: Mathiiaga njaga nĩ kwaga nguo; makuuaga itĩĩa cia ngano, no magatigwo marĩ o ahũtu.
English: so that they go around naked without clothing. Being hungry, they carry the sheaves.

Kikuyu: Mahihagĩra ndamaiyũ mĩtaro-inĩ; nĩo makinyangaga ihihĩro cia ndibei o magĩkuaga nĩ nyoota.
English: They make oil within the walls of these men. They tread wine presses, and suffer thirst.

Kikuyu: Mũcaayo wa arĩa marakua nĩũraiguuo ũkiuma itũũra inene, nayo mĩoyo ya arĩa agurarie no gũkaya ĩrakaya ĩkĩenda ũteithio. No Ngai gũtirĩ mũndũ aratuĩra ciira nĩ ũndũ wa gwĩka ũũru.
English: From out of the populous city, men groan. The soul of the wounded cries out, yet God doesn’t regard the folly.

Kikuyu: “Nĩ kũrĩ andũ arĩa mareganaga na ũtheri, na matiũĩ njĩra ciaguo, o na kana magaikara tũcĩra-inĩ twaguo.
English: “These are of those who rebel against the light. They don’t know its ways, nor stay in its paths.

Kikuyu: Hĩndĩ ĩrĩa gwatuka-rĩ, mũũragani ookagĩra akooraga athĩĩni na abatari; ningĩ ũtukũ agatuĩka ta mũici.
English: The murderer rises with the light. He kills the poor and needy. In the night he is like a thief.

Kikuyu: Riitho rĩa gĩtharia rĩetagĩrĩra kũgĩe mairia; kĩĩraga atĩrĩ, ‘Gũtirĩ riitho o na rĩmwe rĩngĩnyona,’ na gĩgaikara kĩĩhithĩte ũthiũ.
English: The eye also of the adulterer waits for the twilight, saying, ‘No eye will see me.’ He disguises his face.

Kikuyu: Rĩrĩa kũrĩ nduma-rĩ, nĩguo andũ matuaga nyũmba, no mũthenya magatinda mehingĩire; matiendaga ũndũ wa ũtheri.
English: In the dark they dig through houses. They shut themselves up in the daytime. They don’t know the light.

Kikuyu: Nĩgũkorwo andũ acio othe-rĩ, nduma ĩrĩa ndumanu nĩyo rũciinĩ rwao; magĩaga ũrata na imakania cia nduma.
English: For the morning is to all of them like thick darkness, for they know the terrors of the thick darkness.

Kikuyu: “No rĩrĩ, o nĩ mũhũũyũ ũrĩa ũrerete igũrũ rĩa maaĩ; igai rĩao bũrũri-inĩ nĩ irume, na nĩ ũndũ ũcio gũtirĩ mũndũ ũthiiaga mĩgũnda-inĩ ya mĩthabibũ.
English: “They are foam on the surface of the waters. Their portion is cursed in the earth. They don’t turn into the way of the vineyards.

Kikuyu: O ta ũrĩa riũa na ũrugarĩ iniinaga maaĩ ma tharunji-rĩ, ũguo noguo mbĩrĩra ĩhuragia arĩa mehĩtie.
English: Drought and heat consume the snow waters, so does Sheol† those who have sinned.

Kikuyu: Nayo nda ĩrĩa yamaciarire ĩkariganĩrwo nĩo, igunyũ nacio ikamarĩa; andũ arĩa aaganu maticookaga kũririkanwo, no moinangagwo ta mũtĩ.
English: The womb will forget him. The worm will feed sweetly on him. He will be no more remembered. Unrighteousness will be broken as a tree.

Kikuyu: Marĩĩaga indo cia mũtumia thaata na ũrĩa ũtarĩ kaana, na matiiguagĩra mũtumia wa ndigwa tha.
English: He devours the barren who don’t bear. He shows no kindness to the widow.

Kikuyu: No Ngai, nĩ ũndũ wa ũhoti wake, nĩakururagia arĩa marĩ hinya; o na mangĩĩhaanda wega-rĩ, matirĩ na mwĩhoko atĩ nĩmagatũũra muoyo.
English: Yet God preserves the mighty by his power. He rises up who has no assurance of life.

Kikuyu: We no ametĩkĩrie maikare mahurũkĩte makĩĩiguaga ta matarĩ na ũgwati, no maitho make nĩmacũthagĩrĩria njĩra ciao.
English: God gives them security, and they rest in it. His eyes are on their ways.

Kikuyu: Nĩgũkorwo matũũgagĩrio o kahinda kanini, magacooka makeehera; maikũrũkagio na magakua o ta andũ arĩa angĩ othe; makeeheragio o ta igira cia ngano.
English: They are exalted; yet a little while, and they are gone. Yes, they are brought low, they are taken out of the way as all others, and are cut off as the tops of the ears of grain.

Kikuyu: “Akorwo ũguo tiguo gũtariĩ-rĩ, nũũ ũngĩonania atĩ nĩndaheenania, na agĩtue ciugo ciakwa cia tũhũ?”
English: If it isn’t so now, who will prove me a liar, and make my speech worth nothing?”

Kikuyu: Nake Bilidadi ũrĩa Mũshuhi agĩcookia atĩrĩ:
English: Then Bildad the Shuhite answered,

Kikuyu: “Wathani na gwĩtigĩrwo nĩ cia Ngai; nĩwe ũhaandaga watho kũu igũrũ o igũrũ mũno.
English: “Dominion and fear are with him. He makes peace in his high places.

Kikuyu: Mbũtũ ciake no itarĩke? Nũũ ũtaaragĩrwo nĩ ũtheri wake?
English: Can his armies be counted? On whom does his light not arise?

Kikuyu: Mũndũ aakĩhota atĩa gũkorwo arĩ mũthingu mbere ya Mũrungu? Mũndũ ũciarĩtwo nĩ mũndũ-wa-nja-rĩ, akĩhota atĩa gũtuĩka mũtheru?
English: How then can man be just with God? Or how can he who is born of a woman be clean?

Kikuyu: Angĩkorwo o na mweri ti mũcangararu, na njata ti theru maitho-inĩ make-rĩ,
English: Behold, even the moon has no brightness, and the stars are not pure in his sight;

Kikuyu: mũndũ na no ta kĩgunyũ, o we mũrũ wa mũndũ-rĩ, ndakĩrĩ mũnyiihĩre mũno makĩrĩa!”
English: How much less man, who is a worm, and the son of man, who is a worm!”

Kikuyu: Ningĩ Ayubu agĩcookia atĩrĩ:
English: Then Job answered,

Kikuyu: “Kaĩ ũrĩ gũteithia ũrĩa ũtarĩ na ũhoti-ĩ! Kaĩ ũrĩ kũhonokia guoko kũrĩa gũtarĩ na hinya-ĩ!
English: “How have you helped him who is without power! How have you saved the arm that has no strength!

Kikuyu: Kaĩ ũrĩ gũtaara mũndũ ũtarĩ na ũũgĩ-ĩ! Na atĩrĩ, kaĩ nĩwonanĩtie ũmenyo mũnene-ĩ!
English: How have you counseled him who has no wisdom, and plentifully declared sound knowledge!

Kikuyu: Nũũ wagũteithia kwaria ciugo icio? Na nĩ roho waũ waria na kanua gaku?
English: To whom have you uttered words? Whose spirit came out of you?

Kikuyu: “Arĩa akuũ marĩ na ruo rũnene, o acio marĩ rungu rwa maaĩ na kĩrĩa gĩothe gĩtũũraga kuo.
English: “The departed spirits tremble, those beneath the waters and all that live in them.

Kikuyu: Gĩkuũ nĩkĩguũranie mbere ya Ngai; mwanangĩko ũikarĩte ũtarĩ mũhumbĩre.
English: Sheol† is naked before God, and Abaddon‡ has no covering.

Kikuyu: Atambũrũkagia matu ma mwena wa gathigathini igũrũ rĩa kũndũ gũtarĩ kĩndũ; nayo thĩ ndarĩ kĩndũ amĩcunjurĩtie nakĩo.
English: He stretches out the north over empty space, and hangs the earth on nothing.

Kikuyu: Athayaga maaĩ thĩinĩ wa matu make, no matu macio matingĩtembũrwo nĩ ũritũ wamo.
English: He binds up the waters in his thick clouds, and the cloud is not burst under them.

Kikuyu: Ahumbagĩra ũthiũ wa mweri rĩrĩa waiganana, agatambũrũkia matu make igũrũ rĩaguo.
English: He encloses the face of his throne, and spreads his cloud on it.

Kikuyu: Nĩekĩrĩte rũkiriri igũrũ rĩa maaĩ, rũkahakania ũtheri na nduma.
English: He has described a boundary on the surface of the waters, and to the confines of light and darkness.

Kikuyu: Itugĩ iria itiirĩrĩire igũrũ nĩ ithingithaga, ikagegearaga nĩ ũndũ wa ikũũmana rĩake.
English: The pillars of heaven tremble and are astonished at his rebuke.

Kikuyu: Nĩoirugire maaĩ ma iria na ũndũ wa hinya wake; na nĩ ũndũ wa ũũgĩ wake nĩatinaangirie Rahabu tũcunjĩ.
English: He stirs up the sea with his power, and by his understanding he strikes through Rahab.

Kikuyu: Mĩhũmũ yake nĩyo yathakaririe igũrũ; guoko gwake nĩ gwatheecire nyoka ĩrĩa ĩnyororokaga na ihenya.
English: By his Spirit the heavens are garnished. His hand has pierced the swift serpent.

Kikuyu: Atĩrĩrĩ, ĩno no mĩthia ya mawĩra make; kaĩ no kamũheehũ kanini tũiguaga ka ũhoro wake-ĩ! Nũũ ũngĩgĩtaũkĩrwo nĩ marurumĩ ma ũhoti wake?”
English: Behold, these are but the outskirts of his ways. How small a whisper do we hear of him! But the thunder of his power who can understand?”

Kikuyu: Nake Ayubu agĩthiĩ na mbere na mĩario yake, akiuga atĩrĩ:
English: Job again took up his parable, and said,

Kikuyu: “Ti-itherũ o ta ũrĩa Mũrungu atũũraga muoyo, o we ũnyimĩte kĩhooto, ũcio Mwene-Hinya-Wothe, ũrĩa ũtũmĩte ngĩe na ũrũrũ ngoro-inĩ-rĩ,
English: “As God lives, who has taken away my right, the Almighty, who has made my soul bitter

Kikuyu: hĩndĩ ĩrĩa yothe niĩ ngũtũũra muoyo, nayo mĩhũmũ ya Ngai ĩrĩ maniũrũ-inĩ makwa,
English: (for the length of my life is still in me, and the spirit of God is in my nostrils);

Kikuyu: mĩromo yakwa ndĩkaaria maũndũ ma waganu, na rũrĩmĩ rwakwa rũtikaaria maheeni.
English: surely my lips will not speak unrighteousness, neither will my tongue utter deceit.

Kikuyu: Niĩ ndigetĩkĩra atĩ nĩ inyuĩ mũrĩ na kĩhooto; nginya rĩrĩa ngaakua, ndigakaana ũkindĩrĩku wakwa.
English: Far be it from me that I should justify you. Until I die I will not put away my integrity from me.

Kikuyu: Nĩngũtũũria ũthingu wakwa na ndikaũrekia; thamiri yakwa ndĩkanjiirithia rĩrĩa rĩothe ngũtũũra muoyo.
English: I hold fast to my righteousness, and will not let it go. My heart will not reproach me so long as I live.

Kikuyu: “Thũ ciakwa irogĩtuĩka ta arĩa aaganu, arĩa marĩ muku na niĩ marotuĩka ta arĩa matarĩ kĩhooto!
English: “Let my enemy be as the wicked. Let him who rises up against me be as the unrighteous.

Kikuyu: Tondũ-rĩ, kĩĩrĩgĩrĩro kĩa ũrĩa ũtarĩ mwĩtigĩri Ngai gĩkĩrĩ kĩrĩkũ akua, hĩndĩ ĩrĩa Ngai ooya muoyo wake?
English: For what is the hope of the godless, when he is cut off, when God takes away his life?

Kikuyu: Mũrungu nĩakĩiguaga gũkaya gwake rĩrĩa akorwo nĩ mĩnyamaro?
English: Will God hear his cry when trouble comes on him?

Kikuyu: Nĩakenagĩra ũcio Mwene-Hinya-Wothe? Nĩakayagĩra Ngai mahinda mothe?
English: Will he delight himself in the Almighty, and call on God at all times?

Kikuyu: “Nĩngũmũruta ũhoro wĩgiĩ ũhoti wa Mũrungu; ndikũhitha njĩra cia Mwene-Hinya-Wothe.
English: I will teach you about the hand of God. I will not conceal that which is with the Almighty.

Kikuyu: Inyuothe nĩmwĩoneire maũndũ macio. Ĩkĩrĩ yakĩ mĩario ĩno ĩtarĩ kĩene?
English: Behold, all of you have seen it yourselves; why then have you become altogether vain?

Kikuyu: “Ũũ nĩguo Mũrungu aathagĩrĩria arĩa aaganu, na nĩrĩo igai rĩrĩa mũndũ ũrĩa ũtarĩ tha aamũkagĩra kuuma kũrĩ Mwene-Hinya-Wothe:
English: “This is the portion of a wicked man with God, the heritage of oppressors, which they receive from the Almighty.

Kikuyu: O na ciana ciake ciaingĩha atĩa, ciathĩrĩirio rũhiũ rwa njora; rũciaro rwake rũtikoona irio cia kũrũigana.
English: If his children are multiplied, it is for the sword. His offspring will not be satisfied with bread.

Kikuyu: Mũthiro nĩguo ũkaaninũkia arĩa agaatiga thuutha wake, na atumia ao a ndigwa matikamarĩrĩra.
English: Those who remain of him will be buried in death. His widows will make no lamentation.

Kikuyu: O na angĩonganĩrĩria betha ta rũkũngũ, na agĩe na nguo nyingĩ ta hĩba cia rĩũmba,
English: Though he heap up silver as the dust, and prepare clothing as the clay;

Kikuyu: kĩrĩa egũcookanĩrĩria gĩkehumbwo nĩ ũrĩa mũthingu, na arĩa matarĩ mahĩtia nĩo makaagayana betha yake.
English: he may prepare it, but the just will put it on, and the innocent will divide the silver.

Kikuyu: Nyũmba ĩrĩa aakaga no ta nyũmba ya kĩĩhuruta, ningĩ no ta gĩthũnũ gĩakĩtwo nĩ mũrangĩri.
English: He builds his house as the moth, as a booth which the watchman makes.

Kikuyu: Agaakoma arĩ mũtongu, no ndagacooka gwĩka ũguo rĩngĩ; akaahingũra maitho akore gũtirĩ kĩndũ arĩ nakĩo.
English: He lies down rich, but he will not do so again. He opens his eyes, and he is not.

Kikuyu: Imakania imũkoragĩrĩra ta mũiyũro wa maaĩ; kĩhuhũkanio gĩkaamũhuria ũtukũ.
English: Terrors overtake him like waters. A storm steals him away in the night.

Kikuyu: Rũhuho rwa mwena wa Irathĩro rũmuoyaga akabuĩria; rũmweheragia kũrĩa atũũraga.
English: The east wind carries him away, and he departs. It sweeps him out of his place.

Kikuyu: Rũmũhurutaga rũtarĩ na tha o rĩrĩa aroorĩra hinya waruo.
English: For it hurls at him, and does not spare, as he flees away from his hand.

Kikuyu: Rũhũũraga hĩ rũkamũkenerera, na rũkagamba ta nyoka rũkamũruta kũrĩa atũũraga.”
English: Men will clap their hands at him, and will hiss him out of his place.

Kikuyu: “Nĩ kũrĩ handũ harĩa betha yenjagwo o na nĩ harĩ handũ harĩa thahabu ĩtheragĩrio.
English: “Surely there is a mine for silver, and a place for gold which they refine.

Kikuyu: Kĩgera kĩrutagwo kuuma tĩĩri-inĩ, nakĩo gĩcango kĩrutagwo mahiga-inĩ gĩgatwekio.
English: Iron is taken out of the earth, and copper is smelted out of the ore.

Kikuyu: Mũndũ nĩkũniina aniinaga nduma; acaragia mahiga macio nginya kũrĩa kũriku mũno, o kũu nduma ĩrĩ ndumanu mũno.
English: Man sets an end to darkness, and searches out, to the furthest bound, the stones of obscurity and of thick darkness.

Kikuyu: Mũndũ atũrĩkagia irima thĩ kũraya na kũrĩa andũ matũũraga, agakinya kũndũ kũrĩa mũndũ aariganĩirwo nĩgũthiiaga; kũu kũraihanĩrĩirie na andũ nĩkuo acunjuuraga akĩereeraga.*
English: He breaks open a shaft away from where people live. They are forgotten by the foot. They hang far from men, they swing back and forth.

Kikuyu: Thĩ nĩkuo kuumaga irio, no na kũu thĩinĩ mũhuro kũgarũrũkĩte gũkahaana ta gũcinĩtwo na mwaki;
English: As for the earth, out of it comes bread. Underneath it is turned up as it were by fire.

Kikuyu: mahiga-inĩ ma thĩ nĩkuo kuumaga yakuti ĩrĩa ya bururu, na mũthanga wayo ũkoragwo na ngũmba cia thahabu.
English: Sapphires come from its rocks. It has dust of gold.

Kikuyu: Gũtirĩ nyoni ndĩa-nyama yũĩ gacĩra kau kahithe, na gatirĩ konwo nĩ riitho rĩa hũngũ.
English: That path no bird of prey knows, neither has the falcon’s eye seen it.

Kikuyu: Nyamũ iria ciĩtĩĩaga itirĩ ciagathiĩra, o na gũtirĩ mũrũũthi ũkageragĩra.
English: The proud animals have not trodden it, nor has the fierce lion passed by there.

Kikuyu: Guoko kwa mũndũ gũtharĩkagĩra gũkanyiita ihiga rĩa nyaigĩ, na gũkaguũria itina cia irĩma.
English: He puts his hand on the flinty rock, and he overturns the mountains by the roots.

Kikuyu: Enjaga mungu ũgatũrĩkia rwaro rwa ihiga; maitho make makĩonaga igĩĩna ciaruo ciothe.
English: He cuts out channels among the rocks. His eye sees every precious thing.

Kikuyu: Ethaga itwe cia njũũĩ, na indo iria hithe agaciumĩria ũtheri-inĩ.
English: He binds the streams that they don’t trickle. The thing that is hidden he brings out to light.

Kikuyu: “No ũũgĩ-rĩ, ũngĩoneka kũ? Ũmenyo ũtũũraga kũ?
English: “But where will wisdom be found? Where is the place of understanding?

Kikuyu: Mũndũ ndangĩmenya thogora wa ũũgĩ; ndũngĩoneka bũrũri wa arĩa marĩ muoyo.
English: Man doesn’t know its price, and it isn’t found in the land of the living.

Kikuyu: Kũrĩa kũriku mũno kuugaga atĩrĩ, ‘Ndũrĩ thĩinĩ wakwa’; narĩo iria rĩkoiga atĩrĩ, ‘Ndũrĩ gũkũ gwakwa.’
English: The deep says, ‘It isn’t in me.’ The sea says, ‘It isn’t with me.’

Kikuyu: Ndũngĩgũrĩka na thahabu ĩrĩa therie mũno, kana thogora waguo ũthimwo na betha.
English: It can’t be gotten for gold, neither will silver be weighed for its price.

Kikuyu: Ndũngĩgũrĩka na thahabu ya Ofiri, kana ũgũrĩke na onigithi ĩrĩa ĩrĩ goro mũno, o na kana yakuti ĩrĩa ya bururu.
English: It can’t be valued with the gold of Ophir, with the precious onyx, or the sapphire.†

Kikuyu: Thahabu kana icicio-rĩ, itingĩhota kũgerekanio naguo; o na kana ũkũũranio na mathaga ma thahabu.
English: Gold and glass can’t equal it, neither will it be exchanged for jewels of fine gold.

Kikuyu: Maricani kana ngenyekenyi iria cia goro itiagĩrĩire kũgwetanio naguo; thogora wa ũũgĩ ũkĩrĩte wa ruru ĩrĩa ndune.
English: No mention will be made of coral or of crystal. Yes, the price of wisdom is above rubies.

Kikuyu: Yakuti ya Kushi ndĩngĩigananio naguo; o na ndũngĩgũrĩka na thahabu ĩrĩa therie mũno.
English: The topaz of Ethiopia will not equal it. It won’t be valued with pure gold.

Kikuyu: “Hakĩrĩ ũguo-rĩ, ũũgĩ ũngĩkiuma nakũ? Ũmenyo ũtũũraga kũ?
English: Where then does wisdom come from? Where is the place of understanding?

Kikuyu: Nĩmũhithe kũrĩ maitho ma ciũmbe ciothe iria itũũraga muoyo, ũkahithwo o na nyoni cia rĩera-inĩ.
English: Seeing it is hidden from the eyes of all living, and kept close from the birds of the sky.

Kikuyu: Mwanangĩko na gĩkuũ ciugaga atĩrĩ, ‘No mũhuhu waguo ũkinyĩte matũ-inĩ maitũ.’
English: Destruction and Death say, ‘We have heard a rumor of it with our ears.’

Kikuyu: Ngai nĩooĩ njĩra ya gũthiĩ kũrĩa ũrĩ, na nowe wiki ũũĩ kũrĩa ũtũũraga,
English: “God understands its way, and he knows its place.

Kikuyu: nĩgũkorwo nĩonaga mũthia wa thĩ, na nĩonaga maũndũ marĩa mothe marĩ rungu rwa igũrũ.
English: For he looks to the ends of the earth, and sees under the whole sky.

Kikuyu: Rĩrĩa aathimĩire rũhuho nditi yaruo, o na agĩthima maaĩ-rĩ,
English: He establishes the force of the wind. Yes, he measures out the waters by measure.

Kikuyu: rĩrĩa aarutĩire mbura watho ĩrũmagĩrĩre, na agĩtemera rũheni na marurumĩ njĩra-rĩ,
English: When he made a decree for the rain, and a way for the lightning of the thunder,

Kikuyu: nake nĩonire ũũgĩ na akĩũthima; aũrũmirie na akĩũthuthuuria.
English: then he saw it, and declared it. He established it, yes, and searched it out.

Kikuyu: Agĩcooka akĩĩra andũ atĩrĩ, ‘Gwĩtigĩra Mwathani-rĩ, ũcio nĩguo ũũgĩ, Nakuo gũtheemaga ũũru nĩ ũmenyo.’ ”
English: To man he said, ‘Behold, the fear of the Lord,‡ that is wisdom. To depart from evil is understanding.’ ”

Kikuyu: Ningĩ Ayubu nĩathiire na mbere kwaria, akiuga atĩrĩ:
English: Job again took up his parable, and said,

Kikuyu: “Naarĩ korwo no haane ũrĩa ndaatariĩ mĩeri ĩrĩa ya tene, matukũ-inĩ marĩa Ngai aamenyagĩrĩra,
English: “Oh that I were as in the months of old, as in the days when God watched over me;

Kikuyu: rĩrĩa tawa wake wamũrĩkaga igũrũ rĩa mũtwe wakwa, na ũndũ wa ũtheri wake ngatuĩkanagĩria nduma-inĩ!
English: when his lamp shone on my head, and by his light I walked through darkness,

Kikuyu: Korwo ndariĩ ũrĩa ndatariĩ matukũ-inĩ marĩa ndagaacĩire biũ, hĩndĩ ĩrĩa kuumĩrania ngoro na Ngai kwarathimaga nyũmba yakwa,
English: as I was in my prime, when the friendship of God was in my tent,

Kikuyu: rĩrĩa Mwene-Hinya-Wothe aarĩ hamwe na niĩ, nacio ciana ciakwa ikandigiicĩria,
English: when the Almighty was yet with me, and my children were around me,

Kikuyu: rĩrĩa gacĩra gakwa kaihũgĩtio nĩ kĩrimũ kĩa iria, naruo rwaro rwa ihiga rũgaatherũkagĩra tũrũũĩ twa maguta ma mũtamaiyũ!
English: when my steps were washed with butter, and the rock poured out streams of oil for me,

Kikuyu: “Rĩrĩa ndaathiiaga kĩhingo-inĩ kĩa itũũra inene, na ngaikarĩra gĩtĩ gĩakwa hau kĩaraho-inĩ-rĩ,
English: when I went out to the city gate, when I prepared my seat in the street.

Kikuyu: aanake maanyonaga makeehera, nao athuuri makarũgama,
English: The young men saw me and hid themselves. The aged rose up and stood.

Kikuyu: andũ arĩa anene maatigaga kwaria, makahumbĩra tũnua twao na moko;
English: The princes refrained from talking, and laid their hand on their mouth.

Kikuyu: mĩgambo ya andũ arĩa marĩ igweta ĩgakirio, nacio nĩmĩ ciao ikanyiitana na karakara.
English: The voice of the nobles was hushed, and their tongue stuck to the roof of their mouth.

Kikuyu: Ũrĩa wothe wanjiguaga ngĩaria aaragia wega igũrũ rĩakwa, nao arĩa maanyonaga makangaathĩrĩria,
English: For when the ear heard me, then it blessed me, and when the eye saw me, it commended me,

Kikuyu: nĩ ũndũ nĩndahatũraga arĩa athĩĩni maakaya mateithio, o na arĩa mataarĩ na maithe maagĩte mũndũ wa kũmateithia.
English: because I delivered the poor who cried, and the fatherless also, who had no one to help him,

Kikuyu: Mũndũ agĩkua nĩandaathimaga; nĩndatũmaga ngoro ya mũtumia wa ndigwa ĩine.
English: the blessing of him who was ready to perish came on me, and I caused the widow’s heart to sing for joy.

Kikuyu: Ndehumbaga ũthingu ta nguo; ciira wa kĩhooto nĩguo warĩ nguo yakwa ya igũrũ, o na kĩremba gĩakwa.
English: I put on righteousness, and it clothed me. My justice was as a robe and a diadem.

Kikuyu: Nĩ niĩ ndaarĩ maitho ma arĩa atumumu, na magũrũ ma arĩa ithua.
English: I was eyes to the blind, and feet to the lame.

Kikuyu: Ndaarĩ ithe wa arĩa abatari; nĩndaciiragĩrĩra o na mũndũ itooĩ.
English: I was a father to the needy. I researched the cause of him whom I didn’t know.

Kikuyu: Ningĩ nĩndoinangaga magego ma arĩa aaganu, na ngahuria arĩa maarĩ magego-inĩ mao.
English: I broke the jaws of the unrighteous and plucked the prey out of his teeth.

Kikuyu: “Ndeciiragia atĩrĩ, ‘Niĩ ngaakuĩra gwakwa nyũmba, matukũ makwa marĩ maingĩ ta mũthanga.
English: Then I said, ‘I will die in my own house, I will count my days as the sand.

Kikuyu: Mĩri yakwa ĩgataamba ĩkinye maaĩ-inĩ, narĩo ireera rĩkoragwo honge-inĩ ciakwa ũtukũ wothe.
English: My root is spread out to the waters. The dew lies all night on my branch.

Kikuyu: Riiri wakwa ũgũtũũra werũhagio thĩinĩ wakwa, naguo ũta wakwa ũtũũre ũrĩ mwerũ guoko-inĩ gwakwa.’
English: My glory is fresh in me. My bow is renewed in my hand.’

Kikuyu: “Andũ maathikagĩrĩria marĩ na kĩĩrĩgĩrĩro, meetagĩrĩra kĩrĩra gĩakwa makirĩte.
English: “Men listened to me, waited, and kept silence for my counsel.

Kikuyu: Ndaarĩkia kwaria-rĩ, matiacookaga kwaria; ciugo ciakwa ciatoonyaga matũ mao kahora ihooreire.
English: After my words they didn’t speak again. My speech fell on them.

Kikuyu: Maanjetagĩrĩra ta andũ metereire mbura, na makanyua ciugo ciakwa o ta mbura ĩrĩa ya kũrigĩrĩria.
English: They waited for me as for the rain. Their mouths drank as with the spring rain.

Kikuyu: Ndaamathekathekagia moorĩtwo nĩ hinya makaaga gwĩtĩkia; ũtheri wa ũthiũ wakwa warĩ wa bata mũno kũrĩ o.
English: I smiled on them when they had no confidence. They didn’t reject the light of my face.

Kikuyu: Nĩ niĩ ndamoonagia njĩra, ngaikaraga ta ndĩ mũnene wao; ndatũũraga ta mũthamaki arĩ gatagatĩ ga ita rĩake; ningĩ ndaatariĩ ta mũndũ ũrĩa ũhooragĩria arĩa maracakaya.
English: I chose out their way, and sat as chief. I lived as a king in the army, as one who comforts the mourners.

Kikuyu: “No rĩu-rĩ, andũ ethĩ kũngĩra nĩmaanyũrũragia, arĩa o na itangĩendire gũturanĩra maithe mao na ngui ciakwa cia rũũru.
English: “But now those who are younger than I have me in derision, whose fathers I considered unworthy to put with my sheep dogs.

Kikuyu: Hinya wa moko mao ũngĩangʼunire nakĩ, kuona atĩ hinya wao nĩwamehereire?
English: Of what use is the strength of their hands to me, men in whom ripe age has perished?

Kikuyu: Nĩmathĩnĩkĩte nĩ ũndũ wa wagi na ngʼaragu, ũtukũ-rĩ, moorũũraga bũrũri mũngʼaru, bũrũri mwanangĩku ũkirĩte ihooru.
English: They are gaunt from lack and famine. They gnaw the dry ground, in the gloom of waste and desolation.

Kikuyu: Maahaaraga nyeni cia mahuti ma cumbĩ kuuma ihinga-inĩ, na irio ciao ciarĩ mĩri ya mũtĩ wa kĩhaato.
English: They pluck salt herbs by the bushes. The roots of the broom tree are their food.

Kikuyu: Nĩmaingatirwo kuuma kũrĩ mũingĩ, makiugĩrĩrio ta maarĩ aici.
English: They are driven out from among men. They cry after them as after a thief,

Kikuyu: Nĩmahatĩrĩirio maikarage mĩkuru-inĩ ya tũrũũĩ tũhũu, kũu ndwaro-inĩ cia mahiga na marima-inĩ marĩa marĩ thĩ.
English: so that they live in frightful valleys, and in holes of the earth and of the rocks.

Kikuyu: Maanagia ta nyamũ kũu ihinga-inĩ, makahatĩkanagĩra kũu mahuti-inĩ.
English: They bray among the bushes. They are gathered together under the nettles.

Kikuyu: Rũciaro rũtarĩ kĩene na rũtarĩ rĩĩtwa, nĩ rwarutũrũrirwo ruume kũu bũrũri-inĩ.
English: They are children of fools, yes, children of wicked men. They were flogged out of the land.

Kikuyu: “Na rĩu ariũ ao maraanyũrũria na rwĩmbo; ngagĩtuĩka wa kuunagwo thimo nĩo.
English: “Now I have become their song. Yes, I am a byword to them.

Kikuyu: Nĩmathũire na magaikaraga haraihu na niĩ; matiĩtigagĩra kũnduĩra mata ũthiũ.
English: They abhor me, they stand aloof from me, and don’t hesitate to spit in my face.

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ rĩu Ngai nĩaregeretie ũta wakwa, na akandeehera mathĩĩna-rĩ, matirĩ ũndũ merigagĩrĩria gwĩka marĩ harĩa ndĩ.
English: For he has untied his cord, and afflicted me; and they have thrown off restraint before me.

Kikuyu: Mwena wakwa wa ũrĩo kũrĩ rũrĩrĩ rũratharĩkĩra; maigagĩra magũrũ makwa mĩtego, na magaaka ihumbu ciao cia gũũtharĩkĩra.
English: On my right hand rise the rabble. They thrust aside my feet. They cast their ways of destruction up against me.

Kikuyu: Maharaganagia njĩra yakwa; mahotaga kũnyũnũha o na gũtarĩ na mũndũ ũramateithia.
English: They mar my path. They promote my destruction without anyone’s help.

Kikuyu: Mokĩte ta matoonyeire mwanya-inĩ mwariĩ; mokĩire gatagatĩ ga kũu kwanangĩku, makaamomokera.
English: As through a wide breach they come. They roll themselves in amid the ruin.

Kikuyu: Imakania nĩcihootete; gĩtĩĩo gĩakwa kĩũmbũrĩtwo ta kĩhurutĩtwo nĩ rũhuho, naguo ũgitĩri wakwa ũkabuĩria ta itu.
English: Terrors have turned on me. They chase my honor as the wind. My welfare has passed away as a cloud.

Kikuyu: “Na rĩu muoyo wakwa nĩũrathirĩrĩkĩra; matukũ ma thĩĩna nĩmanyiitĩte.
English: “Now my soul is poured out within me. Days of affliction have taken hold of me.

Kikuyu: Ũtukũ ũtheecangaga mahĩndĩ makwa; ruo rwa gũthegenya rũtindigithagĩria.
English: In the night season my bones are pierced in me, and the pains that gnaw me take no rest.

Kikuyu: Ngai angũnjakũnjaga ta nguo na ũndũ wa ũhoti wake mũnene; aanyiitaga ta kanjũ yakwa ngingo-inĩ.
English: My garment is disfigured by great force. It binds me about as the collar of my tunic.

Kikuyu: Anjikĩtie ndoro-inĩ, ngatuĩka ta rũkũngũ na ta mũhu.
English: He has cast me into the mire. I have become like dust and ashes.

Kikuyu: “Nĩwe ndĩrakaĩra, o Wee Ngai, no ndũranjĩtĩka; ndĩrarũgama, no wee no kũndora ũrandora.
English: I cry to you, and you do not answer me. I stand up, and you gaze at me.

Kikuyu: Wee nĩũngarũrũkĩte ũtarĩ na tha; ũtharĩkĩire na hinya wa guoko gwaku.
English: You have turned to be cruel to me. With the might of your hand you persecute me.

Kikuyu: Nĩũũhurĩtie, ũkaandindĩka mbere ya rũhuho; ũũnyugutanĩtie kĩhuhũkanio-inĩ.
English: You lift me up to the wind, and drive me with it. You dissolve me in the storm.

Kikuyu: Nĩnjũũĩ nĩũkanginyia o gĩkuũ-inĩ, ũndware kũrĩa gwathĩrĩirwo arĩa othe marĩ muoyo.
English: For I know that you will bring me to death, to the house appointed for all living.

Kikuyu: “Ti-itherũ gũtirĩ mũndũ ũũkagĩrĩra mũndũ ũthuthĩkĩte ngoro, hĩndĩ ĩrĩa egũkaya ateithio arĩ mĩnyamaro-inĩ.
English: “However doesn’t one stretch out a hand in his fall? Or in his calamity therefore cry for help?

Kikuyu: Niĩ-rĩ, githĩ ndianarĩrio nĩ arĩa marĩ na thĩĩna? Githĩ ngoro yakwa ndĩanaiguĩra arĩa athĩĩni kĩeha?
English: Didn’t I weep for him who was in trouble? Wasn’t my soul grieved for the needy?

Kikuyu: No rĩrĩ, rĩrĩa ndeerĩgagĩrĩra wega, ũũru ũgĩũka; rĩrĩa ndaacaragia ũtheri-rĩ, hĩndĩ ĩyo nduma ĩgĩũka.
English: When I looked for good, then evil came. When I waited for light, darkness came.

Kikuyu: Nda yakwa ndĩtigaga kũruruma; matukũ ma thĩĩna nĩmanginyĩire.
English: My heart is troubled, and doesn’t rest. Days of affliction have come on me.

Kikuyu: Thiiaga njirĩte biũ, no ti ũndũ wa kũhĩa nĩ riũa; ngarũgama kĩũngano-inĩ ngakaya ndeithio.
English: I go mourning without the sun. I stand up in the assembly, and cry for help.

Kikuyu: Nduĩkĩte mũrũ wa nyina na mbwe, ngatuĩka mũthiritũ wa ndundu.
English: I am a brother to jackals, and a companion to ostriches.

Kikuyu: Gĩkonde gĩakwa nĩkĩgarũrũkĩte, gĩgathita na gĩkoonũka; mwĩrĩ wakwa ũhiũhĩte nĩ ũrugarĩ.
English: My skin grows black and peels from me. My bones are burned with heat.

Kikuyu: Kĩnanda gĩakwa kĩa mũgeeto kĩrutaga o mũgambo wa gũcakaya, naguo mũtũrirũ wakwa ũkaruta o mũgambo wa kĩrĩro.
English: Therefore my harp has turned to mourning, and my pipe into the voice of those who weep.

Kikuyu: “Niĩ nĩtwarĩĩkanĩire na maitho makwa ndikanarore mũirĩtu ndĩmwĩrirĩrie.
English: “I made a covenant with my eyes; how then should I look lustfully at a young woman?

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ-rĩ, kaĩ rũgai rwa mũndũ kuuma igũrũ kwa Ngai rũkĩrĩ kĩĩ? Igai rĩake nĩ rĩrĩkũ kuuma kũrĩ ũcio Mwene-Hinya-Wothe ũrĩ igũrũ?
English: For what is the portion from God above, and the heritage from the Almighty on high?

Kikuyu: Githĩ ti kwanangwo kwa arĩa aaganu, na mũtino kũrĩ arĩa meekaga maũndũ mooru?
English: Is it not calamity to the unrighteous, and disaster to the workers of iniquity?

Kikuyu: Githĩ we ndonaga njĩra ciakwa, na agatara o ikinya o ikinya rĩakwa?
English: Doesn’t he see my ways, and count all my steps?

Kikuyu: “Ingĩkorwo thiiaga na njĩra itarĩ cia ma-rĩ, kana kũgũrũ gwakwa gũkahiũha thiĩ ngaheenanie-rĩ,
English: “If I have walked with falsehood, and my foot has hurried to deceit

Kikuyu: Ngai nĩathime na ratiri cia kĩhooto, nake nĩekũmenya atĩ niĩ ndirĩ ũcuuke;
English: (let me be weighed in an even balance, that God may know my integrity);

Kikuyu: makinya makwa mangĩkorwo nĩmahũkĩte makoima njĩra-inĩ, nayo ngoro yakwa ĩngĩkorwo nĩĩtongoretio nĩ maitho makwa, kana moko makwa makorwo nĩmathaahĩtio-rĩ,
English: if my step has turned out of the way, if my heart walked after my eyes, if any defilement has stuck to my hands,

Kikuyu: hĩndĩ ĩyo kĩrĩa haandĩte kĩrorĩĩo nĩ andũ angĩ, nacio irio cia mĩgũnda yakwa iromunywo.
English: then let me sow, and let another eat. Yes, let the produce of my field be rooted out.

Kikuyu: “Ngoro yakwa ĩngĩkorwo yanaheenererio nĩ mũndũ-wa-nja, kana ngorwo ndanaceema mũrango-inĩ wa mũndũ wa itũũra,
English: “If my heart has been enticed to a woman, and I have laid wait at my neighbor’s door,

Kikuyu: hĩndĩ ĩyo mũtumia wakwa arothĩa ngano ya mũndũ ũngĩ, na arũme angĩ tiga niĩ marokoma nake.
English: then let my wife grind for another, and let others sleep with her.

Kikuyu: Nĩgũkorwo ũndũ ũcio nĩ ũmaramari wa thoni, na nĩ rĩĩhia rĩa gũtuĩrwo ciira nĩ kĩama.
English: For that would be a heinous crime. Yes, it would be an iniquity to be punished by the judges,

Kikuyu: Tondũ ũcio nĩ mwaki ũrĩa ũcinaga nginya ũkaananga; na nĩũngĩamunyĩte magetha makwa mothe.
English: for it is a fire that consumes to destruction, and would root out all my increase.

Kikuyu: “Ingĩkorwo nĩnyimĩte ndungata ciakwa cia arũme na cia andũ-a-nja kĩhooto rĩrĩa manateta nĩ ũndũ wakwa-rĩ,
English: “If I have despised the cause of my male servant or of my female servant, when they contended with me,

Kikuyu: niĩ ngeeka atĩa rĩrĩa Mũrungu akaanjũkĩrĩra? Ngaacookia atĩa rĩrĩa ngeetwo ndĩĩtetere ũhoro-inĩ ũcio?
English: what then will I do when God rises up? When he visits, what will I answer him?

Kikuyu: Githĩ ũcio wanyũũmbire kũu nda ya maitũ to we wamoombire? Githĩ tiwe watũthondekire tũrĩ kũu nda cia aa maitũ?
English: Didn’t he who made me in the womb make him? Didn’t one fashion us in the womb?

Kikuyu: “Ingĩkorwo ndanaima athĩĩni kĩrĩa maanerirĩria, kana ngareka maitho ma mũtũmia wa ndigwa morwo nĩ hinya-rĩ,
English: “If I have withheld the poor from their desire, or have caused the eyes of the widow to fail,

Kikuyu: ingĩkorwo ndĩĩaga irio ciakwa nyiki, ngaaga kũgayana na ũrĩa ũtarĩ ithe-rĩ,
English: or have eaten my morsel alone, and the fatherless has not eaten of it

Kikuyu: (no niĩ kuuma ũnini wakwa, mwana ta ũcio ndaamũreraga o ta ũrĩa angĩarerirwo nĩ ithe, na kuuma gũciarwo gwakwa ndũire ndongoragia mũtumia wa ndigwa)
English: (no, from my youth he grew up with me as with a father, I have guided her from my mother’s womb);

Kikuyu: ingĩkorwo ndanoona mũndũ agĩkua nĩ ũndũ wa kwaga nguo, kana ngoona mũndũ mũbatari atarĩ kĩndũ gĩa kwĩhumba,
English: if I have seen any perish for want of clothing, or that the needy had no covering;

Kikuyu: na ngoro yake ndĩandathimire nĩ ũndũ wa kũmũiguithia ũrugarĩ na guoya wa ngʼondu ciakwa-rĩ,
English: if his heart hasn’t blessed me, if he hasn’t been warmed with my sheep’s fleece;

Kikuyu: ingĩkorwo ndanoya guoko gwakwa ngookĩrĩra mwana ũtarĩ ithe, nĩkũmenya atĩ no nyone wa kũndeithia kwagĩa ciira igooti-inĩ-rĩ,
English: if I have lifted up my hand against the fatherless, because I saw my help in the gate;

Kikuyu: hĩndĩ ĩyo guoko gwakwa kũroahũkĩra kĩande-inĩ kũgwe, kũroinĩkĩra o irũngo-inĩ.
English: then let my shoulder fall from the shoulder blade, and my arm be broken from the bone.

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ nĩndetigagĩra mwanangĩko uumĩte kũrĩ Mũrungu, na nĩ ũndũ wa gwĩtigĩra riiri wake, ndingĩekire maũndũ ta macio.
English: For calamity from God is a terror to me. Because of his majesty, I can do nothing.

Kikuyu: “Ingĩkorwo nĩnjigĩte mwĩhoko wakwa harĩ thahabu, kana ngeera thahabu ĩrĩa therie mũno atĩrĩ, ‘Wee nĩwe ũgitĩri wakwa,’
English: “If I have made gold my hope, and have said to the fine gold, ‘You are my confidence;’

Kikuyu: ingĩkorwo ndanakenera ũtonga wakwa mũnene, kana ngakenera uumithio ũrĩa moko makwa mecarĩirie-rĩ,
English: If I have rejoiced because my wealth was great, and because my hand had gotten much;

Kikuyu: ingĩkorwo ndanarũmbũiya riũa rĩarĩte, kana mweri ũgĩthiĩ ũcangararĩte,
English: if I have seen the sun when it shined, or the moon moving in splendor,

Kikuyu: na ngoro yakwa ĩkĩheenererio nĩcio na hitho, kana guoko gwakwa gũgĩcikinyĩria kĩmumunyano gĩa gũcitĩĩa-rĩ,
English: and my heart has been secretly enticed, and my hand threw a kiss from my mouth;

Kikuyu: o na macio mangĩtuĩka mehia ma gũtuĩrwo ciira, nĩgũkorwo ingĩtuĩkĩte mũndũ ũtarĩ mwĩhokeku harĩ Mũrungu ũrĩa ũrĩ igũrũ.
English: this also would be an iniquity to be punished by the judges, for I would have denied the God who is above.

Kikuyu: “Ingĩkorwo ndaanakena nĩ thũ yakwa kuona mũtino, kana ngĩmĩthekerera rĩrĩa thĩĩna wamĩkora,
English: “If I have rejoiced at the destruction of him who hated me, or lifted up myself when evil found him

Kikuyu: no niĩ ndirĩ ndetĩkĩra kanua gakwa keehie na ũndũ wa kũhoera muoyo wayo kĩrumi,
English: (I have certainly not allowed my mouth to sin by asking his life with a curse);

Kikuyu: kũngĩkorwo andũ a nyũmba yakwa matirĩ moiga atĩrĩ, ‘Nũũ ũtarĩ warĩa nyama cia Ayubu akahũũna?’
English: if the men of my tent have not said, ‘Who can find one who has not been filled with his meat?’

Kikuyu: no gũtirĩ mũgeni wanaraara njĩra-inĩ, nĩ ũndũ mũrango wa mũciĩ wakwa ũtũire ũhingũrĩirwo mũgendi,
English: (the foreigner has not camped in the street, but I have opened my doors to the traveler);

Kikuyu: ingĩkorwo ndaanahitha mehia makwa, ta ũrĩa andũ meekaga, na ũndũ wa kũhitha mahĩtia ngoro-inĩ yakwa
English: if like Adam I have covered my transgressions, by hiding my iniquity in my heart,

Kikuyu: tondũ wa gwĩtigĩra kĩrĩndĩ, o na gwĩtigĩra kũmenwo nĩ mĩhĩrĩga ngagĩkira ki na ndiume nja-rĩ,
English: because I feared the great multitude, and the contempt of families terrified me, so that I kept silence, and didn’t go out of the door—

Kikuyu: (“Naarĩ korwo ndaarĩ na mũndũ wa kũnjigua! Rĩu nĩndekĩra rũũri rwa kwĩyarĩrĩria: reke Mwene-Hinya-Wothe anjookerie ũhoro; reke mũũthitangi andĩke marũa ma thitango yake.
English: oh that I had one to hear me! Behold, here is my signature! Let the Almighty answer me! Let the accuser write my indictment!

Kikuyu: Ti-itherũ marũa macio ingĩmaigĩrĩra kĩande, ndĩmehumbe taarĩ thũmbĩ.
English: Surely I would carry it on my shoulder, and I would bind it to me as a crown.

Kikuyu: Njooke ndĩmũhe ũhoro wakwa ikinya gwa ikinya; ndĩmũkuhĩrĩrie ta ndĩ mũnene.)
English: I would declare to him the number of my steps. I would go near to him like a prince.

Kikuyu: “Korwo mũgũnda wakwa wakaya, ũnjũkĩrĩre, nayo mĩtaro yaguo yothe ĩkorwo ĩkĩrĩra maithori,
English: If my land cries out against me, and its furrows weep together;

Kikuyu: ingĩkorwo ndanarĩa maciaro maguo iteekũrĩha, kana ngoraga ngoro cia ene guo-rĩ,
English: if I have eaten its fruits without money, or have caused its owners to lose their life,

Kikuyu: hĩndĩ ĩyo congʼe ũrokũra kuo handũ ha ngano, na riya handũ ha cairi.” Ndeto cia Ayubu nĩciathira.
English: let briers grow instead of wheat, and stinkweed instead of barley.” The words of Job are ended.

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ ũcio andũ acio atatũ nĩmatigire gũcookeria Ayubu, nĩ ũndũ eeyonaga arĩ mũthingu.
English: So these three men ceased to answer Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.

Kikuyu: No rĩrĩ, Elihu mũrũ wa Barakeli ũrĩa Mũbuzi, wa nyũmba ya Ramu, nĩarakaririo mũno nĩ Ayubu nĩ ũndũ wa gwĩtua aarĩ na kĩhooto gũkĩra Ngai.
English: Then the wrath of Elihu the son of Barachel, the Buzite, of the family of Ram, was kindled against Job. His wrath was kindled because he justified himself rather than God.

Kikuyu: Ningĩ nĩarakarĩtio nĩ arata acio atatũ tondũ nĩmagĩte ũndũ mangĩcookeria Ayubu, o na gũtuĩka nĩmamũtuĩrĩire ciira.
English: Also his wrath was kindled against his three friends, because they had found no answer, and yet had condemned Job.

Kikuyu: Na rĩrĩ, Elihu aambĩte gweterera acio angĩ maarie atanaaria na Ayubu, tondũ o maarĩ akũrũ kũmũkĩra.
English: Now Elihu had waited to speak to Job, because they were older than he.

Kikuyu: No rĩrĩa onire atĩ andũ acio atatũ matiarĩ na ũndũ ũngĩ wa kuuga-rĩ, agĩakanwo nĩ marakara.
English: When Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouth of these three men, his wrath was kindled.

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ ũcio Elihu, mũrũ wa Barakeli ũcio Mũbuzi, akiuga atĩrĩ: “Niĩ ndĩ na mĩaka mĩnini, na inyuĩ mũrĩ akũrũ; nĩkĩo ngwĩtigagĩra, ngaaga ũũmĩrĩru wa kũmwĩra ũrĩa njũũĩ.
English: Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite answered, “I am young, and you are very old. Therefore I held back, and didn’t dare show you my opinion.

Kikuyu: Ndeciiragia atĩrĩ, ‘Ũkũrũ nĩwaagĩrĩire warie; ũingĩ wa mĩaka nĩwaagĩrĩire kũrutana ũũgĩ.’
English: I said, ‘Days should speak, and multitude of years should teach wisdom.’

Kikuyu: No nĩ roho ũrĩa ũrĩ thĩinĩ wa mũndũ, o yo mĩhũmũ ya Mwene-Hinya-Wothe, ũheaga mũndũ ũmenyo.
English: But there is a spirit in man, and the Spirit† of the Almighty gives them understanding.

Kikuyu: To arĩa akũrũ oiki oogĩ, na to arĩa akũrũ mamenyaga ũrĩa kwagĩrĩire.
English: It is not the great who are wise, nor the aged who understand justice.

Kikuyu: “Nĩ ũndũ ũcio nguuga atĩrĩ, ‘Thikĩrĩriai; o na niĩ nĩngũmwĩra ũrĩa njũũĩ.’
English: Therefore I said, ‘Listen to me; I also will show my opinion.’

Kikuyu: Nĩngwetereire rĩrĩa mũkwaragia, ndathikĩrĩria ihooto cianyu; rĩrĩa mũgũcaragia ciugo-rĩ,
English: “Behold, I waited for your words, and I listened for your reasoning, while you searched out what to say.

Kikuyu: nĩngũmũtegeire matũ biũ. No gũtirĩ o na ũmwe wanyu wonanirie mahĩtia ma Ayubu; gũtirĩ o na ũmwe wanyu ũmũcookeirie mĩario yake.
English: Yes, I gave you my full attention, but there was no one who convinced Job, or who answered his words, among you.

Kikuyu: Tigai kuuga atĩrĩ, ‘Nĩtũgĩĩte na ũũgĩ; rekei Mũrungu amũkararie, no ti mũndũ.’
English: Beware lest you say, ‘We have found wisdom. God may refute him, not man;’

Kikuyu: No rĩrĩ, Ayubu ti niĩ ekwerekeirie ciugo ciake, na niĩ ndikũmũcookeria kũringana na mĩario yanyu.
English: for he has not directed his words against me; neither will I answer him with your speeches.

Kikuyu: “Nĩmamakĩte, na matirĩ na ũndũ ũngĩ mangiuga; nĩmarigĩtwo nĩ atĩa mangiuga.
English: “They are amazed. They answer no more. They don’t have a word to say.

Kikuyu: no nginya njeterere, nĩ ũndũ rĩu nĩmakirĩte, tondũ atĩ rĩu marũgamĩte hau matarĩ na macookio?
English: Shall I wait, because they don’t speak, because they stand still, and answer no more?

Kikuyu: O na niĩ nĩngwaria; o na niĩ nĩnguuga ũrĩa njũũĩ.
English: I also will answer my part, and I also will show my opinion.

Kikuyu: Nĩgũkorwo njiyũrĩtwo nĩ ciugo, naguo roho ũrĩa ũrĩ thĩinĩ wakwa nĩũrandindĩkĩrĩria;
English: For I am full of words. The spirit within me constrains me.

Kikuyu: thĩinĩ wakwa haana ta ndibei ĩrĩ cuba ngunĩke, ngahaana ta mondo njerũ ya ndibei ĩkirie gũtuthũka.
English: Behold, my breast is as wine which has no vent; like new wineskins it is ready to burst.

Kikuyu: no nginya njarie hũũcũke, no nginya ndumũre mĩromo yakwa njookie ũhoro.
English: I will speak, that I may be refreshed. I will open my lips and answer.

Kikuyu: Ndigũtĩĩra mũndũ o na ũ maũthĩ, kana ngaathĩrĩrie mũndũ o na ũrĩkũ tũhũ;
English: Please don’t let me respect any man’s person, neither will I give flattering titles to any man.

Kikuyu: nĩ ũndũ korwo ndĩ mwara na kũgaathĩrĩria, Mũnyũũmbi no anjeherie narua.
English: For I don’t know how to give flattering titles, or else my Maker would soon take me away.

Kikuyu: “No rĩu Ayubu-rĩ, thikĩrĩria ciugo ciakwa; tega matũ ũigue ũrĩa wothe nguuga.
English: “However, Job, please hear my speech, and listen to all my words.

Kikuyu: Ndĩ hakuhĩ gũtumũra kanua gakwa; ciugo ciakwa irĩ o rũrĩmĩ-inĩ rwakwa.
English: See now, I have opened my mouth. My tongue has spoken in my mouth.

Kikuyu: Ciugo ciakwa ciumĩte ngoro nũngĩrĩru; mĩromo yakwa yaragia ĩtarĩ na ũhinga.
English: My words will utter the uprightness of my heart. That which my lips know they will speak sincerely.

Kikuyu: Roho wa Mũrungu nĩwe ũnyũmbĩte; mĩhũmũ ya Mwene-Hinya-Wothe nĩyo ĩĩheaga muoyo.
English: The Spirit of God has made me, and the breath of the Almighty gives me life.

Kikuyu: Nawe njookeria, akorwo nĩũkũhota; wĩhaarĩrie ũũngʼethere.
English: If you can, answer me. Set your words in order before me, and stand up.

Kikuyu: Niĩ haana o tawe maitho-inĩ ma Mũrungu; o na niĩ ndombirwo na rĩũmba.
English: Behold, I am toward God even as you are. I am also formed out of the clay.

Kikuyu: Kwĩĩndigĩra gũtigakũmakie, kana guoko gwakwa gũkũritũhĩre.
English: Behold, my terror will not make you afraid, neither will my pressure be heavy on you.

Kikuyu: “No rĩrĩ, nĩuugĩte ngĩiguaga, ngaigua ciugo icio ũkiuga atĩ,
English: “Surely you have spoken in my hearing, I have heard the voice of your words, saying,

Kikuyu: ‘Ndĩ mũtheru na ndirĩ na mehia; ndiĩkĩte ũũru, na ndirĩ na mahĩtia.
English: ‘I am clean, without disobedience. I am innocent, neither is there iniquity in me.

Kikuyu: No Ngai nĩanyonete na mahĩtia; anduĩte thũ yake.
English: Behold, he finds occasions against me. He counts me for his enemy.

Kikuyu: Nĩanjohaga magũrũ na mĩnyororo; arangagĩra njĩra ciakwa ciothe.’
English: He puts my feet in the stocks. He marks all my paths.’

Kikuyu: “No ngũkwĩra atĩrĩ, ũhoro-inĩ ũyũ wee ndũrĩ na kĩhooto, nĩgũkorwo Ngai nĩ mũnene gũkĩra mũndũ.
English: “Behold, I will answer you. In this you are not just, for God is greater than man.

Kikuyu: Ũramũtetia nĩkĩ, atĩ ndacookagia kiugo kĩa mũndũ o na kĩmwe?
English: Why do you strive against him, because he doesn’t give account of any of his matters?

Kikuyu: Nĩgũkorwo Mũrungu nĩaaragia, rĩmwe na njĩra ĩmwe, na rĩngĩ akaaria na njĩra ĩngĩ, o na gũtuĩka mũndũ no aage gũkũũrana.
English: For God speaks once, yes twice, though man pays no attention.

Kikuyu: Rĩmwe akaaragia kĩroto-inĩ na kĩoneki-inĩ gĩa ũtukũ, rĩrĩa andũ mahĩtĩtwo nĩ toro mũnene marĩ ũrĩrĩ,
English: In a dream, in a vision of the night, when deep sleep falls on men, in slumbering on the bed,

Kikuyu: no amaarĩrie matũ-inĩ mao, na amamakie nĩguo amakaanie,
English: then he opens the ears of men, and seals their instruction,

Kikuyu: nĩguo agarũre mũndũ atige kũhĩtia, na atigane na mwĩtĩĩo,
English: that he may withdraw man from his purpose, and hide pride from man.

Kikuyu: nĩguo agitĩre roho wake kuuma gĩkuũ-inĩ, na agitĩre muoyo wake ndũkaniinwo na rũhiũ rwa njora.
English: He keeps back his soul from the pit, and his life from perishing by the sword.

Kikuyu: Ningĩ mũndũ no arũithio na gũkomio ũrĩrĩ wa ruo, akorwo na thĩĩna wa mahĩndĩ ũtathiraga,
English: “He is chastened also with pain on his bed, with continual strife in his bones,

Kikuyu: o nginya ngoro yake ĩgathũũra irio, na roho wake ũgathũũra irio iria njega mũno.
English: so that his life abhors bread, and his soul dainty food.

Kikuyu: Nyama cia mwĩrĩ wake ihĩnjaga igathirĩrĩkĩra, na mahĩndĩ make marĩa mataroonekaga makoimĩra.
English: His flesh is so consumed away that it can’t be seen. His bones that were not seen stick out.

Kikuyu: Roho wake ũgakuhĩrĩria mbĩrĩra, na muoyo wake ũgakuhĩrĩria arĩa mareehage gĩkuũ.
English: Yes, his soul draws near to the pit, and his life to the destroyers.

Kikuyu: “No rĩrĩ, angĩkorwo harĩ na mũraika mwena wake arĩ mũiguithania, ũmwe harĩ ngiri, wa kwĩra mũndũ ũndũ ũrĩa ũmwagĩrĩire,
English: “If there is beside him an angel, an interpreter, one among a thousand, to show to man what is right for him,

Kikuyu: nake amũkinyĩrie wega wake na oige atĩrĩ, ‘Mũhonokie ndagatuĩke wa gũikũrũka mbĩrĩra-inĩ; nĩnyonete gĩa kũmũkũũra nakĩo,’
English: then God is gracious to him, and says, ‘Deliver him from going down to the pit, I have found a ransom.’

Kikuyu: hĩndĩ ĩyo nyama cia mwĩrĩ wake igeethĩha ta cia mwana; igaacooka ta ũrĩa ciarĩ matukũ-inĩ ma wĩthĩ wake.
English: His flesh will be fresher than a child’s. He returns to the days of his youth.

Kikuyu: Ahooyaga Ngai ageekwo wega nĩwe, oonaga ũthiũ wa Ngai akaanĩrĩra nĩ gũkena; agacookio ũthingu-inĩ wake nĩ Ngai.
English: He prays to God, and he is favorable to him, so that he sees his face with joy. He restores to man his righteousness.

Kikuyu: Nake agacooka agathiĩ kũrĩ andũ akameera atĩrĩ, ‘Nĩndehirie, na ngĩogomia ũndũ ũrĩa warĩ wa ma, no ndiigana kũherithio ũrĩa ndaagĩrĩirwo nĩkũherithio.
English: He sings before men, and says, ‘I have sinned, and perverted that which was right, and it didn’t profit me.

Kikuyu: Nĩakũũrire roho wakwa ndũkaharũrũkio mbĩrĩra, na niĩ ngũtũũra ngenagĩra ũtheri ũcio.’
English: He has redeemed my soul from going into the pit. My life will see the light.’

Kikuyu: “Mũrungu nĩekaga mũndũ maũndũ macio mothe, maita meerĩ o na kana matatũ,
English: “Behold, God does all these things, twice, yes three times, with a man,

Kikuyu: nĩguo agarũre roho wake ndũkaharũrũkio mbĩrĩra, nĩgeetha ũtheri ũcio wa muoyo ũmũtherere.
English: to bring back his soul from the pit, that he may be enlightened with the light of the living.

Kikuyu: “Atĩrĩrĩ Ayubu, tega matũ na ũũthikĩrĩrie; kira ki na niĩ njarie.
English: Mark well, Job, and listen to me. Hold your peace, and I will speak.

Kikuyu: Wakorwo ũrĩ na ũndũ wa kuuga-rĩ, njĩĩra; aria, nĩgũkorwo ingĩenda woneke ndwĩhĩtie.
English: If you have anything to say, answer me. Speak, for I desire to justify you.

Kikuyu: No akorwo ti ũguo-rĩ, wee gĩthikĩrĩrie; kira ki, na nĩngũkũruta ũũgĩ.”
English: If not, listen to me. Hold your peace, and I will teach you wisdom.”

Kikuyu: Ningĩ Elihu akiuga atĩrĩ:
English: Moreover Elihu answered,

Kikuyu: “Iguai ciugo ciakwa, inyuĩ andũ aya oogĩ; thikĩrĩriai, inyuĩ amenyi a maũndũ.
English: “Hear my words, you wise men. Give ear to me, you who have knowledge.

Kikuyu: Nĩgũkorwo gũtũ gũthuuranagia ciugo o ta ũrĩa rũrĩmĩ rũcamaga irio.
English: For the ear tries words, as the palate tastes food.
