Kikuyu: Nĩtwĩkũũranĩrei ithuĩ ene ũndũ ũrĩa wagĩrĩire; nĩtwĩrute tũrĩ hamwe ũndũ ũrĩa mwega.
English: Let us choose for us that which is right. Let us know among ourselves what is good.

Kikuyu: “Ayubu aroiga atĩrĩ, ‘Niĩ ndihĩtĩtie, no Mũrungu nĩanjagithĩtie kĩhooto gĩakwa.
English: For Job has said, ‘I am righteous, God has taken away my right.

Kikuyu: O na gũtuĩka ndĩraria ũrĩa kũrĩ, ndĩratuuo mũheenania; o na gũtuĩka ndirĩ na mahĩtia, mũguĩ wake ũngurarĩtie kĩronda gĩtangĩhona.’
English: Notwithstanding my right I am considered a liar. My wound is incurable, though I am without disobedience.’

Kikuyu: Nĩ mũndũ ũrĩkũ ũhaana ta Ayubu, mũndũ ũnyuuaga kĩnyũrũri taarĩ maaĩ aranyua?
English: What man is like Job, who drinks scorn like water,

Kikuyu: Atwaranaga na andũ arĩa mekaga ũũru; agĩĩaga thiritũ na andũ arĩa aaganu.
English: who goes in company with the workers of iniquity, and walks with wicked men?

Kikuyu: Nĩgũkorwo oigaga atĩrĩ, ‘Gũtirĩ uumithio mũndũ onaga rĩrĩa arageria gũkenia Ngai.’
English: For he has said, ‘It profits a man nothing that he should delight himself with God.’

Kikuyu: “Nĩ ũndũ ũcio gĩĩthikĩrĩriei, inyuĩ andũ aya mũrĩ na ũtaũku. Ũhoro wa kwĩhia ũroaga kuoneka harĩ Mũrungu, Mwene-Hinya-Wothe aroaga gwĩka ũũru.
English: “Therefore listen to me, you men of understanding: far be it from God, that he should do wickedness, from the Almighty, that he should commit iniquity.

Kikuyu: Arĩhaga mũndũ kũringana na ũrĩa ekĩte; akamũrehere o kĩrĩa kĩringaine na mĩthiĩre yake.
English: For the work of a man he will give to him, and cause every man to find according to his ways.

Kikuyu: Gũtingĩhoteka atĩ Mũrungu no eeke mahĩtia, atĩ ũrĩa Mwene-Hinya-Wothe no ogomie kĩhooto.
English: Yes surely, God will not do wickedly, neither will the Almighty pervert justice.

Kikuyu: Nũũ wamũtuire mũrori wa thĩ? Nũũ wamũtuire mũrũgamĩrĩri wa thĩ yothe?
English: Who put him in charge of the earth? Or who has appointed him over the whole world?

Kikuyu: Korwo aagĩa na muoroto wa kweheria roho wake na mĩhũmũ-rĩ,
English: If he set his heart on himself, if he gathered to himself his spirit and his breath,

Kikuyu: andũ othe mangĩthiranĩra hamwe, nake mũndũ acooke rũkũngũ-inĩ.
English: all flesh would perish together, and man would turn again to dust.

Kikuyu: “Akorwo ũrĩ mũndũ ũrĩ na ũtaũku-rĩ, igua ũhoro ũyũ; thikĩrĩria ũrĩa nguuga.
English: “If now you have understanding, hear this. Listen to the voice of my words.

Kikuyu: Mũndũ ũthũire kĩhooto-rĩ, no ahote gwathana? Ũrĩa ũrĩ kĩhooto, o Ũcio kĩhoti-rĩ, no ũmũtue mwĩhia?
English: Should even one who hates justice govern? Will you condemn him who is righteous and mighty,

Kikuyu: Githĩ ti we wĩraga athamaki atĩrĩ, ‘Inyuĩ mũtirĩ kĩene,’ na akeera arĩa marĩ igweta atĩrĩ, ‘Inyuĩ mũrĩ aaganu,’
English: who says to a king, ‘Vile!’ or to nobles, ‘Wicked!’?

Kikuyu: o ũcio ũtatĩagĩra anene maũthĩ, na ndendaga arĩa atongu gũkĩra arĩa athĩĩni, nĩgũkorwo othe nĩ wĩra wa moko make?
English: He doesn’t respect the persons of princes, nor respect the rich more than the poor, for they all are the work of his hands.

Kikuyu: Makuuaga o rĩmwe, o ũtukũ gatagatĩ; andũ mainainaga magakua; arĩa marĩ hinya meeheragio matahutĩtio nĩ guoko kwa mũndũ.
English: In a moment they die, even at midnight. The people are shaken and pass away. The mighty are taken away without a hand.

Kikuyu: “Maitho make maikaraga macũthĩrĩirie mĩthiĩre ya andũ; nĩonaga mĩthiĩre yao yothe.
English: “For his eyes are on the ways of a man. He sees all his goings.

Kikuyu: Gũtirĩ handũ harĩ nduma, kana handũ harĩ kĩĩruru kĩnene, hangĩĩhithwo nĩ arĩa meekaga ũũru.
English: There is no darkness, nor thick gloom, where the workers of iniquity may hide themselves.

Kikuyu: Mũrungu ndabatairio nĩgũthuthuuria ndeto cia andũ makĩria, atĩ nĩguo moke mbere yake maciirithio.
English: For he doesn’t need to consider a man further, that he should go before God in judgment.

Kikuyu: Ahehenjaga arĩa marĩ ũhoti atekũũria mũndũ na akarũgamia andũ angĩ ithenya rĩao.
English: He breaks mighty men in pieces in ways past finding out, and sets others in their place.

Kikuyu: Tondũ we nĩamenyaga maũndũ marĩa meekaga, amangʼaũranagia ũtukũ magathuthĩka.
English: Therefore he takes knowledge of their works. He overturns them in the night, so that they are destroyed.

Kikuyu: Amaherithagĩria waganu wao makĩonagwo nĩ mũndũ o wothe,
English: He strikes them as wicked men in the open sight of others;

Kikuyu: tondũ nĩmagarũrũkire magĩtiga kũmũrũmĩrĩra, na matirũmbũyagia njĩra yake o na ĩrĩkũ.
English: because they turned away from following him, and wouldn’t pay attention to any of his ways,

Kikuyu: Nĩmatũmire kĩrĩro kĩa arĩa athĩĩni gĩkinye hau mbere yake, nĩ ũndũ ũcio akĩigua kĩrĩro kĩa arĩa abatari.
English: so that they caused the cry of the poor to come to him. He heard the cry of the afflicted.

Kikuyu: No rĩrĩ, angĩikara akirĩte-rĩ, nũũ ũngĩmũtua muhĩtia? Angĩhitha ũthiũ wake-rĩ, nũũ ũngĩmuona? Nowe arĩ igũrũ rĩa mũndũ na igũrũ rĩa rũrĩrĩ o ũndũ ũmwe,
English: When he gives quietness, who then can condemn? When he hides his face, who then can see him? He is over a nation or a man alike,

Kikuyu: nĩguo agirie mũndũ ũtarĩ na ũngai gwathana, amũgirie kũigĩra kĩrĩndĩ mĩtego.
English: that the godless man may not reign, that there be no one to ensnare the people.

Kikuyu: “Korwo mũndũ no ere Mũrungu atĩrĩ, ‘Nĩnjĩhĩtie no ndikehia rĩngĩ.
English: “For has any said to God, ‘I am guilty, but I will not offend any more.

Kikuyu: Nduta menye ũrĩa itarahota kuona; ingĩkorwo nĩnjĩkĩte ũũru-rĩ, ndigacooka gwĩka ũguo rĩngĩ.’
English: Teach me that which I don’t see. If I have done iniquity, I will do it no more’?

Kikuyu: Ngai-rĩ, no agĩkũrĩhe kũringana na ũrĩa wee ũkwenda rĩrĩa ũregete kwĩrira? No nginya we ũtue itua, no ti niĩ; nĩ ũndũ ũcio kĩnjĩĩre ũrĩa ũũĩ.
English: Shall his recompense be as you desire, that you refuse it? For you must choose, and not I. Therefore speak what you know.

Kikuyu: “Andũ arĩa marĩ na ũtaũku maroiga atĩrĩ, nao andũ acio oogĩ maiguĩte ngĩaria manjĩĩrĩte atĩrĩ,
English: Men of understanding will tell me, yes, every wise man who hears me:

Kikuyu: ‘Ayubu aaragia atarĩ na ũmenyo; ciugo ciake nĩciagĩte ũũgĩ.’
English: ‘Job speaks without knowledge. His words are without wisdom.’

Kikuyu: Hĩ, naarĩ korwo Ayubu aagerio nginya mũthia, nĩ ũndũ macookio make nĩ ta ma mũndũ mwaganu!
English: I wish that Job were tried to the end, because of his answering like wicked men.

Kikuyu: Nĩongereire ũremi harĩ mehia make; atũhũũragĩra hĩ cia kĩnyũrũri, na akaingĩhia ciugo ciake cia gũũkĩrĩra Mũrungu.”
English: For he adds rebellion to his sin. He claps his hands among us, and multiplies his words against God.”

Kikuyu: Ningĩ Elihu akiuga atĩrĩ:
English: Moreover Elihu answered,

Kikuyu: “Nĩũgwĩciiria ũhoro ũyũ nĩ wa kĩhooto? Ũroiga atĩrĩ, ‘Mũrungu nĩekũnjarĩrĩria atue ndiĩhĩtie.’
English: “Do you think this to be your right, or do you say, ‘My righteousness is more than God’s,’

Kikuyu: No rĩrĩ, wee no ũramũũria atĩrĩ, ‘Kũrĩ na uumithio ũrĩkũ harĩ niĩ, na ngũgunĩka nakĩ ndaaga kwĩhia?’
English: that you ask, ‘What advantage will it be to you? What profit will I have, more than if I had sinned?’

Kikuyu: “No nyende gũgũcookeria ũhoro, wee hamwe na arata aku.
English: I will answer you, and your companions with you.

Kikuyu: Ta rora igũrũ wone; ta cũthĩrĩria matu macio marĩ igũrũ rĩaku kũraya mũno.
English: Look to the skies, and see. See the skies, which are higher than you.

Kikuyu: Ũngĩĩhia-rĩ, ũndũ ũcio ũngĩhutia Ngai atĩa? Mehia maku mangĩingĩha mũno-rĩ, ũndũ ũcio ũngĩmwĩka atĩa?
English: If you have sinned, what effect do you have against him? If your transgressions are multiplied, what do you do to him?

Kikuyu: Ũngĩkorwo ũrĩ mũthingu-rĩ, ũngĩmũhe kĩĩ, kana nĩ kĩĩ aamũkagĩra kuuma guoko-inĩ gwaku?
English: If you are righteous, what do you give him? Or what does he receive from your hand?

Kikuyu: Waganu waku ũhutagia o mũndũ tawe, na ũthingu waku ũkahutia o ciana cia andũ.
English: Your wickedness may hurt a man as you are, and your righteousness may profit a son of man.

Kikuyu: “Andũ makayaga nĩ icooki rĩa kũhinyĩrĩrio; mathaithanaga mateithũrwo guoko-inĩ kwa ũcio ũrĩ hinya mũingĩ.
English: “By reason of the multitude of oppressions they cry out. They cry for help by reason of the arm of the mighty.

Kikuyu: No gũtirĩ mũndũ uugaga atĩrĩ, ‘Ngai ũrĩa wanyũũmbire arĩ ha, ũrĩa ũheaga mũndũ nyĩmbo ũtukũ,
English: But no one says, ‘Where is God my Maker, who gives songs in the night,

Kikuyu: ũrĩa ũtũrutaga maũndũ gũkĩra ũrĩa arutaga nyamũ cia werũ-inĩ, o na agatũhe ũũgĩ gũkĩra nyoni cia rĩera-inĩ?’
English: who teaches us more than the animals of the earth, and makes us wiser than the birds of the sky?’

Kikuyu: Ndacookagia rĩrĩa andũ maakaya nĩ ũndũ wa mwĩtũũgĩrio wa andũ arĩa aaganu.
English: There they cry, but no one answers, because of the pride of evil men.

Kikuyu: Ti-itherũ, Mũrungu ndathikagĩrĩria mathaithana mao ma tũhũ; ũcio Mwene-Hinya-Wothe ndarũmbũyagia mathaithana macio.
English: Surely God will not hear an empty cry, neither will the Almighty regard it.

Kikuyu: Githĩ ndakaaga gũthikĩrĩria mũno makĩria rĩrĩa ũkuuga atĩ ndũramuona, na atĩ ciira waku ũrĩ mbere yake, na no nginya ũmweterere,
English: How much less when you say you don’t see him. The cause is before him, and you wait for him!

Kikuyu: na makĩria ma ũguo ũkoiga atĩ marakara make matiherithanagia na ndarũmbũyagia waganu o na hanini!
English: But now, because he has not visited in his anger, neither does he greatly regard arrogance,

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ ũcio Ayubu atumũrĩte kanua gake akaaria ũhoro wa tũhũ; nĩarĩĩtie ndeto nyingĩ atarĩ na ũmenyo.”
English: therefore Job opens his mouth with empty talk, and he multiplies words without knowledge.”

Kikuyu: Elihu agĩthiĩ na mbere kwaria, akiuga atĩrĩ:
English: Elihu also continued, and said,

Kikuyu: “Ngirĩrĩria hanini, na nĩngũkuonia atĩ harĩ maũndũ mangĩ mangiugwo ma gũciirĩrĩra Ngai.
English: “Bear with me a little, and I will show you; for I still have something to say on God’s behalf.

Kikuyu: Ũmenyo wakwa ndĩũrutĩte kũraihu; niĩ ngũtũũgĩria kĩhooto kĩa ũcio Mũnyũũmbi.
English: I will get my knowledge from afar, and will ascribe righteousness to my Maker.

Kikuyu: Menya wega atĩ ndeto ciakwa ti cia maheeni; ũyũ mũrĩ nake arĩ na ũmenyo mũkinyanĩru.
English: For truly my words are not false. One who is perfect in knowledge is with you.

Kikuyu: “Mũrungu nĩwe mwene hinya, no ndairaga andũ; we nĩ mwene hinya, na nĩarũmagia muoroto wake.
English: “Behold, God is mighty, and doesn’t despise anyone. He is mighty in strength of understanding.

Kikuyu: Ndatũũragia arĩa aaganu muoyo, no nĩaheaga arĩa anyariire kĩhooto kĩao.
English: He doesn’t preserve the life of the wicked, but gives justice to the afflicted.

Kikuyu: Ndeheragia maitho make harĩ arĩa athingu; amaikaragĩria gĩtĩ kĩa ũnene hamwe na athamaki, na akamatũũgĩria nginya tene.
English: He doesn’t withdraw his eyes from the righteous, but with kings on the throne, he sets them forever, and they are exalted.

Kikuyu: No rĩrĩ, andũ mangĩkorwo mohetwo na mĩnyororo, makanyiitio na mĩhĩndo ya mĩnyamaro,
English: If they are bound in fetters, and are taken in the cords of afflictions,

Kikuyu: we nĩameeraga ũrĩa mekĩte, atĩ mehĩtie na ũtũrĩka.
English: then he shows them their work, and their transgressions, that they have behaved themselves proudly.

Kikuyu: We nĩatũmaga mathikĩrĩrie ũtaaro, na akamaatha merire ũũru wao.
English: He also opens their ears to instruction, and commands that they return from iniquity.

Kikuyu: Mangĩmwathĩkĩra na mamũtungatĩre, megũtũũra matukũ mao marĩa matigaru magaacĩire, na mĩaka yao o maiganĩire.
English: If they listen and serve him, they will spend their days in prosperity, and their years in pleasures.

Kikuyu: No mangĩaga kũigua, nĩmakaniinwo na rũhiũ rwa njora, na makue matarĩ na ũmenyo.
English: But if they don’t listen, they will perish by the sword; they will die without knowledge.

Kikuyu: “Arĩa matarĩ na Ngai ngoro-inĩ meiigagĩra marakara; o na rĩrĩa aramooha na mĩnyororo, matikayaga mateithio.
English: “But those who are godless in heart lay up anger. They don’t cry for help when he binds them.

Kikuyu: Makuuaga marĩ ethĩ, magakua hamwe na arũme arĩa maraya ma mahooero-inĩ.
English: They die in youth. Their life perishes among the unclean.

Kikuyu: No arĩa mathĩĩnĩkaga, nĩamakũũraga kuuma thĩĩna-inĩ wao; nĩamaragĩria marĩ mĩnyamaro-inĩ.
English: He delivers the afflicted by their affliction, and opens their ear in oppression.

Kikuyu: “We-rĩ, nĩarakũguucĩrĩria uume magego-inĩ ma mĩnyamaro, agũtware handũ haariĩ hatarĩ na ũkunderu, na agũtware akũhurũkie metha-inĩ yaku ĩiyũrĩte irio iria njega.
English: Yes, he would have allured you out of distress, into a wide place, where there is no restriction. That which is set on your table would be full of fatness.

Kikuyu: No rĩu-rĩ, ũtitikithĩtio ituĩro rĩrĩa rĩagĩrĩire arĩa aaganu; ituĩro rĩa ciira na kĩhooto nĩcigũkumbatĩte.
English: “But you are full of the judgment of the wicked. Judgment and justice take hold of you.

Kikuyu: Wĩmenyerere mũndũ o na ũrĩkũ ndakanakũheenererie na ũtonga; ndũgetĩkĩrie ihaki inene rĩkũhĩtithie njĩra.
English: Don’t let riches entice you to wrath, neither let the great size of a bribe turn you aside.

Kikuyu: Ũtonga waku o na kana kĩyo gĩaku kĩnene-rĩ, no ikũnyiitĩrĩre nĩguo ndũgatoonye mĩnyamaro-inĩ?
English: Would your wealth sustain you in distress, or all the might of your strength?

Kikuyu: Tiga kwĩrirĩria ũtukũ, nĩguo ũguucũrũrie andũ kuuma kwao mĩciĩ.
English: Don’t desire the night, when people are cut off in their place.

Kikuyu: Wĩmenyerere ndũkeerekere ũũru-inĩ, tondũ ũkuoneka taarĩ guo wendete gũkĩra gũthĩĩnĩka.
English: Take heed, don’t regard iniquity; for you have chosen this rather than affliction.

Kikuyu: “Mũrungu nĩatũgĩrĩtio nĩ ũndũ wa ũhoti wake. Nũũ mũrutani take?
English: Behold, God is exalted in his power. Who is a teacher like him?

Kikuyu: Nũũ ũmwathĩrĩire njĩra ciake, kana akamwĩra atĩrĩ, ‘Wee nĩwĩkĩte ũũru’?
English: Who has prescribed his way for him? Or who can say, ‘You have committed unrighteousness’?

Kikuyu: Ririkanaga gwĩkĩrĩra wĩra wake, ũrĩa andũ manakumia na rwĩmbo.
English: “Remember that you magnify his work, about which men have sung.

Kikuyu: Andũ othe nĩmawonete; andũ mawĩroragĩra marĩ o kũraya.
English: All men have looked on it. Man sees it afar off.

Kikuyu: Ĩ Mũrungu ndakĩrĩ mũnene; nĩ mũnene gũkĩra ũmenyi witũ! Mũigana wa mĩaka yake ndũngĩtuĩrĩka.
English: Behold, God is great, and we don’t know him. The number of his years is unsearchable.

Kikuyu: “Ambatagia matata ma maaĩ, marĩa macookaga gũtaatĩra tũrũũĩ ta mbura;
English: For he draws up the drops of water, which distill in rain from his vapor,

Kikuyu: matu magaita ũigũ wamo, nayo mbura nyingĩ ĩkoirĩra andũ.
English: which the skies pour down and which drop on man abundantly.

Kikuyu: Nũũ ũngĩmenya ũrĩa atambũrũkagia matu, kana ũhoro wa marurumĩ marĩa moimaga hema-inĩ yake?
English: Indeed, can anyone understand the spreading of the clouds and the thunderings of his pavilion?

Kikuyu: Kĩone ũrĩa ahurunjaga rũheni rwake rũkamũthiũrũrũkĩria, agathambia iria kũrĩa kũriku.
English: Behold, he spreads his light around him. He covers the bottom of the sea.

Kikuyu: Ũũ nĩguo aathaga ndũrĩrĩ na akaheana irio nyingĩ.
English: For by these he judges the people. He gives food in abundance.

Kikuyu: Akumbatagĩria rũheni na moko make, na akarwatha rũringe kĩrĩa kĩorotetwo.
English: He covers his hands with the lightning, and commands it to strike the mark.

Kikuyu: Marurumĩ make nĩmanagĩrĩra kĩhuhũkanio kĩrĩa kĩroka; o na ngʼombe nĩimenyithanagia atĩ kũrĩ kĩhuhũkanio kĩroka.
English: Its noise tells about him, and the livestock also, concerning the storm that comes up.

Kikuyu: “Ndaigua ũguo ngoro yakwa ĩgatumatuuma, na ĩkambarara ĩkoima handũ hayo.
English: “Yes, at this my heart trembles, and is moved out of its place.

Kikuyu: Thikĩrĩria! Thikĩrĩria mũraramo wa mũgambo wake, mũrurumo ũrĩa uumaga kanua gake.
English: Hear, oh, hear the noise of his voice, the sound that goes out of his mouth.

Kikuyu: Arekagĩrĩria rũheni rwake rungu rwa igũrũ guothe na akarũtũma nginya ituri cia thĩ.
English: He sends it out under the whole sky, and his lightning to the ends of the earth.

Kikuyu: Thuutha waruo gũũkaga mũgambo wa mũraramo wake; arurumaga na mũgambo wake mũkaru. Hĩndĩ ĩrĩa mũgambo wake waiguuo-rĩ, ndarigagĩrĩria heni.
English: After it a voice roars. He thunders with the voice of his majesty. He doesn’t hold back anything when his voice is heard.

Kikuyu: Mũgambo wa Mũrungu ũrurumaga na njĩra ya magegania; ekaga maũndũ manene tũtangĩhota kũmenya.
English: God thunders marvelously with his voice. He does great things, which we can’t comprehend.

Kikuyu: Eeraga tharunji atĩrĩ, ‘Gwa thĩ,’ nayo mbura ya rũthuthuũ akamĩĩra atĩrĩ, ‘Tuĩka mbura nene.’
English: For he says to the snow, ‘Fall on the earth,’ likewise to the shower of rain, and to the showers of his mighty rain.

Kikuyu: Nĩatigithagia mũndũ o wothe wĩra wake nĩgeetha andũ othe ombĩte mamenye wĩra wake.
English: He seals up the hand of every man, that all men whom he has made may know it.

Kikuyu: Nyamũ nacio nĩciĩhithaga; ciikaraga imamo-inĩ ciacio.
English: Then the animals take cover, and remain in their dens.

Kikuyu: Kĩhuhũkanio kiumaga gĩikaro gĩakĩo, heho nayo ĩkoima rũhuho-inĩ rũkĩhurutana.
English: Out of its room comes the storm, and cold out of the north.

Kikuyu: Mĩhũmũ ya Mũrungu nĩĩthondekaga mbarabu, namo maaĩ harĩa maaramĩire makanyiitana.
English: By the breath of God, ice is given, and the width of the waters is frozen.

Kikuyu: Nĩaiyũragia matu na ũigũ; ahurunjaga rũheni rũkamatũrĩkia.
English: Yes, he loads the thick cloud with moisture. He spreads abroad the cloud of his lightning.

Kikuyu: Mathiiaga magĩthiũrũrũkaga o kũrĩa angĩmeerekeria thĩ yothe, mageeke o ũrĩa wothe angĩmaatha.
English: It is turned around by his guidance, that they may do whatever he commands them on the surface of the habitable world,

Kikuyu: Arehaga matu macio nĩguo aherithie andũ, kana aihũgie thĩ yake na onanie wendani wake.
English: whether it is for correction, or for his land, or for loving kindness, that he causes it to come.

Kikuyu: “Ayubu, thikĩrĩria ũhoro ũyũ; tithĩria hau wĩcũũranie ũhoro wa magegania ma Mũrungu.
English: “Listen to this, Job. Stand still, and consider the wondrous works of God.

Kikuyu: Wee nĩũũĩ ũrĩa Ngai aathaga matu, na ũrĩa atũmaga rũheni rwake rũhenũke?
English: Do you know how God controls them, and causes the lightning of his cloud to shine?

Kikuyu: Wee nĩũũĩ ũrĩa matu macio macuurĩtio wega, magegania macio ma ũrĩa ũrĩ ũmenyo mũkinyanĩru?
English: Do you know the workings of the clouds, the wondrous works of him who is perfect in knowledge?

Kikuyu: Wee ũringĩkaga nĩ ũrugarĩ wa nguo ciaku rĩrĩa bũrũri ũkirĩte ki hĩndĩ ya rũhuho rwa gũthini-rĩ,
English: You whose clothing is warm when the earth is still by reason of the south wind?

Kikuyu: no ũhote kũruta wĩra nake ũhoro-inĩ wa gũtambũrũkia matu mairũ, o macio momĩte o ta gĩcicio gĩa gĩcango?
English: Can you, with him, spread out the sky, which is strong as a cast metal mirror?

Kikuyu: “Ta twĩre ũrĩa twagĩrĩirwo nĩ kũmwĩra; tũtingĩhota gwĩciirĩra nĩ ũndũ wa nduma iitũ.
English: Teach us what we will tell him, for we can’t make our case by reason of darkness.

Kikuyu: Nĩagĩrĩire kwĩrwo atĩ nĩngwenda kwaria? Nĩ kũrĩ mũndũ o na ũ ũngiuga amerio?
English: Will it be told him that I would speak? Or should a man wish that he were swallowed up?

Kikuyu: Rĩu-rĩ, gũtirĩ mũndũ ũngĩhota kũrora riũa, rĩcangararĩte kũu igũrũ thuutha wakuo kũhaatwo nĩ rũhuho gũgathera.
English: Now men don’t see the light which is bright in the skies, but the wind passes, and clears them.

Kikuyu: Okaga kuuma mwena wa gathigathini arĩ na riiri ukengeete ta wa thahabu; Ngai okaga arĩ na ũkaru wa gwĩtigĩrwo.
English: Out of the north comes golden splendor. With God is awesome majesty.

Kikuyu: Ũcio Mwene-Hinya-Wothe-rĩ, tũtingĩhota kũmũkinyĩra, nĩatũũgĩrĩtio nĩ ũndũ wa ũhoti wake; tondũ wa ũrĩa arĩ wa kĩhooto na ũthingu mũnene-rĩ, ndahinyanagĩrĩria.
English: We can’t reach the Almighty. He is exalted in power. In justice and great righteousness, he will not oppress.

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ ũcio andũ nĩmamũtĩĩte, tondũ githĩ ndarũmbũyagia arĩa meyonaga ta marĩ oogĩ na ngoro ciao?”
English: Therefore men revere him. He doesn’t regard any who are wise of heart.”

Kikuyu: Nake Jehova agĩcookeria Ayubu ũhoro arĩ kĩhuhũkanio-inĩ, akĩmwĩra atĩrĩ:
English: Then Yahweh answered Job out of the whirlwind,

Kikuyu: “Nũũ ũyũ ũrekĩra kĩrĩra gĩakwa nduma na ciugo itarĩ na ũmenyo?
English: “Who is this who darkens counsel by words without knowledge?

Kikuyu: Wĩhotore ta mũndũ mũrũme; nĩngũkũũria ciũria, nawe ũkĩnjookerie.
English: Brace yourself like a man, for I will question you, then you answer me!

Kikuyu: “Warĩ kũ rĩrĩa ndaakire mũthingi wa thĩ? Njĩĩra akorwo ũrĩ na ũũgĩ wa kũmenya.
English: “Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth? Declare, if you have understanding.

Kikuyu: Nũũ wathimire mũigana wayo? Ti-itherũ wee nĩũũĩ! Nũũ watambũrũkirie rũrigi rwa gũthima igũrũ rĩayo?
English: Who determined its measures, if you know? Or who stretched the line on it?

Kikuyu: Mĩthingi yayo yahandirwo igũrũ rĩa kĩĩ, kana nũũ wahaandire ihiga rĩayo rĩa koine,
English: What were its foundations fastened on? Or who laid its cornerstone,

Kikuyu: hĩndĩ ĩrĩa njata cia rũciinĩ ciainire hamwe, na araika othe makĩanĩrĩra nĩ gũkena?
English: when the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy?

Kikuyu: “Nũũ wahingĩrĩirie iria na mĩrango rĩrĩa rĩatumũkire kuuma nda,
English: “Or who shut up the sea with doors, when it broke out of the womb,

Kikuyu: rĩrĩa ndatuire matu nguo ciarĩo, na ngĩrĩoha nduma nene ta taama warĩo,
English: when I made clouds its garment, and wrapped it in thick darkness,

Kikuyu: rĩrĩa ndarĩkĩrĩire mĩhaka, na ngĩrĩhingĩra na mĩrango yarĩo, na ngĩĩkĩra mĩgĩĩko handũ hayo,
English: marked out for it my bound, set bars and doors,

Kikuyu: rĩrĩa ndoigire atĩrĩ, ‘Ũkinyage o haha na ndũkanahakĩre; makũmbĩ maku macio metĩĩi-rĩ, hau nĩho marĩĩkinyaga’?
English: and said, ‘You may come here, but no further. Your proud waves shall be stopped here’?

Kikuyu: “Kuuma o kĩambĩrĩria-rĩ, ũrĩ waathana atĩ rũciinĩ rũgĩe ho, kana ũkĩonereria ũtheri wa rũciinĩ harĩa ũkuumĩrĩra,
English: “Have you commanded the morning in your days, and caused the dawn to know its place,

Kikuyu: nĩguo ũhote kũnyiita thĩ na mĩthia yaguo, nao arĩa aaganu maribaribwo moime kuo?
English: that it might take hold of the ends of the earth, and shake the wicked out of it?

Kikuyu: Thĩ ĩhaanaga ta rĩũmba rĩhũrĩtwo mũhũũri; mũonekere wayo ũtariĩ ta mũhianĩre wa nguo.
English: It is changed as clay under the seal, and presented as a garment.

Kikuyu: Andũ arĩa aaganu nĩmaimagwo ũtheri wao, na guoko kwao kũrĩa kuoetwo na igũrũ gũkoinwo.
English: From the wicked, their light is withheld. The high arm is broken.

Kikuyu: “Ũrĩ wathiĩ rũgendo nginya kũrĩa iria rĩtherũkagĩra, kana ũgaceera itwe-inĩ cia ndia kũrĩa kũriku mũno?
English: “Have you entered into the springs of the sea? Or have you walked in the recesses of the deep?

Kikuyu: Ũrĩ wonio ihingo cia gĩkuũ? Ũrĩ wona ihingo cia kĩĩruru gĩa gĩkuũ?
English: Have the gates of death been revealed to you? Or have you seen the gates of the shadow of death?

Kikuyu: Ũrĩ wamenya ũnene wa wariĩ wa thĩ? Njĩĩra akorwo nĩũũĩ maũndũ macio mothe.
English: Have you comprehended the earth in its width? Declare, if you know it all.

Kikuyu: “Njĩra ya gũthiĩ kũrĩa ũtheri ũtũũraga nĩĩrĩkũ? Nayo nduma ĩikaraga kũ?
English: “What is the way to the dwelling of light? As for darkness, where is its place,

Kikuyu: No ũcitware gwacio? Nĩũũĩ tũcĩra twa gũthiĩ kũrĩa itũũraga?
English: that you should take it to its bound, that you should discern the paths to its house?

Kikuyu: Ti-itherũ wee nĩũũĩ, nĩgũkorwo warĩ mũciare! Wee-rĩ, nĩũtũũrĩte mĩaka mĩingĩ!
English: Surely you know, for you were born then, and the number of your days is great!

Kikuyu: “Ũrĩ watoonya makũmbĩ kũrĩa tharunji ĩigĩtwo, kana ũkĩona makũmbĩ kũrĩa mbura ya mbembe ĩigĩtwo,
English: Have you entered the storehouses of the snow, or have you seen the storehouses of the hail,

Kikuyu: o icio njigĩte nĩ ũndũ wa mahinda ma thĩĩna, ngaciiga nĩ ũndũ wa matukũ ma mbaara na ma kũrũa.
English: which I have reserved against the time of trouble, against the day of battle and war?

Kikuyu: Njĩra ya gũthiĩ kũrĩa ũtheri ũgayanagĩrio nĩĩrĩkũ, kana ya gũthiĩ kũrĩa rũhuho rwa irathĩro rũhurunjagĩrwo gũkũ thĩ?
English: By what way is the lightning distributed, or the east wind scattered on the earth?

Kikuyu: Nũũ wenjagĩra mbura ya kĩboboto mũtaro wa kũgerera, kana agatemera mbura ya marurumĩ njĩra,
English: Who has cut a channel for the flood water, or the path for the thunderstorm,

Kikuyu: nĩguo mbura yure bũrũri ũtatũũraga mũndũ, na yure werũ kũrĩa gũtarĩ mũndũ,
English: to cause it to rain on a land where there is no man, on the wilderness, in which there is no man,

Kikuyu: nĩguo ĩhũũnagie kũu gũtiganĩrie gũgakira ihooru, na ĩtũme kũmere nyeki?
English: to satisfy the waste and desolate ground, to cause the tender grass to grow?

Kikuyu: Mbura nĩĩrĩ ithe? Nũũ mũciari wa matata ma ime?
English: Does the rain have a father? Or who fathers the drops of dew?

Kikuyu: Tharunji yumaga nda ya ũ? Nũũ ũciaraga mbaa ĩrĩa yumaga igũrũ,
English: Whose womb did the ice come out of? Who has given birth to the gray frost of the sky?

Kikuyu: rĩrĩa maaĩ momaga ta ihiga, rĩrĩa maaĩ marĩa marĩ igũrũ wa iria magwatana?
English: The waters become hard like stone, when the surface of the deep is frozen.

Kikuyu: “Wee-rĩ, wahota kuohania njata iria thaka cia Kĩrĩmĩra? Wahota kuohora mĩkanda ya njata iria ciĩtagwo Karaũ?
English: “Can you bind the cluster of the Pleiades, or loosen the cords of Orion?

Kikuyu: Wahota kuumagaragia njata iria ciĩtagwo Mazarothu o mahinda maacio maakinya, kana wahota gũtongoria Nduba na ciana ciayo?
English: Can you lead the constellations out in their season? Or can you guide the Bear with her cubs?

Kikuyu: Nĩũũĩ mawatho ma igũrũ? No ũhote kũhaanda wathani wa Ngai ũrũme gũkũ thĩ?
English: Do you know the laws of the heavens? Can you establish its dominion over the earth?

Kikuyu: “Wahota kwanĩrĩra nginya mũgambo waku ũkinye matu-inĩ nĩguo kuure wĩhumbĩre na kĩguũ kĩa maaĩ?
English: “Can you lift up your voice to the clouds, that abundance of waters may cover you?

Kikuyu: Wee nĩwe ũtũmaga heni ithiĩ na njĩra ciacio? Nĩikũrehagĩra ũhoro igakwĩra atĩ, ‘Tũrĩ haha’?
English: Can you send out lightnings, that they may go? Do they report to you, ‘Here we are’?

Kikuyu: Nũũ waheire ngoro ũũgĩ, kana akĩhe meciiria ũmenyo?
English: Who has put wisdom in the inward parts? Or who has given understanding to the mind?

Kikuyu: Nũũ ũrĩ na ũũgĩ wa gũtara matu? Nũũ ũngĩhota kũinamia ndigithũ cia maaĩ cia igũrũ
English: Who can count the clouds by wisdom? Or who can pour out the containers of the sky,

Kikuyu: rĩrĩa rũkũngũ rwatondora, nayo ndoro ĩkooma ĩkanyiitana?
English: when the dust runs into a mass, and the clods of earth stick together?

Kikuyu: “Nĩwe ũguĩmagĩra mũrũũthi wa mũgoma wone gĩa kũrĩa, kana nĩwe ũniinagĩra mĩrũũthi ngʼaragu
English: “Can you hunt the prey for the lioness, or satisfy the appetite of the young lions,

Kikuyu: rĩrĩa ĩkomereire imamo-inĩ ciayo, kana rĩrĩa ĩikaraga yoheirie nyamũ ihinga-inĩ?
English: when they crouch in their dens, and lie in wait in the thicket?

Kikuyu: Nũũ ũheaga ihuru irio rĩrĩa tũcui twarĩo tũgũkaĩra Mũrungu tũkĩũrũũraga nĩ kwaga irio?
English: Who provides for the raven his prey, when his young ones cry to God, and wander for lack of food?

Kikuyu: “Wee nĩũũĩ rĩrĩa mbũri cia irĩma-inĩ iciaraga? Wee nĩwĩroragĩra rĩrĩa thwariga ĩgũciara kaana kayo?
English: “Do you know the time when the mountain goats give birth? Do you watch when the doe bears fawns?

Kikuyu: Wee nĩũtaraga mĩeri ĩrĩa ciikaraga ingĩgaaciara? Nĩũũĩ hĩndĩ ĩrĩa iciaraga?
English: Can you count the months that they fulfill? Or do you know the time when they give birth?

Kikuyu: Ciĩthunaga igaciara twana twacio; ruo rwacio rwa gũciara rũgathira.
English: They bow themselves. They bear their young. They end their labor pains.

Kikuyu: Twana twacio twagĩraga mwĩrĩ, tũgakũra tũrĩ na hinya o kũu gĩthaka-inĩ; tũkinyaga ihinda rĩa kwehera na tũticookaga.
English: Their young ones become strong. They grow up in the open field. They go out, and don’t return again.

Kikuyu: “Nũũ warekereirie njagĩ ĩthiiage ĩtarĩ mũũria? Nũũ wamĩohorire mĩhĩndo?
English: “Who has set the wild donkey free? Or who has loosened the bonds of the swift donkey,

Kikuyu: Ndaamĩheire werũ ũtuĩke mũciĩ wayo, naguo bũrũri wa cumbĩ ũtuĩke gĩtũũro kĩayo.
English: whose home I have made the wilderness, and the salt land his dwelling place?

Kikuyu: Ĩthekagĩrĩra inegene rĩrĩ thĩinĩ wa itũũra; ndĩiguaga mũkaĩrĩrio wa mũtwarithia.
English: He scorns the tumult of the city, neither does he hear the shouting of the driver.

Kikuyu: Ĩrimũthagĩra irĩma-inĩ ĩgĩetha gwa kũrĩa, ĩkahaara kahuti o gothe karuru.
English: The range of the mountains is his pasture. He searches after every green thing.

Kikuyu: “Mbogo ya njamba-rĩ, yetĩkĩra gũgũtungata? No ĩkindĩrie mũharatĩ-inĩ waku ũtukũ?
English: “Will the wild ox be content to serve you? Or will he stay by your feeding trough?

Kikuyu: No ũhote kũmĩoha matandĩko ĩrĩme na mũraũ? No ĩkuume thuutha ituamba-inĩ ĩkĩrĩmaga na mũraũ?
English: Can you hold the wild ox in the furrow with his harness? Or will he till the valleys after you?

Kikuyu: No ũmĩĩhoke nĩ ũndũ atĩ ĩrĩ na hinya mũingĩ? No ũmĩtigĩre wĩra waku mũritũ ĩrutage?
English: Will you trust him, because his strength is great? Or will you leave to him your labor?

Kikuyu: No ũmĩĩhoke ĩkũrehere ngano yaku, na ĩmĩcookanĩrĩrie kĩhuhĩro-inĩ gĩaku?
English: Will you confide in him, that he will bring home your seed, and gather the grain of your threshing floor?

Kikuyu: “Mathagu ma nyaga mabatabataga nĩ gũkena, no matingĩgerekanio na mathagu na njoya cia njũũ.
English: “The wings of the ostrich wave proudly, but are they the feathers and plumage of love?

Kikuyu: Ĩrekagĩria matumbĩ mayo tĩĩri-inĩ na ĩkamatiga mũthanga-inĩ magwate ũrugarĩ,
English: For she leaves her eggs on the earth, warms them in the dust,

Kikuyu: ĩtegwĩciiria atĩ no makinywo na magũrũ makue, kana marangwo nĩ nyamũ ya gĩthaka.
English: and forgets that the foot may crush them, or that the wild animal may trample them.

Kikuyu: Ĩĩkaga ciana ciayo ũũru ta itarĩ ciayo; ndĩmakaga atĩ wĩra wayo no ũtuĩke wa tũhũ,
English: She deals harshly with her young ones, as if they were not hers. Though her labor is in vain, she is without fear,

Kikuyu: nĩgũkorwo Ngai ndaamĩheire ũũgĩ kana akĩmĩhe igai rĩa mwĩciirĩrie mwega.
English: because God has deprived her of wisdom, neither has he imparted to her understanding.

Kikuyu: No rĩrĩ, rĩrĩa yatambũrũkia mathagu ĩhanyũke, ĩthekagĩrĩra mbarathi na mũmĩhaici.
English: When she lifts up herself on high, she scorns the horse and his rider.

Kikuyu: “Wee nĩwe ũheaga mbarathi hinya wayo, kana ũkamĩhumba ngingo na mũreera?
English: “Have you given the horse might? Have you clothed his neck with a quivering mane?

Kikuyu: Wee nĩwe ũtũmaga ĩrũũge ta ngigĩ, ĩkahahũra andũ na mũtiihĩre wayo wa mwĩtĩĩo?
English: Have you made him to leap as a locust? The glory of his snorting is awesome.

Kikuyu: Ĩhuragia thĩ na ũcamba ĩgĩkenagĩra hinya wayo, ĩkaguthũka ĩtoonyete mbaara-inĩ.
English: He paws in the valley, and rejoices in his strength. He goes out to meet the armed men.

Kikuyu: Ĩthekagĩrĩra guoya, ĩtarĩ ũndũ ĩngĩtigĩra; ndĩmakagio nĩ rũhiũ rwa njora.
English: He mocks at fear, and is not dismayed, neither does he turn back from the sword.

Kikuyu: Thiaka wa mũmĩhaici ũbocabocaga mbaru-inĩ ciayo, hamwe na itimũ rĩkũhenia na mĩcengi.
English: The quiver rattles against him, the flashing spear and the javelin.

Kikuyu: Irĩĩaga tĩĩri nĩ ũrũme; ndĩngĩrũgama ĩkindĩirie hĩndĩ ĩrĩa karumbeta kagamba.
English: He eats up the ground with fierceness and rage, neither does he stand still at the sound of the trumpet.

Kikuyu: Hĩndĩ ĩrĩa karumbeta kagamba ĩgatiiha, ‘Hĩ!’ Ĩnyiitaga thaaha wa mbaara ĩrĩ o haraaya, na ĩkaigua kayũ ka anene a mbaara, o na mbugĩrĩrio ya mbaara.
English: As often as the trumpet sounds he snorts, ‘Aha!’ He smells the battle afar off, the thunder of the captains, and the shouting.

Kikuyu: “Rwĩgĩ-rĩ, nĩwe ũrũhotithagia kũmbũka na ũũgĩ waku, kana gũtambũrũkia mathagu maruo rwerekeire mwena wa gũthini?
English: “Is it by your wisdom that the hawk soars, and stretches her wings toward the south?

Kikuyu: Nderi nĩwe ũmĩathaga yũmbũke na igũrũ, na ĩkeyakĩra gĩtara kĩayo igũrũ mũno?
English: Is it at your command that the eagle mounts up, and makes his nest on high?

Kikuyu: Ĩtũũraga kĩharũrũka-inĩ kĩa ihiga, na nĩ ho ĩraaraga; rũhĩa-inĩ rwa ihiga iraaya mũno nĩ ho mwĩgitio wayo.
English: On the cliff he dwells and makes his home, on the point of the cliff and the stronghold.

Kikuyu: Ĩrĩ hau nĩguo ĩcaragĩria gĩa kũrĩa; maitho mayo moonaga irio irĩ o kũraya.
English: From there he spies out the prey. His eyes see it afar off.

Kikuyu: Tũcui twayo tũnyuuaga thakame, na handũ harĩa arĩa moragĩtwo marĩ, hau nĩ ho ĩkoragwo.”
English: His young ones also suck up blood. Where the slain are, there he is.”

Kikuyu: Ningĩ Jehova akĩĩra Ayubu atĩrĩ:
English: Moreover Yahweh answered Job,

Kikuyu: “Mũndũ ũrĩa ũrũaga na Mwene-Hinya-Wothe-rĩ, no amũrute mahĩtia? Ũcio ũkararagia Ngai-rĩ, nĩakĩmũcookerie!”
English: “Shall he who argues contend with the Almighty? He who argues with God, let him answer it.”

Kikuyu: Nake Ayubu agĩcookeria Jehova, akĩmwĩra atĩrĩ:
English: Then Job answered Yahweh,

Kikuyu: “Niĩ ndiagĩrĩire o na hanini; ndaakĩhota atĩa gũgũcookeria? Nĩndehumbĩra kanua na guoko.
English: “Behold, I am of small account. What will I answer you? I lay my hand on my mouth.

Kikuyu: Nĩndaririe rĩmwe, no ndirĩ na macookio; o na ngĩaria rĩa keerĩ, no ndirĩ na ũndũ ũngĩ nguuga.”
English: I have spoken once, and I will not answer; Yes, twice, but I will proceed no further.”

Kikuyu: Ningĩ Jehova akĩarĩria Ayubu arĩ kĩhuhũkanio-inĩ, akĩmwĩra atĩrĩ:
English: Then Yahweh answered Job out of the whirlwind:

Kikuyu: “Wĩhotore ta mũndũ mũrũme; nĩngũkũũria ciũria, nawe ũkĩnjookerie.
English: “Now brace yourself like a man. I will question you, and you will answer me.

Kikuyu: “Gũtua ciira gwakwa na kĩhooto-rĩ, githĩ no ũkũmenererie? Githĩ no ũndue mwĩhia nĩgeetha wee ũtuĩke ndwĩhĩtie?
English: Will you even annul my judgment? Will you condemn me, that you may be justified?

Kikuyu: Wee-rĩ, ũrĩ na guoko ta kwa Mũrungu? Wee wahota kũruruma na mũgambo ta wake?
English: Or do you have an arm like God? Can you thunder with a voice like him?

Kikuyu: Ta kĩĩgemie na riiri na ũkengi, na wĩhumbe gĩtĩĩo na ũnene.
English: “Now deck yourself with excellency and dignity. Array yourself with honor and majesty.

Kikuyu: Rekereria marakara mahiũ ma mangʼũrĩ maku, wone mũndũ o wothe mwĩtĩĩi ũmũharũrũkie,
English: Pour out the fury of your anger. Look at everyone who is proud, and bring him low.

Kikuyu: rora mũndũ o wothe mwĩtĩĩi na ũmũnyiihie, ũmemende andũ arĩa aaganu o harĩa marũngiĩ.
English: Look at everyone who is proud, and humble him. Crush the wicked in their place.

Kikuyu: Mathike othe hamwe tĩĩri-inĩ; ũmoohe mothiũ na nduma kũu mbĩrĩra-inĩ.
English: Hide them in the dust together. Bind their faces in the hidden place.

Kikuyu: Hĩndĩ ĩyo niĩ mwene nĩngetĩkania nawe atĩ guoko gwaku mwene kwa ũrĩo no gũkũhonokie.
English: Then I will also admit to you that your own right hand can save you.

Kikuyu: “Ta rora nyamũ ĩrĩa ĩtagwo Behemothu,* ĩyo ndoombire hamwe nawe, na ĩrĩĩaga nyeki ta ndegwa.
English: “See now behemoth, which I made as well as you. He eats grass as an ox.

Kikuyu: Nĩ hinya ũigana atĩa ĩrĩ naguo njohero, na nĩ ũhoti mũnene atĩa ũrĩ mĩkiha-inĩ yayo ya nda!
English: Look now, his strength is in his thighs. His force is in the muscles of his belly.

Kikuyu: Ĩinagia mũtingʼoe wayo ta mũtarakwa; nga cia ciero ciayo ciohanĩtio hamwe ta mĩhĩndo.
English: He moves his tail like a cedar. The sinews of his thighs are knit together.

Kikuyu: Mahĩndĩ mayo mahaana ta mĩberethi ya gĩcango, nacio ciĩga ciayo cihaana ta irungʼo cia kĩgera.
English: His bones are like tubes of bronze. His limbs are like bars of iron.

Kikuyu: Nĩyo nyamũ ya mbere harĩ ciũmbe cia Mũrungu, no rĩrĩ, Mũũmbi wayo nowe ũngĩmĩkuhĩrĩria na rũhiũ rwake rwa njora.
English: He is the chief of the ways of God. He who made him gives him his sword.

Kikuyu: Irĩma ĩmĩheaga maciaro maacio, na nyamũ ciothe cia gĩthaka itũũhagĩra gũkuhĩ na kũu.
English: Surely the mountains produce food for him, where all the animals of the field play.

Kikuyu: Ĩkomaga rungu rwa mahũa ma maaĩ-inĩ, ĩĩhithĩte thĩinĩ wa ithanjĩ kũrĩa kũrĩ mũtondo.
English: He lies under the lotus trees, in the covert of the reed, and the marsh.

Kikuyu: Mahũa macio ma maaĩ-inĩ makamĩhitha; nakĩo kĩĩruru kĩa mĩtĩ ya irura hũgũrũrũ-inĩ cia karũũĩ gĩkamĩthiũrũrũkĩria.
English: The lotuses cover him with their shade. The willows of the brook surround him.

Kikuyu: Rĩrĩa rũũĩ ruoka na nditi, ndĩmakaga; nĩngitĩre, o na Rũũĩ rwa Jorodani rũngĩmĩiyũrĩrĩra nginya kanua.
English: Behold, if a river overflows, he doesn’t tremble. He is confident, though the Jordan swells even to his mouth.

Kikuyu: Kũrĩ mũndũ ũngĩhota kũmĩnyiita rĩrĩa ĩĩhũũgĩte, kana amĩtege, amĩtũrĩkie iniũrũ na amĩĩkĩre kĩana kĩa rũrigi?
English: Shall any take him when he is on the watch, or pierce through his nose with a snare?

Kikuyu: “No ũhote kũguucũrũria nyamũ ĩrĩa ĩĩtagwo Leviathani na ndwano, kana wohe rũrĩmĩ rwayo na mũkanda?
English: “Can you draw out Leviathan† with a fish hook, or press down his tongue with a cord?

Kikuyu: No ũhote kũmĩtoonyia rũrigi iniũrũ, kana ũmĩtũrĩkanie rũthĩa na ndwano?
English: Can you put a rope into his nose, or pierce his jaw through with a hook?

Kikuyu: No ĩtinde ĩgĩgũthaitha ũmĩiguĩre tha? No ĩkwarĩrie na ciugo cia ũhooreri?
English: Will he make many petitions to you, or will he speak soft words to you?

Kikuyu: No ĩrĩkanĩre nawe ũthiĩ nayo, ĩtũũre ĩrĩ ngombo yaku nginya tene?
English: Will he make a covenant with you, that you should take him for a servant forever?

Kikuyu: No ũhote kũmĩhooreria ta nyoni, kana ũmĩoherere handũ nĩguo airĩtu aku mamĩmeemagie?
English: Will you play with him as with a bird? Or will you bind him for your girls?

Kikuyu: Onjoria no mamĩkũũranie na indo ciao? No mamĩgayanie kũrĩ onjorithia?
English: Will traders barter for him? Will they part him among the merchants?

Kikuyu: No ũhote gũtheecanga rũũa rwayo na mĩcengi, kana ũtheecange mũtwe wayo na mĩcengi ĩrĩa ĩtegaga thamaki?
English: Can you fill his skin with barbed irons, or his head with fish spears?

Kikuyu: Ũngĩmĩhutia na guoko, ũngĩtũũra ũririkanaga kĩgiano kĩu, na ndũngĩgacookera!
English: Lay your hand on him. Remember the battle, and do so no more.

Kikuyu: Mwĩrĩgĩrĩro wa atĩ no ũmĩtoorie nĩ kwĩheenia; o kũmĩona tu nĩkũiganĩte gũtũma mũndũ amake, orwo nĩ hinya.
English: Behold, the hope of him is in vain. Won’t one be cast down even at the sight of him?

Kikuyu: Gũtirĩ mũndũ ũrĩ ũcamba mũiganu wa kũmĩarahũra. Nũũ ũngĩkĩhota kwĩĩndiiria niĩ?
English: None is so fierce that he dare stir him up. Who then is he who can stand before me?

Kikuyu: Nũũ ũngĩnandũra kĩndũ atĩ nĩguo ndĩmũrĩhe? Kĩndũ gĩothe kĩrĩ rungu rwa igũrũ nĩ gĩakwa.
English: Who has first given to me, that I should repay him? Everything under the heavens is mine.

Kikuyu: “Ndikwaga kwaria ũhoro wa ciĩga ciayo, o na wa hinya wayo, na wa ũthaka wayo.
English: “I will not keep silence concerning his limbs, nor his mighty strength, nor his goodly frame.

Kikuyu: Nũũ ũngĩhota kũmĩaũra nguo yayo ya igũrũ? Nũũ ũngĩmĩkuhĩrĩria amĩĩkĩre matamu?
English: Who can strip off his outer garment? Who will come within his jaws?

Kikuyu: Nũũ ũngĩũmĩrĩria kũmĩathamia kanua, kau kaiyũrĩte magego ma kũmakania?
English: Who can open the doors of his face? Around his teeth is terror.

Kikuyu: Mũgongo wayo ũrĩ na ngo ciĩiganĩrĩire mĩhari, ikomanĩire ikanyiitana;
English: Strong scales are his pride, shut up together with a close seal.

Kikuyu: o ĩmwe ĩnyiitanĩte na ĩrĩa ĩngĩ, ũũ atĩ gũtirĩ rĩera rĩngĩtoonyera gatagatĩ ga cio.
English: One is so near to another, that no air can come between them.

Kikuyu: Igwatanĩtio hamwe irĩ nũmu; inyiitanĩte hamwe ũndũ itangĩtigithũkana.
English: They are joined to one another. They stick together, so that they can’t be pulled apart.

Kikuyu: Gũtiiha kwayo kũmenũkagia ũtheri; maitho mayo nĩ ta mĩrũri ya rũciinĩ gũgĩthererũka.
English: His sneezing flashes out light. His eyes are like the eyelids of the morning.

Kikuyu: Imũrĩ cia mwaki ciumaga kanua-inĩ kayo; ĩrathũkagia thandĩ cia mwaki.
English: Out of his mouth go burning torches. Sparks of fire leap out.

Kikuyu: Ĩrutaga ndogo na maniũrũ taarĩ nyũngũ ĩratherũka ĩhagĩrĩtwo igũrũ rĩa mwaki wa ithanjĩ.
English: Out of his nostrils a smoke goes, as of a boiling pot over a fire of reeds.

Kikuyu: Mĩhũmũ yayo ĩgwatagia makara mwaki, naruo rũrĩrĩmbĩ rũkoima kanua kayo.
English: His breath kindles coals. A flame goes out of his mouth.

Kikuyu: Ngingo-inĩ yayo nĩho hinya wayo ũkoragwo, ũrĩa ũmakagia kĩrĩa gĩothe gĩtũnganaga nayo.
English: There is strength in his neck. Terror dances before him.

Kikuyu: Mĩgũtha ya nyama ciayo nĩmĩnyiitanu mũno; nĩ mĩrũmu ũũ atĩ ndĩngĩenyenyeka.
English: The flakes of his flesh are joined together. They are firm on him. They can’t be moved.

Kikuyu: Ngoro yayo yũmĩte ta ihiga, ĩkooma ta ihiga rĩa gũthĩa rĩa na thĩ.
English: His heart is as firm as a stone, yes, firm as the lower millstone.

Kikuyu: Rĩrĩa yarahũka, arĩa marĩ hinya nĩmamakaga; mooraga ĩtanamahũũra.
English: When he raises himself up, the mighty are afraid. They retreat before his thrashing.

Kikuyu: Gũtirĩ rũhiũ rwa njora rũngĩmĩĩka ũndũ, o na kana itimũ, kana mũguĩ, kana mĩcengi.
English: If one attacks him with the sword, it can’t prevail; nor the spear, the dart, nor the pointed shaft.

Kikuyu: Harĩ Leviathani-rĩ, kĩgera no ta nyeki nyũmũ, nakĩo gĩcango no ta gĩcunjĩ kĩbuthu kĩa mũtĩ.
English: He counts iron as straw, and bronze as rotten wood.

Kikuyu: Mĩguĩ ndĩngĩtũma yũre; mahiga ma kĩgũtha no ta mũũngũ harĩ yo.
English: The arrow can’t make him flee. Sling stones are like chaff to him.

Kikuyu: Harĩ yo njũgũma no ta gacunjĩ ka rũnyeki rũmũ; ĩthekagĩrĩra kũbĩrĩrĩka gwa itimũ.
English: Clubs are counted as stubble. He laughs at the rushing of the javelin.

Kikuyu: Nda yayo nĩ ta rũgĩo rũrĩ na mageca; ĩtigaga ngururo ndaka-inĩ ta cia ngaari iria ikonyoraga ngano.
English: His undersides are like sharp potsherds, leaving a trail in the mud like a threshing sledge.

Kikuyu: Ĩtũmaga iria kũrĩa kũriku gũtherũke ta nyũngũ, na ĩkoiruga iria ta nyũngũ ya maguta ma kwĩhaka.
English: He makes the deep to boil like a pot. He makes the sea like a pot of ointment.

Kikuyu: Harĩa yagerera ĩtigaga mũhari ũkũhenia; mũndũ no eciirie atĩ ndia ĩrĩ na mbuĩ.
English: He makes a path shine after him. One would think the deep had white hair.

Kikuyu: Gũtirĩ kĩndũ kĩngĩigananio nayo gũkũ thĩ; nĩ kĩũmbe gĩtarĩ guoya.
English: On earth there is not his equal, that is made without fear.

Kikuyu: Ĩnyũrũragia kĩrĩa gĩothe gĩĩtũũgagĩria; nĩyo mũthamaki wa kĩrĩa gĩothe gĩĩtĩĩaga.”
English: He sees everything that is high. He is king over all the sons of pride.”

Kikuyu: Ningĩ Ayubu agĩcookeria Jehova, akĩmwĩra atĩrĩ:
English: Then Job answered Yahweh:

Kikuyu: “Nĩnjũũĩ atĩ wahota gwĩka maũndũ mothe; gũtirĩ mũbango waku ũngĩgirĩrĩka.
English: “I know that you can do all things, and that no purpose of yours can be restrained.

Kikuyu: Nĩworirie atĩrĩ, ‘Nũũ ũyũ ũrahithania kĩrĩra gĩakwa nĩ kwaga ũmenyo?’ Ti-itherũ ndaaririe maũndũ itaamenyete, maũndũ ma magegania itangĩmenya.
English: You asked, ‘Who is this who hides counsel without knowledge?’ therefore I have uttered that which I didn’t understand, things too wonderful for me, which I didn’t know.

Kikuyu: “Woigire atĩrĩ, ‘Thikĩrĩria rĩu, na niĩ njarie; nĩngũkũũria ciũria, nawe nĩũkũnjookeria.’
English: You said, ‘Listen, now, and I will speak; I will question you, and you will answer me.’

Kikuyu: Matũ makwa nĩmaiguĩte ũhoro waku no rĩu maitho makwa nĩgũkuona makuonete.
English: I had heard of you by the hearing of the ear, but now my eye sees you.

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ ũcio nĩngwĩmena niĩ mwene, na ndĩrire, ndĩhurĩrie rũkũngũ na mũhu.”
English: Therefore I abhor myself, and repent in dust and ashes.”

Kikuyu: Thuutha wa Jehova kwĩra Ayubu maũndũ macio-rĩ, nĩerire Elifazu ũrĩa Mũtemaani atĩrĩ, “Nĩndakarĩtio nĩwe na arata aku eerĩ, tondũ mũtiarĩtie ũhoro wakwa ũrĩa wagĩrĩire, ta ũrĩa ndungata yakwa Ayubu ĩĩkĩte.
English: It was so, that after Yahweh had spoken these words to Job, Yahweh said to Eliphaz the Temanite, “My wrath is kindled against you, and against your two friends; for you have not spoken of me the thing that is right, as my servant Job has.

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ ũcio, rĩu oyai ndegwa mũgwanja na ndũrũme mũgwanja, mũthiĩ kũrĩ ndungata yakwa Ayubu, mũkarute igongona rĩa njino nĩ ũndũ wanyu inyuĩ ene. Ndungata yakwa Ayubu nĩĩkamũhoera, na niĩ nĩngetĩkĩra mahooya make, na ndikamwĩka kũringana na ũrimũ wanyu. Mũtiarĩtie ũhoro wakwa ũrĩa wagĩrĩire ta ũrĩa ndungata yakwa Ayubu ĩĩkĩte.”
English: Now therefore, take to yourselves seven bulls and seven rams, and go to my servant Job, and offer up for yourselves a burnt offering; and my servant Job shall pray for you, for I will accept him, that I not deal with you according to your folly. For you have not spoken of me the thing that is right, as my servant Job has.”

Kikuyu: Nĩ ũndũ ũcio Elifazu ũrĩa Mũtemaani, na Bilidadi ũrĩa Mũshuhi, na Zofaru ũrĩa Mũnaamathi magĩĩka o ta ũrĩa Jehova aameerire; nake Jehova nĩetĩkĩrire ihooya rĩa Ayubu.
English: So Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite went and did what Yahweh commanded them, and Yahweh accepted Job.

Kikuyu: Thuutha wa Ayubu kũhoera arata ake-rĩ, Jehova nĩamũcookeirie ũtonga wake na akĩmũhe maita meerĩ ma indo iria aarĩ nacio mbere.
English: Yahweh restored Job’s prosperity when he prayed for his friends. Yahweh gave Job twice as much as he had before.

Kikuyu: Ariũ na aarĩ a nyina othe, na mũndũ o wothe wamũũĩ mbere, magĩũka makĩrĩĩanĩra nake mũciĩ gwake, nao makĩmũhooreria na makĩmũcakaithia nĩ ũndũ wa mathĩĩna marĩa mothe Jehova aamũreheire. Andũ acio o mũndũ akĩmũhe gĩcunjĩ kĩa betha na gĩcũhĩ gĩa thahabu.
English: Then all his brothers, all his sisters, and all those who had been of his acquaintance before, came to him and ate bread with him in his house. They comforted him, and consoled him concerning all the evil that Yahweh had brought on him. Everyone also gave him a piece of money,† and everyone a ring of gold.

Kikuyu: Jehova nĩarathimire matukũ ma mũthia ma muoyo wa Ayubu gũkĩra marĩa ma mbere. Nĩaagĩire na ngʼondu 14,000, na ngamĩĩra 6,000, na ndegwa cia kuohwo macooki 1,000, na ndigiri 1,000.
English: So Yahweh blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning. He had fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, one thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand female donkeys.

Kikuyu: Nĩacookire akĩgĩa na aanake mũgwanja na airĩtu atatũ.
English: He had also seven sons and three daughters.

Kikuyu: Mwarĩ wa mbere aamũtuire Jemima, na wa keerĩ aamũtuire Kezia, nake wa gatatũ akĩmũtua Kereni-Hapuku.
English: He called the name of the first, Jemimah; and the name of the second, Keziah; and the name of the third, Keren Happuch.

Kikuyu: Gũtirĩ handũ o na ha bũrũri- inĩ wothe hangĩonekire andũ-a-nja athaka ta airĩtu a Ayubu, nake ithe wao akĩmahe igai hamwe na ariũ a nyina.
English: In all the land were no women found so beautiful as the daughters of Job. Their father gave them an inheritance among their brothers.

Kikuyu: Thuutha wa maũndũ macio-rĩ, Ayubu nĩatũũrire mĩaka igana rĩa mĩrongo ĩna; akĩona ciana ciake na akĩona ciana ciacio, nginya rũciaro rwa kana.
English: After this Job lived one hundred forty years, and saw his sons, and his sons’ sons, to four generations.

Kikuyu: Nake agĩkua arĩ mũkũrũ, na arĩ na mĩaka mĩingĩ.
English: So Job died, being old and full of days.
